News.title: Mile-long trail of blood led to dying headteacher who was dragged beneath car, murder trial hears
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A trail of blood more than a mile in length led to a dying headmaster who was mowed down and dragged underneath a car, a murder trial jury heard.

Michael Mullins, 56, was struck by a black Volvo XC90 as he cycled home from Stretford Grammar School in Manchester during the early evening of April 20.

Simon Richardson, 35, is said to have driven at speed through give way markers at a junction in Warburton, Altrincham, and into the path of Mr Mullins.

Prosecutors accuse Richardson of murder because they say he knew Mr Mullins was beneath the wheels of his vehicle but drove on anyway.

On Wednesday, jurors heard from a motorcyclist who discovered Mr Mullins lying on a grass verge in Lymm, Cheshire – 2.2 kilometres from the collision in Paddock Lane.

Andrew Besant-Roberts arrived at the collision scene at the junction with Dunham Road and was told a cyclist may have been trapped under the car.

In a statement read to the court, he said: “I very quickly noticed a strange trail on the road.

“I didn’t know what it was initially, but I thought it was suspicious.

“As I followed the trail, it suddenly occurred to me that it was blood.

“As it went over a white line I could see it was red.”

open image in gallery Prosecutors accuse Simon Richardson of murder because they say he knew Mr Mullins was beneath the wheels of his vehicle but drove on anyway ( AFP/Getty )

The trail led to Mill Lane, a single carriageway in Lymm, and then on to Wet Gate Lane, a quiet country lane, the court heard.

Mr Besant-Roberts added: “I noticed the trail started to weave from left to right.

This continued for a couple of hundred yards.

“Then I saw a cyclist on a grass verge who appeared to be in a position similar to the recovery position.

“He was laid on his side unconscious but I could see he was still breathing.”

He dialled 999 but said the cyclist “began to deteriorate”.

He said: “His breathing became worse and worse. It was irregular with long pauses and then it just stopped.”

Mr Besant-Roberts was instructed by a call handler to give chest compressions before a paramedic arrived shortly after.

Mr Mullins, from Northwich, Cheshire, was pronounced dead at the scene at 6.50pm – about 40 minutes after the collision.

Earlier, a motorist parked at the Green Dragon pub in Mill Lane said she noticed something underneath a vehicle travelling at speed.

In a witness statement, Katie Woodward said: “My first thought was that it was a body but I thought this was ridiculous and surely a body can’t be under the car.

“I convinced myself it must have been an animal.

“As the vehicle drove along the road I saw it was leaving a trail coming from the passenger side.”

She too decided to follow the “thick, dark trail”, the court was told, which stopped where Mr Mullins laid as he was being tended to by Mr Besant-Roberts.

Dog walker Peter Connell was on Mill Lane when he said he heard a “loud, dragging sound” coming from a passing black car.

He said: “It was an unusual sound.

“Something flapping round like cardboard or a plastic sheet.

“I looked under the car and I saw something big and flapping round the front passenger wheel.

“I thought it was bizarre that the driver had not realised they had something under the car and didn’t stop.”

The Crown say Richardson “veered sharply and deliberately from side to side” in Wet Gate Lane before his car mounted the verge, and that he then drove over his victim at least once before he was finally dislodged.

The defendant denies murder and an alternative count of manslaughter.

He has also pleaded not guilty to an allegation of dangerous driving on April 21 in a police pursuit before he was arrested.

News.title: Marine Le Pen promises ‘trial of strength’ with EU if elected French president
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Marine Le Pen, the far-right leader in France, has vowed to engage in a “trial of strength” with the EU over its finances if she is elected as president next year.

Le Pen, the former leader of the far-right National Rally, is the frontrunner for France’s presidential election in April, as incumbent Emmanuel Macron steps down following two consecutive terms.

The 58-year-old has defined much of her political career against the European bloc, which is now working to push through a seven-year budget before the French presidential elections. Speaking to the Financial Times from her Paris office, Le Pen described the move as “deeply objectionable”.

“In fact, I think it reveals the contempt the Commission has for democratic processes in Europe,” she said, although accepted that her promise to cut France’s contribution to the EU budget would be difficult. “We know there will be a tough debate, even a trial of strength. But we have the will and the conviction that we will be able to do it.”

open image in gallery Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) candidate in France's 2027 presidential election Marine Le Pen ( AFP/Getty )

Brussels wants a deal by Christmas, but France and Germany are in dispute over the long-term budget amid proposals for deep cuts.

The EU Commission has proposed a budget for 2028-2034 that is worth nearly €2 trillion, well beyond the roughly €1.2 trillion budget during the 2021-2027 period.

Germany, Austria, Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands, and Sweden want to cut several hundred billion euros from the budget, but France has hit out at these calls, with Macron declaring that the bloc needs an “ambitious” budget.

Le Pen’s five-year, €140bn plan to cut the deficit if she is elected, would see France save €11bn by cutting its contributions to the EU budget in 2027, she said. Paris would ultimately limit its net contribution to the EU budget to €5 billion, the level it was at in the early 2000s, a move that would prompt anger in Brussels.

The negotiations come ahead of a busy election year, with French polling currently forecasting a run-off between French far-right leader Marine Le Pen and hard-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon, an indication of the growing polarisation as Macron's era ends.

open image in gallery French far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) and allied party UDR's members of parliament, with group president Marine Le Pen sitting in the middle ( AFP/Getty )

Le Pen, who in recent weeks has been polling around 33 to 37 per cent, promised pragmatism with the economy, admitting that her main constraint if elected would be the “gigantic, enormous debt... that could become uncontrollable”.

“Politics is in reality a question of conviction confronted by constraints,” she said. “I have no intention of losing my convictions.”

Fighting in her fourth presidential election - and projected to reach her third successive run-off - Le Pen believes next year could be significant for nationalist and anti-EU parties across Europe.

Next year will be an “extraordinary event” as elections also take place in Spain, Italy and Poland, Le Pen said, expressing hope that it could signal a radical new era for the continent.

Le Pen hit out at EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, and suggested she “no longer has the confidence of many governments in the EU” and therefore cannot remain in post until the end of her mandate in 2029.

Le Pen officially launched her presidential campaign in western France in July, just one day after an appeals court confirmed her conviction for embezzling EU funds, yet crucially enabled her to stand for office.

The Paris appeals court had upheld her March 2025 conviction for misusing European Parliament funds to pay party staff, but simultaneously shortened her ban on running for office, allowing her to run in the 2027 race.

News.title: Zimbabwe’s Caine Prize winner rejects claim he used AI to write his story
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza, whose prize for a short story is under review over allegations of AI use, denied using artificial intelligence to write what he said was a story inspired by his family’s experiences, and he suggested that AI-detection technology is biased.

Kundizeza's “The Blue Fighter” won this year’s $10,000 Caine Prize for African Writing last week, but a report in The Atlantic magazine said the AI detection tool Pangram had indicated the entire story was AI-generated with the exception of an excerpt from a poem by another author.

Kundizeza posted a denial on X late Tuesday, and in an interview Wednesday with The Associated Press said that African writers and readers should challenge such accusations.

“There is need to use technology responsibly so that it is not deployed to create a bias against natives who seek to write about their own experiences and cultures,” he said. “Although I am not too well versed with these technologies, it is well known that AI is in certain ways biased against us, it’s something that really needs to be looked at because this kind of treatment I got is not going to stop,” he added.

The Caine Prize organizers have not retracted the prize, but have said that it is under review and that they have a responsibility to examine such AI claims. “We aim to do this by taking a human-centered approach, ensuring that writers are supported and cared for during the process. We have initiated that process in this case,” the organizers said this week.

In his statement on X, Kundizeza insisted that his story, centered on family relationships and economic hardship, was entirely his own work. He said it had gone through standard editorial processes. He said the story reflected his family’s life during Zimbabwe’s years of economic turmoil.

“Aspects of the story, including characters and the setting, are drawn from events in my own life,” he said, describing it as “a deeply personal story about economic collapse and familial relationships.”

He challenged the suggestion that differences between the winning story and his earlier work should cast doubt on his authorship.

“As writers, we develop recurring interests, but we don’t produce work from a single fixed template. To suggest that a writer cannot write in different styles or genres, or improve his writing substantially after five or more years, fundamentally misunderstands the craft of writing,” he said in his X post.

The allegations have prompted a wider debate on social media, with some questioning whether Black authors are being unfairly targeted by AI-related accusations.

Radical Books Collective, an international group that organizes online book clubs, literary events and podcasts focused on political literature and ideas, described the controversy as part of a broader pattern. “The digital lynchings continue as Black authors are being targeted in AI/plagiarism scandals: Jamir Nazir, Jerry Falade, Thélyson Orélien and now Simbarashe Kundizeza,” the collective posted.

Nhlandla Duba, a linguist from Zimbabwe who researches English literature at the University of Pretoria, said Kundizeza's story rings true.

“That story sounds human. Zimbabwean literature is alive!" Duba proclaimed on X.

News.title: ‘An exhibition’: Steven Gerrard salutes PSG after stunning first half against Man City
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Steven Gerrard hailed “a 31-minute exhibition” from Paris Saint-Germain as the best football he had seen in years after the Champions League holders scored three first-half goals against Manchester City.

Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha struck for the visitors and Achraf Hakimi hit the post in a rampant 17-minute spell while former City manager Pep Guardiola watched on at the Etihad.

Guardiola was making his first appearance at the Etihad since leaving the club in May, in what was City’s first home appearance since the were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

But PSG became the first team to score three first-half goals against Manchester City away from home since Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool in November 2015 as Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions produced a statement performance.

And former Liverpool captain Gerrard was stunned to see a City side who have won all six of their Premier League games this season and were 3-0 winners at Anfield on Sunday be so comprehensively outplayed.

“It’s been a 31-minute exhibition, it’s been so one-sided,” Gerrard said on TNT Sports. “Outstanding. I think Enzo Maresca has to speak to his staff and change something. I think they’re a man down in the centre of the pitch with [Rayan] Cherki.”

Former England international Owen Hargreaves called PSG’s football “ridiculous” and said: “The quality of the touches and finishing [from PSG] is exquisite. That is as good as I’ve seen live maybe ever. Technically this is best of what the Premier League has to offer and they’ve put on a masterclass.”

News.title: Barcola starts to justify £123m price tag with hat-trick as Liverpool hit LASK for six
News.content:
Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Second Ebola case confirmed in Kenya
News.content:
Kenya has recorded its second-ever case of Ebola after a relative of a patient who died last week tested positive for the virus, officials have said.

A 39-year-old man fell ill on Tuesday and has since been confirmed to be infected with Ebola, according to Kenyan health authorities.

The patient, who is now isolated, is a family member of Kenya’s first-ever Ebola case, who died in a hospital in Nairobi last Monday.

The index case, a 40-year old businessman, had travelled to Kenya from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the epicentre of the deadly outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which has so far killed more than 4,300 people.

Kenyan authorities have identified 128 of his contacts and have successfully tracked down 113 of them, who are having their temperatures checked daily for a period of three weeks, the country’s Director-General for Health, Dr Patrick Amoth, said in a statement.

“There is no evidence of spread in the wider community,” the statement, issued on Wednesday, added.

However, questions remain over whether more cases will crop up in the coming weeks.

News.title: I tried Apple’s new smart home hub – the brand faithful will love it
News.content:
HomeView can control smart lights, heating, security cameras and video doorbells via touch or voice, but devices must support Matter – the cross-brand smart home standard. That means you aren’t confined to Apple-approved gadgets, but you are still limited – Ring video doorbells, for example, aren’t Matter-compatible, so they won’t work with HomeView, which could be a deal-breaker for even the biggest Apple fan.

But for anyone put off by the complexity of setting up a smart home, Apple is trying to simplify things. It has partnered with LG on Home Collection – a range of devices, including security cameras and a video doorbell – that connect with a single tap, just as AirPods do with an iPhone. They won’t be available until later in the year, but they could mark a major step towards making smart home set-up less complicated.

My early verdict

HomeView is built for the Apple faithful: set-up requires an iPhone or iPad, personalised AI features need a recent Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone, and some apps work only when your phone is nearby. In a household split between iPhone and Android, Android users will get a much thinner experience, and Apple’s own services come first at every turn.

Still, HomeView is the most polished smart display I have seen. Face recognition makes it both a great shared and personalised device; the sound quality is excellent; and Siri AI is finally worth talking to, especially when it can draw on your personal context. I’ll need to live with it for a few weeks before giving a final verdict, but so far it’s a beautifully designed device I’d be happy to invite into my home.

News.title: Ed Miliband calls for ‘new deal on debt’ as developing countries face spiralling borrowing costs
News.content:
Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, has called for a “new deal on debt” as spiralling borrowing costs force developing countries to spend more on interest payments than on education or health.

In a speech in Bangkok on Wednesday, Mr Miliband warned that the global financial system is failing emerging markets, and promised to use the UK’s diplomatic heft to push for urgent reform.

He said: “The short-term repayments are crippling, and while many are not defaulting on their payments they are being forced, if you like, to default on the lives and prospects of future generations.

“So we need a new deal on debt, a deal that supports countries to repay over longer time horizons and, crucially, refinancing with better rates to give developing countries precious fiscal space.”

Although public debt is not inherently problematic, servicing costs are at a 25-year-high – squeezing government coffers just as conflict, climate change and a ‘Godzilla’ El Niño push food and fuel prices ever higher.

Emerging economies in particular have little headroom: according to the Rockefeller Foundation, average interest payments now exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing nations, while UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) analysis found 3.7 billion people live in countries where debt servicing costs exceed spending on health or education.

At the same time, overseas development aid (ODA) spending from wealthy countries has plummeted – hitting social, infrastructure and humanitarian projects, and disaster response.

The mounting global debt pile has dominated discussions in Bangkok this week, where some 15,000 people have descended for the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank annual meetings.

This included the first meeting of the newly formed Borrowers’ Platform on Monday. A group of finance ministers and central bank governors from some 30 countries, it was formed to exchange ideas about how to deal with debt burdens – and how to avoid pitfalls.

News.title: Trump backs down in Zambia mineral and data-sharing row
News.content:
Zambia has signed a five-year health financing agreement with the US government after the US dropped demands for access to sensitive health data and separated the deal from negotiations over the country’s mineral resources.

The agreement follows months of negotiations over a $2.49 billion health aid package, with Zambia pushing back against US demands to share medical data and give preferential access to the country’s rich mineral reserves in exchange for money to provide lifesaving healthcare.

Under the final agreement, Zambia will not be required to hand over individual patient records or biological specimens, which the US had previously argued was important for global disease surveillance.

Data sharing will be restricted to monitoring and evaluating US-funded health programmes.

A separate agreement covering US access to Zambia’s critical minerals has also been decoupled from the health financing deal, it was confirmed last week.

“The government will not be sharing any specimens with the United States because we removed all those aspects that raised concern,” Zambian Health Minister Roma Chilengi said last week as the agreement was signed.

Zambia’s Foreign Minister Mulambo Haimbe also confirmed that the health and mineral agreements had been separated.

“There was this [memorandum of understanding] on health and another on critical minerals, and we were saying that these need to be decoupled, and this has been done,” he said.

News.title: Progress against HIV stalls in South Africa, research shows
News.content:
South Africa’s progress in tackling the Aids and HIV crisis has stalled in one of its most populous provinces, new research has found.

The number of new cases of the infection in KwaZulu-Natal province, centred around the eastern port of Durban, have stopped falling after years of steep declines.

Data from a long-running study following thousands of people also showed those with detectable levels of virus in their blood had risen slightly despite years of medics prescribing antiretroviral drugs.

Researchers said the peer-reviewed study published in The Lancet HIV medical journal “provides a stark warning on prevailing HIV trends in rural South Africa, where ground is being lost in the fight against the HIV epidemic”.

The researchers, led by scientists at Durban’s Africa Health Research Institute (AHRI) and Stellenbosch University’s South African Centre for Epidemiological Modelling and Analysis (SACEMA), used a 20-year study which has tested nearly 60,000 people.

Analysis showed that after steep reductions in HIV incidence from 2013 to 2018, incidence rates for both males and females showed little or no decrease from 2019 onwards.

Incidence rates had continued to fall for young people under 35, but that had been offset by a lack of progress for those in middle age.

News.title: Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox
News.content:
They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

News.title: Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop
News.content:
The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

Sports.title: Mason Greenwood booed by Aston Villa fans as star plays in England for first time since rape charges dropped
Sports.content:
Next

MASON Greenwood received plenty of boos on his return to English football for the first time since the rape charges against him were dropped.

The 25-year-old forward, who has not played in England since January 2022, was named in the starting XI for Fenerbahce against Aston Villa in tonight’s Champions League clash.



The Villans are looking to open their Champions League campaign with back-to-back wins as they host Fenerbahce for the group-stage tie.

Greenwood’s name was read out ahead of kick-off after a stunning pre-match show, with the atmosphere sour towards the former Manchester United winger.



No other player was targeted, despite plenty of them also spending time in the Premier League, including Ederson, Nelson Semedo, N’Golo Kante, Matteo Guendouzi and Romelu Lukaku.

But loud boos rang out inside Villa Park as Greenwood was announced as starting for the Turkish giants.



Once the game was underway, every touch Greenwood took was booed by the home supporters.

He will be looking to add to his tally against Villa tonight, having already bagged six goals in 14 games this season.



Villa Park held it’s breath when the ball fell to Greenwood on the edge of the 18-yard box after 17 minutes, only for him to roll his shot into the palms of Zion Suzuki.

A collective “wahey” was cheered shortly after, followed by chants directed at the forward, referring to the previous charges against him.

Greenwood faced charges of attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour following his arrest in February 2022.

They were eventually dropped after key witnesses withdrew from the case and “new material” came to light.

Greenwood, 25, who was suspened by United, left the club in August 2023 following a six-month internal investigation into his behaviour.



He resumed his career across Europe at Getafe, Marseille and now Fenerbahce.

The forward initially signed for LaLiga outfit Getafe and hadn’t played in 20 months when he made his first appearance.

The Madrid side’s fans heckled him on his debut with chants of: “Greenwood, die!”

After scoring ten goals during that stint, he was sold to Marseille for £26.6million, plus a sell-on clause.

He netted 21 goals in his first season and followed that up with 26 goals in all competitions in the following campaign.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But after friction off the pitch with then-manager Roberto De Zerbi and sporting director Medhi Benatia, Greenwood was sold to Turkish side Fenerbahce for £33million.

He is worshipped as a hero in Turkey for Fenerbahce, and was mobbed by fans at Istanbul airport when he joined the club from Marseille, but is clearly still not highly thought of in England if tonight was anything to go by.

Sports.title: Man Utd stars divided over Lisandro Martinez outburst with Argentine among three defenders at risk of being released
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED players are split over Lisandro Martinez’s post-match outburst against the club hierarchy.

Martinez questioned the standard of the squad and rounded on those at the top – specifically director of football Jason Wilcox – over a lack of investment in the summer transfer window.



The 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid on Tuesday night extended United’s winless run to five games and they head to Leeds on Sunday.

Although some players appreciated Martinez’s honesty, others are reluctant to explicitly side with the Argentine.



One senior player feels Martinez’s comments exacerbated coverage of United’s loss to Atletico when the squad felt they had performed respectably against last season’s Champions League semi-finalists..

Another player believes the absence of certain team-mates has affected the harmony in the squad.



United travelled to Madrid without Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko, who all would have likely started if fully fit.

Martinez dodged photographers when United returned to Manchester Airport just before 3am on Wednesday morning.

Some players and staff were ferried back to the club’s Carrington training complex to collect their vehicles in the early hours. Head coach Michael Carrick is also believed to have returned to Carrington.

United players had a day off on Wednesday but senior staff still reported at Carrington amid the latest crisis.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The club have not responded for comment on whether Martinez will be disciplined.

United have a hefty Latino contingent in their squad and Martinez was included in their six-man leadership group that former head coach Ruben Amorim reassembled last year.

Martinez, 28, has entered the final year of his contract and United have the option of an additional year.

If United do not trigger that extension before the January transfer window, Martinez can negotiate a pre-contract agreement with an overseas club.



SunSport revealed last month Martinez was on trial to continue at United beyond this season ahead of a planned defensive rebuild next summer.

The club are expected to move for two full backs and a centre back. United could release Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw in eight months.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola & Man City chief given heroes’ welcome as they take to the stands for first home game since guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Next

PEP GUARDIOLA was given a heroes’ welcome as he returned to the Etihad.

The former Manchester City boss was sat in the posh seats as his old side took on Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League.



Guardiola, 55, made his first return to the Etihad since leaving City in the summer after 10 glittering years.

The Spaniard sat just behind club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and City Group CEO Ferran Soriano.



Ahead of the game, fans sat in the Pep Guardiola Stand held up cards, creating the message CTID – standing for “City ‘Til I Die”.

It is unclear whether the timing of Guardiola’s return related to City recently being found guilty of more than 100 of the 130 charges levelled against them by the Premier League.

But prior to the verdict, which City strongly contest and have appealed, it had been expected that Guardiola would stay away for longer.

The former boss remains a City Football Group ambassador.



And after news of their guilty verdict emerged last month, Guardiola quickly came out in support of his employers.

He wrote in a statement: “I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here – more than ever.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

“Let me be clear: we will get through this together.



“I love you all.”

SunSport reported last week that Guardiola would be returning to City for this game.

He is expected to meet up with former colleagues Enzo Maresca and Luis Enrique after the game, before then jetting away from Manchester.

On the pitch, City have had a fantastic start to life after Guardiola.

Sunday’s resounding 3-0 win at Liverpool made six wins out of six in the Premier League for Maresca.



But in front of their former boss, Prem leaders City got off to a nightmare start against PSG.

Desire Doue fired the two-time defending champions into a 13th minute lead, with Ousmane Dembele then adding a quickfire second.

Sports.title: Why do Man City fans have inflatable bananas in the stands?
Sports.content:
Next

SINCE the news of their guilty verdict, Manchester City fans have brought back the inflatable bananas into the crowd.

During the international break, the Mancunian side were found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules and falsely inflating sponsorship deals by £900million.



They have appealed the decision and will fight to prove their innocence, with the club saying they have “irrefutable evidence” which will overturn the verdict.

If they fail in doing so, they could face a punishment as severe as relegation from the Premier League.



Despite this, their fans remain confident in their club and have brought back an old tradition in a show of support.

SunSport has all the details on why the City fans bring the bananas into the stands.

Why do Man City fans have inflatable bananas?

Inflatable bananas have been a City symbol since 1987/88, following relegation to the second tier that season.

The exact reason has been disputed, but many claim it is due to former striker Imre Varadi.

Supporters nicknamed him “Imre Banana” and a chant naming him just that took off.

It led to one fan bringing an inflatable banana to the ground and it bizarrely led to a trend throughout 80s and 90s at City games.



Dante Friend, who dished out bananas to fans before facing Liverpool last weekend, explained: “It was just one guy at the game who referred to him as “Imre Banana”.

“A guy called Frank Newton took an inflatable banana to the next game, and then everyone started doing it.

At a time of hooliganism taking over football, it added some light-hearted fun to a hostile atmosphere.



Friend explained: “They weren’t interested in fighting.

“Most of the fans were having a laugh.

“We were s***, we were in Division Two.

“I think, every now and then, when it’s fan-led and not club-led, [bringing back the bananas] can be really good. It’ll be a laugh.”

Sports.title: LASK 3 Liverpool 6: Bradley Barcola finally gets off mark for Reds with stunning hat-trick… but defensive issues arise
Sports.content:
Next

AT LEAST this might be the start of something good for Liverpool and Andoni Iraola.

At least Bradley Barcola collected a treble and Florian Wirtz actually looked like he was enjoying himself.



But an Austrian waltz doesn’t necessarily suggest that the pair are going to help Liverpool dance towards silverware.

Try Brentford on Saturday at the Gtech. Try attempting to forget how Iraola’s side fell apart at Anfield after Ryan Gravenberch was red-carded against Manchester City.



Remember that until Barcola and Wirtz came up against a LASK side that was there for the taking right the pair who could ultimately cost a total of £239million had come up with ONE assist between them before arriving in Linz.

Recall also that after the City humiliation one Anfield legend in Jamie Carragher declared that Wirtz, who arrived from Bayer Leverkusen as a double Bundesliga player of the year 15 months ago “wasn’t working.”



Or how another in ex-skipper Steven Gerrard declared that floundering Flo needed “help,” adding: “ I can just picture him beating himself up on how his Liverpool thing started.”

Well, at least he looked a lot happier as Iraola’s side claimed their second successive Champions League victory.

Barcola, too, with his first-ever senior hat-trick – except that the reality since the pair teamed up at the start of this campaign is that they have been almost embarrassingly poor.

They, Iraola and the rest of the side that floated through their opponents last night, were entitled to a little joy because since the Spaniard replaced Arne Slot there has been precious little of that.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Reality will be back to bite at Brentford and only then and in a Premier League campaign that will continue, will Iraola know whether he really does have two Kop superstars on his hands.

Or if he sees them go straight back into their shells.

Liverpool took control right from the start even if Iraola took a couple of gambles.

Rested was captain Virgil van Dijk, the first time in 39 games he hadn’t started in the Champions League leaving a back four that had never played together.

Further up youngsters Lewis Koumas (21), Rio Ngumoha (18) and Trey Nyoni (19) were brought in as Iraola made four changes from the side that was hammered 3-0 by City.



Then again the Spaniard’s team were up against a club that was playing in only its second home fixture in the Champions League proper since 1985.

They finished last season as Austrian double winners and they did produce a magnificent 5-1 victory to come from four goals down to beat Celtic to come through the play-offs.

But they began their European campaign with a limp 1-0 defeat to away to AEK Athens and by the 24th minute – after Barcola had lashed home Liverpool’s second – they didn’t look like they belonged in Europe’s elite.



Iraola was without injured attacking stars Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai and how that hurt them against City.

But he could have played almost a whole team of youngsters and still come away with a victory from Austria’s steel town on Linz.

It was boys against men and the kids were alright.

Liverpool went ahead in the 22nd minute as Ronald Araujo claimed his first goal since his summer arrival on loan from Barcelona with a simple header.

Koumas thought he had his first Champions League goal after barging through his side’s red-clad opponents but his effort was ruled offside.



No matter. Within 120 seconds Barcola had his first of the night, thanks to the darting menace of Ngumoha.

He caused panic as he flashed his way into the LASK box, forcing it to Koumas who showed the experience of a veteran to touch backwards.

Barcola smashed home the kind of chance he had dreamed of for the six long, long games in which he had struggled so desperately since arriving from Paris Saint-Germain.



By the 37th minute the Frenchman was celebrating his second as – finally – he made a killing connection with Wirtz.

He picked up a loose ball, flicked on to his new German team-mate who had looked far livelier than for months.

Then the player who has so often looked like a lost soul and hardly a wonder playmaker, delivered a delicious through-ball.

Barcola was not going to miss and the only question that remained was by how many Liverpool would win by.

A lot more, as it should have turned out.



Jeremie Frimpong clipped home the fourth from close range, Barcola then taking a neat pass from the full back to claim his treble after another brilliant contribution from Ngumoha.

Koumas finally got the goal he’ll always have dreamed of, but at the back Liverpool were switching off.

Robert Ljubicic grabbed a first for the home side, Florian Flecker added two more in seven minutes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But the job had already been done. The real hard work starts again on Saturday.

It will likely be a lot tougher than this goal-fest that was little more than a relaxing re-boot.

Sports.title: Why are Shakhtar playing their Champions League home games at Stamford Bridge?
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA did not qualify for the Champions League this season, but Stamford Bridge will still play host to Europe’s top competition as Shakhtar take over West London.

The Ukrainian giants have agreed a deal to host their ‘home’ games at the Blues’ home.



SHAKHTAR VS AEK ATHENS LIVE

Shakhtar were held to a draw against PSV in their opening Champions League game of the season – Sergino Dest equalised for the Dutchmen after Gleiker Mendoza’s opener.



Now, they head to London for their first ‘home’ game, where they are hoping to play in front of around 30,000 fans.

Why are Shakhtar playing their Champions League home games at Stamford Bridge?

Shakhtar are from the Ukrainian city of Donetsk, but they haven’t played at the Donbas Arena since 2014.

Due to security reasons amid Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Shakhtar needed somewhere else to play their home Champions League fixtures.

Since the 2022 invasion, the Ukrainian champions have played their ‘home’ games in Poland, Germany and Slovenia.

Over the past three seasons, they played their at German sides Hamburg and Schalke, as well as Poland’s Wisla Krakow.

After discussions with Brentford and Fulham, they ended up choosing Stamford Bridge as their base for this season.



Shakhtar chief executive Sergei Palkin said that Stamford Bridge gives the club the best opportunity to show that Ukraine remains “alive” during a difficult period.

Palkin went on to say: “There are a lot of Ukrainian refugees and a lot of Ukrainians living here.

“London is the football capital of the world. It’s the biggest marketplace for players.

“For our young players to play at this level in a legendary stadium like Stamford Bridge provides extra motivation and can bring positive results.

“I first contacted Behdad Eghbali (Chelsea co-owner) and said: ‘What do you think about this idea – playing Champions League matches in your stadium?’



“The reaction was positive. Step by step, it became a reality. Chelsea were very professional.”

Talks between the clubs began in July, as the Ukrainians were forced to abandon the Donbas Arena when Russian troops invaded Crimea and a war broke out in the region in 2014.

Upon the announcement, Chelsea said: “FC Shakhtar have played in countries across Europe and we look forward to welcoming them to London for their Champions League campaign this year.

“We will be working with the Shakhtar team closely over the coming weeks to ensure that matchdays run safely and smoothly for their team and supporters.”

Sports.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola scored a hat-trick and Florian Wirtz shone after recent criticism as Liverpool thrashed LASK 6-3 to earn their second win in the Champions League.

Barcola kick-started his Liverpool career, having not scored or assisted in six appearances since his £123m move from Paris Saint-Germain, while Wirtz responded to calls for him to be dropped with a fine performance in what was expected to be a comfortable evening against the Austrian Bundesliga champions.

Liverpool had 19 shots in the opening period, a new record for an away team in the first half of a Champions League game, as Ronald Araujo headed in his first goal for the club before Barcola got off the mark with a tidy finish and then slotted in another from a Wirtz pass.

Andoni Iraola's side were relentless with Trey Nyoni, 19, impressing in midfield alongside Ryan Gravenberch and they helped add a fourth when Jeremie Frimpong met Kostas Tsimikas' cross with an excellent header that went in off the post just six minutes after the break.

Iraola benched Virgil van Dijk in Austria for only the third time in Liverpool's 39 Champions League games since 2022, but when he and Joe Gomez were introduced at centre-back in the 62nd minute, they conceded three times.

Barcola's hat-trick, a tap-in from Frimpong's cross, followed Robert Ljubicic's consolation before Wales striker Lewis Koumas, leading the line in Alexander Isak's absence, deservedly scored Liverpool's sixth after he had two efforts ruled out for offside.

Florian Flecker reduced the deficit late on with two clinical finishes in two minutes, exposing Liverpool's sloppy defending to take some shine off the victory.

Sports.title: Red Roses make four changes to starting XV for Canada Test
Sports.content:
England's Red Roses have made four changes to their starting XV for their game against Canada in Rugby's WXV Global Series.

Experienced hooker Amy Cokayne, centre Tatyana Heard, loosehead prop Hannah Botterman and back-row Abi Burton are each brought in to start in Toronto by head coach John Mitchell.

The Red Roses face Canada on Saturday a month after they were held to an entertaining 26-26 draw in Exeter, and having most-recently needed a try in the final play of the match to beat New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

To make way for the four alterations, centre Helena Rowland, hooker Bryony Field and prop Mackenzie Carson drop down to the replacements bench, while flanker Sadia Kabeya returns to the bench following a leg injury with Marlie Packer missing England's North American tour ahead of partner Rosie Galligan giving birth.

5m ago 15.36 EDT GOAL! Manchester City 0-3 Paris Saint-Germain (Vitinha 32) A cross into the City box from the left. Hakimi’s header caroms off the left-hand post. But PSG don’t feel sorry for themselves. They come again., Zaire-Emery back-flicking Akliouche’s low right-wing cross back into the path of Vitinha, who opens his body and slams forensically into the right-hand side of the net. Donnarumma with no chance! View image in fullscreen Wow! This could get very messy for MAn City. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at 15.41 EDT

7m ago 15.34 EDT 30 min: Zaïre-Emery’s drive is blocked by Guehi. Akliouche then brushes Semenyo off the ball. The referee’s whistle goes, awarding City a very generous foul. Akliouche, livid, lashes the ball into the net from long range. It won’t count, obviously, but neither is he booked. Share

9m ago 15.32 EDT 29 min: Vitinha is given a little bit too much time to the left of the City D. He doesn’t catch his shot properly, and it’s claimed by Donnarumma before it can squeak into the bottom left. Share

11m ago 15.30 EDT 27 min: PSG again with the metronomic passing, their fans again with the olés. The City of Manchester Stadium is otherwise pretty quiet, save for some pensive mumbling. Share

12m ago 15.29 EDT 25 min: … but City come again, through Doku down the left. Doku wedges a cross into the middle for Haaland, who from close range should do much better with his header than send it sailing back through the six-yard box. The ball clanks out for a corner, from which nothing comes. Share

13m ago 15.28 EDT 24 min: Semenyo crosses poorly from the right, looking for Haaland. As the ball sails high over the bar, the PSG fans – en fête – cheer in the hearty style. Share

15m ago 15.27 EDT 23 min: Nuno Mendes should release Fabian Ruiz into acres down the right. But he clanks a seemingly simple pass straight at Guehi. Had he made it, Ruiz was one-on-one with Donnarumma and City were facing a world of pain. Share

17m ago 15.25 EDT 21 min: PSG are passing it around to a chorus of “olé!”s from their fans. To be fair, City and their players have heard worse recently. Share

19m ago 15.22 EDT 19 min: Haaland takes matters into his own hands with a power-bustle down the middle. He reaches the box, but he’s been pushed a little to the left by Pacho, who then blocks the shot with a well-timed lunge … and nothing comes from the resulting corner. City and their fans a little bit stunned here. Share

21m ago 15.21 EDT 17 min: One minute and 39 seconds elapsed between the goals. And it could be three, because Vitinha has a shot aimed for the bottom left deflected off Khusanov’s ankle and towards the bottom right, making things much easier for Donnarumma. On the touchline, all the blood drains from Enzo Maresca’s face. Share Updated at 15.24 EDT

22m ago 15.19 EDT GOAL! Manchester City 0-2 Paris Saint-Germain (Dembélé 15) It’s a double whammy! In their very next attack, Dembélé crosses long from the right. Doué takes the ball down on the left, afforded too much space by Khusanov, and returns it to the far post, where Dembélé plants a header home! View image in fullscreen Ousmane Dembélé doubles the lead for PSG! Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 15.30 EDT

24m ago 15.18 EDT GOAL! Manchester City 0-1 Paris Saint-Germain (Doue 13) From the restart, PSG play their way upfield. From the right wing to the left. Doué cuts in from the flank and from the edge of the box, decides to see if he can trick Donnarumma at his near post. And he can do it! Having given the keeper the eyes, he whistles a low drive into the bottom left! That’s a hell of a move with a finish to match. View image in fullscreen Desire Doue scores a brilliant opener for PSG. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 15.30 EDT

25m ago 15.16 EDT 12 min: It wasn’t a penalty, but City do get a free kick, because at the end of the phase of play, Semenyo was fouled out on the left. Fernandez sends the set piece low towards the near post, where Safanov clumsily bundles the ball around his post. From the corner, Safonov punches the ball onto his own crossbar, then Semenyo skies a shot over the bar from six yards! But Guehi is penalised anyway for a shove on the keeper. Share

27m ago 15.14 EDT 10 min: Cherki bursts into the PSG box down the left. Marquinhos sticks a leg across him. Cherki goes over. There’s contact – and a VAR check – but turns out Marquinhos got a touch on the ball. No penalty. View image in fullscreen Rayan Cherki goes down in the box after contact from Marquinhos. No penalty, says the ref. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters Share Updated at 15.16 EDT

28m ago 15.14 EDT 8 min: Akliouche looks to have won a corner off Gvardiol down the right, but the linesman awards a goal kick. From the restart, Semenyo gets a bit careless and allows Zaïre-Emery a shot. Donnarumma has it covered. Share

32m ago 15.09 EDT 6 min: Semenyo surges down the inside-right channel but his flick towards Cherki on the wing is no good. But that’s City’s first sortie into enemy territory. Share

34m ago 15.08 EDT 4 min: The PSG fans are making all of the noise. City’s supporters are subdued, perhaps all tuckered out after partying hard at Anfield. Share

36m ago 15.06 EDT 2 min: Cherki is caught dozing by Dembélé, who sends Doué scampering down a cul-de-sac on the left. Cherki will be pleased Khusanov was on point there. Share

38m ago 15.04 EDT PSG, in their blue shirts with red central panel, launch the kick-off in their usual rugby-union style. City in their sky blue. Share

39m ago 15.03 EDT The teams make it onto the pitch … after a fashion. City left their visitors waiting in the tunnel for a couple of minutes. Then the Champions League theme, to the usual chorus of disgust. As loud as the Uefa-focused opprobrium usually is? Not sure; it’s almost as though City fans have their minds on a different admin-infused opponent. Whatever, the atmosphere seems a little subdued; everyone’s been through the ringer, one way or the other, in recent weeks. Sure it’ll get going in a minute when the match eventually kicks off (late). Share

55m ago 14.47 EDT Enzo Maresca speaks to TNT. “It’s a special night … Champions League night against the best team in Europe … hopefully we can win the game … I know Pep [Guardiola] will be here but he was not at the training ground [earlier today] and I did not speak with him … by showing support to the club even when he is not here, for sure it’s a special moment for him tonight also … he is back to his home … also for the fans, they will be happy to see Pep here tonight … to beat PSG you need a complete performance … on and off the ball … we are going to create some chances and concede some chances … we need to find the right balance.” Share

2h ago 14.02 EDT Manchester City go strong in the wake of their 3-0 win at Anfield. Jeremy Doku, Abdukodir Khusanov and Josko Gvardiol replace Iliman Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes and Nico O’Reilly in the starting XI. PSG haven’t quite gone so strong, in so much as Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is only on the bench. But then again he can come off it later when everyone else is a bit knackered, so it’s swings and roundabouts. Ferran Torres, erstwhile of City, is also named as a sub. View image in fullscreen Irrefutable evidence. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian Share Updated at 14.10 EDT

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola’s clinical hat-trick inspires Liverpool to 6-3 rout of Lask
Sports.content:
Liverpool cleansed themselves from the stains of defeat by Manchester City at the earliest opportunity. A rampant performance in Austria, where Bradley Barcola opened his account for Andoni Iraola’s side with a hat-trick, maintained Liverpool’s 100% start to the Champions League and shattered Lask’s big night on the elite European stage.

Iraola defended the majority of Liverpool’s display against City, the club’s £123m signing from Paris Saint-Germain and the effectiveness of Florian Wirtz before the return to European action. His faith and confidence were rewarded as his team routed limited opponents who may have surprised themselves to score three in consolation. Barcola hit his stride in a Liverpool shirt with Ronald Araújo also scoring his first goal for the club on a restorative evening in Linz.

The home end was full and in strong voice over an hour before kick-off as Lask supporters came to savour their club’s first home game in the Champions League proper. The Lask team proved to be much less impressive though, in fairness to the Austrian crowd, their support rarely wavered even as a rout unfolded. Liverpool revelled in their superiority and the invitation to recover from Sunday’s first defeat of the season.

Iraola rested Virgil van Dijk, delaying the defender’s 200th game as Liverpool captain, and Alexis Mac Allister as he managed workloads ahead of Saturday’s visit to Brentford. A new-look central defence of Araújo and Jérémy Jacquet were given a physical test by the Lask strikers Samuel Adeniran and Krystof Danek but handled the hosts’ rudimental approach comfortably. Araújo also showcased his attacking talents. It was the on-loan defender’s ball that Wirtz took in his stride before gliding between two Lask players and testing the goalkeeper, Lukas Jungwirth, with a low shot. Araújo then headed wide from a Kostas Tsimikas corner. He would find his range from the stand-in captain’s next set piece.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola slides the ball into the bottom corner to score his second in the first half. Photograph: Dénes Erdős/AP

Liverpool were utterly dominant against an opponent that struggled to retain possession in all areas of the pitch. The breakthrough was inevitable but also a result of uncertainty in the Lask defence. Alemão had to concede the first of two successive corners after his keeper failed to come off his line to collect a routine through ball. From the second corner, conceded by Alemão’s headed clearance, Araújo towered above his marker to head home Tsimikas’s delivery.

Merely 96 seconds later it was 2-0 as Barcola also opened his account for Liverpool. The summer recruit found himself under scrutiny ahead of the game, along with Wirtz, having gone six appearances for his new club without a goal or an assist. That issue was put to bed when Rio Ngumoha weaved in from the right and, after the teenager had stumbled, Lewis Koumas laid the ball back to the lurking winger. Barcola swept a first-time shot inside Jungwirth’s far post. Liverpool were enjoying themselves.

Wirtz soon found himself with a much-needed assist for Barcola’s second goal of the evening. The Germany international has looked more at home for Liverpool in the Champions League than Premier League and this was no exception. Wirtz picked out his fellow big-money signing’s run into the Lask area and Barcola rolled a cool finish beyond the exposed keeper.

Lask could have been seriously embarrassed before half-time. Koumas had a fine finish disallowed for offside and, following another neat exchange between Wirtz and Barcola, Ryan Gravenberch saw his shot kiss the inside of the far post and rebound clear. Liverpool’s 19 attempts on goal were the most by an away side in the first half of a Champions League game since records began in 2003-04.

View image in fullscreen Liverpool’s Lewis Koumas jumps for joy after opening his Champions League account. Photograph: Michael Zemanek/Shutterstock

There would be no letup from Iraola’s team after the interval. Jeremie Frimpong morphed into an old-fashioned centre-forward to rise above Yvan Dibango and bury a textbook header into the bottom corner when Tsimikas floated a delightful cross over from the left byline.

Koumas had a second goal disallowed for offside before Alisson’s clean sheet was ruined by the Lask substitute Robert Ljubicic sweeping home inside his near post. The Brazil keeper’s disgust washed over his teammates. Barcola was presented with his hat-trick when Ngumoha released Frimpong down the right and the full-back flashed a low cross through the Lask six-yard box. The unmarked Barcola applied a simple finish at the back post.

Frimpong also supplied the assist for Koumas’s deserved goal, converted from close range after the home side were caught playing out from the back. The Lask substitute Florian Flecker brought a touch of respectability to the scoreline with two goals in four minutes, both from Dibango deliveries from the left, but there was no disguising the emphatic manner of Liverpool’s victory nor the surge of confidence it should give to Barcola.

Sports.title: ‘I expect more’: the key questions from Martínez’s Manchester United broadside | Jamie Jackson
Sports.content:
After Manchester United’s 2-0 loss at Atlético Madrid, Lisandro Martínez teed off at the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and the rest of the executive. “We don’t have the best squad at the moment compared with other top teams,” said the defender. “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Jason Wilcox] … Really poor [the Atlético defeat] – I have to control myself a lot but something is a reflection of the mirror of how our club is at the moment.” Here we consider the key questions emerging from Martínez’s explosive remarks.

Is Martínez’s view reflective of the squad generally?

Yes is the short answer. The Guardian has been told the decision to target three midfielders in Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba caused bemusement in the squad that no other areas were strengthened in the summer. Carrick led United to third last term after the side only had 17 league games remaining when he took over in January, having been eliminated from the other competitions. The need for defensive reinforcements is particularly acute because the back four of Diogo Dalot, Martínez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw has been together since 2022. Martínez is out of contract next summer and it is thought the 28-year-old may not be offered a new deal or have his one-year option triggered by the club, so teammates are conscious his outburst also came because he expects to leave.

How culpable is Wilcox?

As United’s director of football the 55-year-old wields near-unilateral power on football decisions, with only Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls sporting policy, above him. If the buck stops with the executive, the most recent transfer window was Wilcox’s responsibility. This was the latest in a line of missteps on his United record. One concerns when Dan Ashworth (Wilcox’s predecessor) was on gardening leave from Newcastle in the first half of 2024, Wilcox interviewed potential replacements for Erik ten Hag before, oddly, deeming that the head coach should stay. The Dutchman signed a fresh contract but was sacked that autumn. Another involves Wilcox’s major falling out with the man he hired as the Dutchman’s successor, Ruben Amorim, after which the Portuguese said the director of football had told him he should change his favoured 3-4-3 shape. “I came here to be the manager of Manchester United – not to be the coach of Manchester United,” said Amorim, after a 1-1 draw at Leeds on 4 January (his job title was head coach). He was sacked the next day. Wilcox worked with Omar Berrada, United’s chief executive, at Manchester City, where Berrada rose to become chief football operations officer, and Wilcox became academy director. Wilcox moved to Southampton and became director of football from summer 2023 until April 2024, when he joined United, having been identified by Berrada, so there is scrutiny of his experience at elite level.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez’s post-match interview has exposed the divisions at Manchester United. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

How much blame is Carrick’s?

The 45-year-old’s ability to prosper is related to the quality of Wilcox’s work, primarily in the market, so he cannot be solely responsible for a dire six points from six league games and two victories in all competitions all season. Yet by definition his role as head coach demands Carrick do the best with his resources, and that progress is made on the training ground. On matchdays there is scant excuse for United’s disjointedness, inferior running stats and inability, twice, to take advantage against 10 men: the 1-0 loss to City and Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham. How is Carrick viewed by his players? According to Santos they back him. “We believe in the manager, we believe in the whole staff, we believe in [ourselves as] players,” he said after the Atlético game. “We are in a bad moment but we have to work to change this result.”.

Is United’s unity and discipline crumbling?

For further evidence see Amad Diallo’s Snapchat post after the defeat by Atlético: “Fucking disgrace; I have no words.” So United have a World Cup-winner, Martínez, aiming shots at Wilcox and by implication Ratcliffe and Berrada, and a fellow senior player, Diallo, cursing but in ambiguous fashion, adding to the sense of meltdown at the club because it is unclear whether the “disgrace” meant the performance, Martínez’s diatribe, the squad his teammate referred to as not good enough, or something else. All of this is mirrored on the pitch, where United’s 671.4km run in the Premier League is the fifth-lowest (Arsenal’s 716.2 is the highest), and their 581 sprints the fourth-lowest (Brentford’s 765 the most).

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick has support from his squad but Manchester United’s form has dropped significantly this season. Photograph: Susana Vera/Reuters

Where are the Glazers in all this?

In mitigation Wilcox can point to the six American siblings, who remain majority owners and whose family has placed an eye-watering £1.1bn-plus debt on the club that severely restricts the transfer budget. Wilcox oversaw a £155m summer outlay and a net spend of about £100m in a summer when City’s corresponding figures were £457.5m and about £175m. City buying players such as Enzo Fernández (for a British record-equalling £125m), Elliot Anderson (£115m), Ayyoub Bouaddi (£81m) and Iliman Ndiaye (£65m) showed their greater financial muscle, helped by being much better sellers of talent. How they have reached this point has, though, been thrown into sharp focus by last month’s verdict that they have serially cheated.

Are there positives for United?

Any straw should be clutched at so Carrick and his staff can view the first 97 minutes of Baleba’s United career as a rosy augury. After entering on 59 minutes against Spurs, a cute swivel and deft chip to Bruno Fernandes was a moment as impressive as the rest of his debut, and at Atlético the 22-year-old hunted down opponents and crunched into tackles, suggesting his game contains energy, muscularity and skill. It’s early days but perhaps if Baleba had been fit to start the campaign (he was recovering from an ankle problem) he might have affected one or more of the defeat at Hull, the 2-2 draw at Everton when Ainsley Maitland-Niles equalised late, the 1-0 loss to City when Phil Foden was sent off after 23 minutes or the Carabao Cup elimination by Brighton.

Sports.title: Manchester City staff invited on government trade trip to India
Sports.content:
A club representative from Manchester City was invited on a government-backed trade delegation to India this week, despite the club being found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League rules.

Andy Burnham’s successor as Manchester mayor Bev Craig took a representative from the club to Delhi and Mumbai on a trip organised by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds, where she and other northern mayors have been promoting British trade and tourism.

She defended the decision to invite City even as the prime minister came under fire for his own contacts with the club, telling the Guardian it had played a vital role in helping build infrastructure in her city.

“If a football club has broken the rules, a football club should be punished for breaking the rules, and that is pretty clear in an independent process,” she said.

“I think what can also be true at the same time though, if you ask residents in east Manchester, have they benefited from a new library, a new leisure centre, a new sixth-form college, infrastructure investment, the job opportunities that come from them being a good employment charter signee and an early adopter of the real living wage – then they will have felt that benefit.”

City, which says it is innocent of the charges and has appealed against them, declined to comment.

The revelation comes as Burnham faced pressure over his relationship with City’s owners during his time as mayor of Greater Manchester. The prime minister was forced to clarify on Wednesday that he had two additional dinners with the club chair, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, at the Etihad Stadium, having previously declared those only as matchday hospitality.

Speaking at PMQs, Burnham said no one from the club had raised the Premier League charges with him.

Craig’s defence of the club came as her mayoral authority published details of Burnham’s contacts with City officials when he was mayor.

The release showed the prime minister had attended a formal meeting with al-Mubarak, chatted to him in the stands at a player’s testimonial game and was accompanied by staff from the club on official overseas visits.

But the Sun newspaper revealed later on Monday that Burnham had twice attended a pre-match dinner with the chair, which was declared in now-deleted council paperwork. No 10 said it was routine for the records to be deleted when a new mayor was in place.

View image in fullscreen Andy Burnham with Khaldoon al-Mubarak. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

Burnham’s initial response to the findings against City had drawn criticism after he said he would be “really concerned” if its Abu Dhabi owners sold the club in the wake of the Premier League findings, calling them a “huge partner in the building of modern Manchester”.

As the prime minister came under fire for his comments, Downing Street clarified that he believed where wrongdoing had been established, those responsible should face the consequences.

City attended the trade delegation alongside several other northern sports and leisure organisations, including Lancashire cricket club and Visit Lake District. While in India, the football club took part in an event in Delhi promoting British tourism.

The Great North – a coalition of mayors from the north of England which organised the India event – said its aim was “to shine a spotlight on the great tourism products across the north of England”.​
