The Greater Manchester mayoral authority said on Tuesday that representatives of Greater Manchester sporting clubs would “routinely join business delegations” on international visits during Burnham’s time as mayor.

Burnham’s defence of City and its owners has focused attention not only on his links to the club but on how reliant he was on investment from Abu Dhabi to power Manchester’s strong growth rates when he was mayor.

View image in fullscreen Andy Burnham with Bev Craig after her victory in the Greater Manchester mayoral election. Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA

Other senior politicians on this week’s trade delegation include Jonathan Reynolds, the business secretary, Douglas Alexander, the Scotland secretary, and Angela Eagle, the environment secretary.

Reynolds took part in a Premier League event on Tuesday, where he met schoolchildren being taught by British-trained coaches. He denied afterwards that the charges against City had tainted the league’s reputation. It is otherwise one of Britain’s most successful cultural exports.

“The brand of the Premier League – one of the UK’s most important brands … that is incredibly powerful,” he said.

Asked whether it was appropriate for City to have been invited, given the charges it faced, he said: “That’s a Greater Manchester issue, and obviously they are a major participant in the economy in Greater Manchester.

“I understand the interest – the relationship between Manchester and Manchester City – but in terms of the allegations, their appeal, that is a football matter.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino faces grilling at potentially ‘explosive’ Fifa council meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino will be questioned by Fifa council members over his involvement in the aborted World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair and the decision to award Donald Trump the inaugural Fifa peace prize at what is expected to be a heated meeting at the world governing body’s headquarters on Thursday.

The Fifa president rejected repeated calls for an extraordinary general meeting of council in the summer after the emergence of the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals, but will meet his critics for the first time since then in Zurich, with one attender predicting that the talks could be “explosive”.

Aleksander Ceferin, Victor Montagliani and Sheikh Salman Bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, the presidents of Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation respectively, all of whom have called for Infantino to resign, will be present to press home demands for an independent review of Fifa’s governance.

Quick Guide How do I 

In response to letters from Ceferin, Montagliani and Salman sent last month Infantino pledged to commission an external review of Fifa’s future governance, but no details have been forthcoming, and there is scepticism over whether it will be truly independent.

In addition to FFE, Balogun and the peace prize, which featured on an agenda circulated by Fifa last month, Infantino is also likely to face questions about a report in the Times this week that he received a “second salary” of about £1.3m in 2024, on top of the £3.9m declared in Fifa’s accounts.

US Internal Revenue Service filings show a Fifa subsidiary in charge of running last summer’s World Cup paid Infantino $1.76m, that was not mentioned in Fifa’s annual report, in which his salary is recorded as 4.27m Swiss francs (£3.86m).

Fifa statutes state that “the individual compensation of the Fifa president … shall be made public”. The governing body has denied wrongdoing.

“Fifa does not pay a second salary to the Fifa president and complies with all reporting requirements in relation to compensation,” it said. “The Fifa president’s annual compensation, as well as other contractual benefits, are decided by the independent compensation subcommittee.

“Fifa strongly rejects any claims that it has failed to disclose any financial information and has violated Fifa’s statutes. Fifa accounts are independently audited, and all declarations are in line with tax regulations in Switzerland, the United States and elsewhere.”

Despite these controversies, and the public opposition of the European, Asian and North and Central American and Caribbean confederations, Infantino is on course to be re-elected unopposed in March’s election.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Montagliani has rejected calls to stand against Infantino to focus on being re-elected as Concacaf’s president and Uefa has yet to find an alternative candidate despite tentatively sounding out high-profile footballing figures including Arsène Wenger and Michele Kang, who owns clubs including London City Lionesses.

The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to stand is 18 November, with the election due to be held at Fifa congress in Rabat on 18 March.

Infantino is expected to put forward a £2.6bn increase in the amount of money Fifa hands out for global football development at the meeting in Zurich, using cash from the governing body’s reserves to do so. The hike, covering funding from 2027 to 2030, would take the total Fifa spend on football development for the period to £4.83bn.

Sports.title: Sunderland hope to enjoy warmth in Portugal after 53 years away
Sports.content:
There is a pleasing symmetry about Sunderland’s Europa League trip to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday night. The club’s last competitive venture on European soil, 53 years ago, was the second leg of a European Cup Winners’ Cup second-round tie against Sporting in Lisbon for the FA Cup holders, then in the Second Division.

In a striking parallel, second-tier Torreense prompted widespread surprise by beating Sporting in the Portuguese Cup final last season. The reward was a place in the Europa League and their chances of reaching the next phase of the competition early next year were boosted when they beat Lillestrøm 2-1 in Norway last month.

Torreense are struggling in the league – they sit 15th with six points from seven games. They face a side who have made an underwhelming opening to the Premier League campaign featuring one win, against their fellow strugglers Fulham.

With a visit to Bournemouth, who are 18th, a place and a point below Sunderland, on Sunday, Régis Le Bris is expected to rotate his squad. Even so, it would be a minor shock if Sunderland fail to beat Torreense.

Torreense’s home ground, the Estádio Manuel Marques in Torres Vedras, 31 miles north of Lisbon, holds 2,431 spectators, falling short of Uefa regulations. This has prompted the match being switched to the medieval town of Leiria, an hour’s drive north of Torres Vedras and almost two hours from the luxury Lisbon hotel where Sunderland are basing themselves after failing to find suitable accommodation elsewhere.

Almost 4,000 Sunderland fans are travelling to the 23,888-capacity Estádio Dr Magalhães Pessoa, normally the home of second-tier União Leiria. With a limited supply of local hotel rooms, some are staying in Lisbon or Porto, while others have found lodgings in nearby towns and villages, including Fátima. A pilgrimage town, Fátima is one of the most important shrines in the Catholic world and attracts more than six million tourists every year. As visitors from Wearside sightsee in forecast bright sunshine and 25C, they may be tempted to pray for respite from a harsh north-east winter at the Stadium of Light.

Although Sunderland have played well at times this season, the failure to sign a specialist right-winger during the summer has led to Le Bris frequently fielding two natural right-backs in Trai Hume and Thomas Meunier. Hamstring injuries to Brian Brobbey and Dan Ballard have caused problems at both ends of the pitch and the previously reliable Robin Roefs has suffered a few untypical goalkeeping wobbles.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland’s keeper, Robin Roefs, has slipped from his usual high standards at times this season. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Ed Sykes/Sportsphoto

Context is required though. Sunderland’s first six league fixtures have been against the present top four – Manchester City, Arsenal, Brighton and Brentford. Nonetheless, quiet concern will segue into downright panic should the next two domestic games – at Bournemouth and then at home to Leeds – fail to produce at least one win. There is also anxiety that Malick Fofana, the £30m left-winger signed from Lyon on deadline day who is struggling to displace the erratic Nilson Angulo, may be too lightweight for England’s top tier.

On Tuesday evening, Sunderland announced their set-piece coach, James Brayne, had left and would be replaced by Thor Herdal. The 34-year-old arrives from Nordsjælland, where he was head of set pieces and analysis. He has also worked with Denmark’s national team.

Given that Sunderland travel to Poland to face Lech Poznan next Thursday, minimising travel and the attendant fatigue has become a priority. It explains why they will fly straight from Lisbon to Bournemouth on Friday.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Not that Torreense intend to merely make up the numbers. Back in the club’s home town, locals are preparing for an annual national day of celebration on 20 October.

It commemorates the role played by an imposing series of forts and military defences built in 1809-10 and known as the Lines of Torres Vedras in defending Lisbon from French invaders during the Peninsular war.

Torreense are hoping to demonstrate similarly stout resistance against a team led by a Frenchman and with several French-speaking players.

Sunderland have reason to be wary of Stopira, Torreense’s influential 38-year-old captain and left-back, who played for Cape Verde at this summer’s World Cup, and their gifted playmaker João Marques and Ghanaian striker Malik Abubakari. The challenge for Sunderland is to use this last blast of southern European warmth to revitalise a season in danger of unravelling.

Sports.title: Tottenham’s forgotten man Richarlison scores for under-21s: ‘I was missing it’
Sports.content:
Tottenham’s forgotten man Richarlison has been hailed for his attitude after he scored for the under-21s on Tuesday. Richarlison has not played for the first team since an opening-day defeat at Brentford on 22 August after he was left out of the 25-man Premier League squad list, having been told he was not part of the plans for this season.

Failed moves to Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama, after talks with Everton collapsed in the final days before the transfer window in England shut, have left Richarlison in limbo for the first half of the campaign. However, the Brazil international made a surprise appearance in the Jersey Mike’s (EFL) Trophy tie at Cheltenham. He scored after 56 minutes in a 2-2 draw and converted a spot-kick in a 7-6 penalty shootout loss.

The Cheltenham manager, Steve Cotterill, told Gloucestershire Live: “We weren’t expecting it. When I found out he was on the team sheet, I was actually chuffed with that. It gives our lads a glimpse of what it’s like at that top level.

“Richarlison’s attitude was immaculate tonight. He was really, really good and his attitude was great. He could have easily come down here and thought: ‘I am not too bothered about tonight.’

“We had a decent crowd here, but he’s used to playing in front of 60,000 every week – when he gets picked anyway. It was great for our lads to play against someone of his stature. I really enjoyed tonight.”

After Richarlison’s fine first-time finish in the 56th minute, Tottenham’s academy players joined him in performing his pigeon celebration. He later posted on Instagram: “Happy to do what I love the most in life. I was missing it!”

Sports.title: Removing political speech from MLS fans is untenable – just ask Austin FC
Sports.content:
On 26 September, Daniela Silva was expelled from Austin FC’s match with San Diego FC for wearing a T-shirt reading “Abolish ICE”. She says she was banned from Q2 Stadium for a year (Austin FC said that the ban was issued by the Austin Police Department, not the club, and that they offered to rescind it but that Silva declined).

This happened, really, truly, and you cannot make this up, during Austin FC’s Hispanic Heritage Night. It also happened six days after Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents shot a Venezuelan delivery driver, 28-year-old Wilber Garcés Pérez, in the torso in Austin, sparking protests in the city.

The club’s Hispanic Heritage Night included folk dances and highlighted local nonprofits serving the Hispanic community. “For Austin FC, celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month means celebrating the many cultures and communities that help make Austin what it is,” the club’s website still declares.

And yet, a fan sporting a T-shirt with a very reasonable response to the ongoing assault on the Hispanic community of Austin, and indeed the nation, was banished.

The club referred to Q2 Stadium policy, the wording of which is an exact copy of Major League Soccer’s fan code of conduct. Both prohibit, among other things, “Displaying signs, symbols or images for commercial purposes or for electioneering, campaigning or advocating for or against any candidate, political party, legislative issue, or government action.” It’s the same policy MLS has cited in several other instances, though an MLS spokesperson said on Wednesday that the league policy no longer governs articles of clothing, but that a stadium policy would, hence why Silva was removed under the stadium policy.

Regardless of which policy was responsible, Austin FC supporter groups Los Verdes and La Murga de Austin took issue, releasing a joint statement. “Opposition to ICE is not an abstract political debate for many of our members and neighbors,” it read. “It is about what is happening here, in our community, and about their safety, dignity, and ability to move through it without fear. In the days since, members of our community have questioned whether they feel safe and welcome returning to Q2. That should matter to Austin FC. The club has a responsibility to communicate clearly that our Hispanic and immigrant communities are welcome and safe at Q2.”

At the club’s home game on Saturday, a 4-1 loss to runaway league leaders Nashville SC, La Murga de Austin walked out in protest of Silva’s ejection, clearing out much of the supporters section. Its banner, reading “NO ICE IN THIS MELTING POT”, was taken down.

“We love this club. But love is not silent,” La Murga said in a statement. “We are asking Austin FC to speak out – publicly, with conviction – against the injustice ICE is inflicting on the communities of Austin. The same communities the club says it supports. The same communities whose faces fill your marketing, whose voices fill your stadium, whose hands and hearts make this place what it is.”

The club told the Guardian it is engaging with supporters on the topic of rules around political messaging in stadiums. But those rules are unjustifiable and, in this climate, possibly even untenable.

MLS has priors when it comes to these ideological confrontations with its own fans. In 2015, it ordered the removal of “Refugees welcome” banners at Toronto FC games. In 2019, the league had to walk back its ban on the Iron Front symbol, first used by anti-Nazi paramilitaries in the 1930s and since broadly appropriated by the antifa movement – which has always been more of an idea than an actual organization but was nevertheless deemed to be political by the league. At the other end of the ideological spectrum, a man in a Make America Great Again hat was ejected from St Louis City’s stadium during a game last year.

In the weeks after the war between Israel and Hamas began in 2023, MLS banned both Israeli and Palestinian flags in its stands as a measure it called “temporary” but which, three years on, remains in place. A carveout exists, however, for Columbus Crew fans, who were awarded an exemption to fly a single Palestinian flag after the club signed Palestinian striker Wessam Abou Ali. Fans of the teams who field the league’s eight Israeli players can fly a single Israeli flag.

Meanwhile, when Latino Nashville fans stayed away from their stadium in droves for fear of ICE arrests on their way home from games, the league did permit a banner reading “We’re not all here” to note their absence. The subtext was self-evident.

Herein lies the trouble. The rules feel squishy because there is no one way to coherently and consistently keep political speech out of stadiums. The notion of apolitical sports, idealized by some as a kind of how-things-used-to-be paradigm that never existed, is a fantasy.

MLS isn’t alone in trying to make it a reality. Most of the other American major leagues try just as hard to stay neutral in any matter that may cost them a few dollars by upsetting fans, or draw the ire of their overwhelmingly conservative owners. Then again, few sports seem to have hardcore fans as politically engaged as those in American soccer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

I’d also argue that the approach is counterproductive. An MLS stadium banning T-shirts with mainstream messages draws far more attention than just treating fans as adults with a worldview, who don’t need to be policed.

MLS loves to highlight its hardcore fans when it sells itself to new audiences. Yet it also wants to sanitize them, rather than just accepting that most of them skew progressive and will proclaim their values accordingly.

A league cannot cleanse itself of the inconveniences of reality outside its facilities, especially when that reality is expressly hostile to as many as 30% of its fans, per its own count. Pretending that it can only leads to ugly episodes like the one in Austin. Not to mention a disillusioned and mistrusting fanbase.

Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now. He teaches at Marist University.

This article was amended on 14 October to reflect MLS’s clarification that, though the wordings of the league’s fan code of conduct and the Q2 Stadium fan code of conduct are identical, the league’s does not govern articles of clothing while a stadium’s may.

Sports.title: Man City fans send defiant unity message with a giant tifo of support at the Etihad in their first home match since guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City fans again threw their support behind their team in their first home game since they were found guilty in the vast majority of their financial charges against the Premier League.

The club's fans displayed a giant tifo reading 'CTID' before kick-off in the Champions League against Paris Saint-Germain – which stands for 'City til I die'.

City are appealing their verdict, which could see them face significant punishment if the decision is upheld.

They played their first game since the verdict against Liverpool on Sunday, winning 3-0.

Their fans opted to see the sunny side of things in mocking their situation, with Liverpool supporters chanting that the club are 'cheats'.

City fans, though, like their players, continue to support their club.

Manchester City fans threw their support behind their club with a giant tifo before their Champions League game against PSG

They continue to back the club and chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in the battle with the Premier League

Another sign on show read: 'In Khaldoon we trust - we've won it all!'

Erling Haaland said after the game against Liverpool: 'Every single person part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time.

'It was tough, it was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone. (It's) important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about, and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do.'

Former City manager Pep Guardiola, meanwhile, was sat in Manchester City's directors' box for the tie, seated behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

The Spaniard, who won six Premier League titles during his ten-year stint in Manchester, also threw his support behind his former side.

The 55-year-old has been replaced by Enzo Maresca, with the new boss now having to contend with the explosive fallout of the Premier League bombshell verdict, in which City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges against them.

The era covering the charges – from 2009 to 2018 – laid the foundations for Guardiola's huge success at the Etihad Stadium, and has called into question the legendary manager's legacy as a result.

City have strenuously denied any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the verdict, while Guardiola took to Instagram in the wake of the findings to publicly back his former club.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola returns to Manchester City: Legendary former boss attends PSG clash after insisting he will 'always be behind' former club following Premier League's bombshell cheating verdict
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has returned to Manchester City for the first time since his emotional farewell in the summer, with his former club marooned in the biggest scandal in English football history.

The Spaniard, who won six Premier League titles during his ten-year stint in Manchester, threw his support behind his former side as they took on Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Guardiola was sat in Manchester City's directors' box for the tie, seated two rows behind chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano.

The 55-year-old has been replaced by Enzo Maresca, with the new boss now having to contend with the explosive fallout of the Premier League bombshell verdict, in which City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges against them.

The era covering the charges - from 2009 to 2018 - laid the foundations for Guardiola's huge success at the Etihad Stadium, and has called into question the legendary manager's legacy as a result.

City have strenuously denied any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal against the verdict, while Guardiola took to Instagram in the wake of the findings to publicly back his former club.

Pep Guardiola has returned to Manchester City for the first time since leaving the club

Guardiola was seated two rows behind Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and chief executive Ferran Soriano

Man City chairman Khaldoon warmly embraced PSG chief executive Nasser Al-Khelaifi before the match

'I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters.

'Let me be clear: we will get through this together.

'I love you all.'

City received an overwhelmingly positive reception in their first match back at the Etihad following the seismic verdict, with supporters rallying around the club despite the sheer volume of charges found against the Premier League leaders.

Prior to kick-off, Man City fans created a tifo reading 'CTID', meaning 'City 'til I die'.

Maresca's side were treated to an altogether more hostile welcome by Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, in their first competitive fixture since the guilty findings.

But the visitors rode the early storm to run away with a convincing 3-0 victory, with their jubilant celebrations the subject of criticism from the watching football world.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki all scored in the space of 13 second-half minutes, with wild scenes in front of an exuberant away end.

Maresca danced down the touchline and stuck fingers in his ears, with staff and players branded arrogant by their detractors.

Maresca hit back at critics before their Champions League tie against Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad.

'Criticised for what?' he said. 'We won 3-0 at Anfield! What do you want us to do? And even if it was 0-1, it would be exactly the same.

'I'm here today, and the players are here today, to win tomorrow's game. And we work every day to win games. It's the only thing, again, that we can think and be focussed.

'The rest? It's just things from outside that we need to deal with, but we were so, so, so happy inside the pitch, and you cannot imagine inside the changing room.'

Maresca added: 'We were very happy, sharing time with our fans. Probably it's been more tough for our fans than our players or for me.

Man City fans made a display reading 'CTID' - City 'til I die - before the Champions League tie

'It's more complicated for them because if I am an Arsenal fan or Utd fan, I look at City fans and say 'hey my friend, you are a cheat'. Inside the changing room we were very happy because we knew how difficult Anfield is. Anfield was unbelievable.'

City skipper Ruben Dias stood behind Maresca's words – and claimed they will continue to celebrate with passion.

'We'll celebrate however we feel in the moment,' Dias said. 'It'll be a show of how much things mean to us.

'Yes there is a lot of noise and it's almost impossible to not see something – even us being so private. But I feel like we're also very good at focusing on ourselves.

'You build yourself against any kind of noise. I feel like I speak for the whole group when I say we're very calm. We trust the club. We know the team we've got and want to win. It's the same noise as before because people don't love us.'

Sports.title: LASK 3-6 Liverpool: Bradley Barcola breaks his duck in stunning style - but Reds must back up impressive performance in the league to regain confidence lost by Man City thumping, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
LASK 3-6 Liverpool: Bradley Barcola breaks his duck in stunning style - but Reds must back up impressive performance in the league to regain confidence lost by Man City thumping, writes LEWIS STEELE

A mid-autumn trip to the sleepy Danubian city of Linz might not be the first outing to pop into mind when Liverpool fans look back on this era in several years – but it might just be an important checkpoint.

It was here in Austria’s third-largest city that the much-criticised £123million new boy Bradley Barcola got his Reds career off the mark with a slick hat-trick. And maybe for manager Andoni Iraola, it was the night the new manager’s style had its lift-off moment and all clicked together.

Another under-fire figure, Florian Wirtz, ran the show as the Reds put in a blistering, relentless display that choked the Austrian champions into submission. The scoreline was not reflective of Liverpool’s dominance on and off the ball.

They attacked at a breakneck speed and in merciless fashion, scoring three times in 16 first-half minutes, as Ronald Araujo’s 22nd-minute header started a rout that left poor LASK goalkeeper Lukas Jungwirth looking like he wanted to tap out and go home.

The victory helped blow away the cobwebs of any potential post-Manchester City hangover and, above all, injected some much-needed confidence into the legs of Liverpool’s attackers ahead of three testing league assignments against Brentford, Brighton and champions Arsenal.

Of course, this impressive performance will mean zero if it is not backed up in west London on Saturday. There have been glimpses of class in most games this season but the problem for new boss Iraola has been sustaining that high level or taking it into the next game.

Bradley Barcola opened his Liverpool account with a hat-trick against LASK on Wednesday

Lewis Koumas scored his first goal of the season on a confidence-boosting evening for Reds

But Liverpool will look to back up a fine showing against European minnows in the league next

Some will also point to the fact that this was LASK’s first-ever main-draw home game in the Champions League and argue Liverpool should be able to beat these rookies with ease. That might be true but let it take nothing away from the easy-on-the-eye performance.

After all, poor old Celtic rocked up here in the qualifying rounds and lost 5-1, a result that might be one to use in your next pub debate about where the Scottish champions would fare in English football.

Speaking of Glasgow, Barcola’s treble was the first away hat-trick for Liverpool since Mohamed Salah did so at Ibrox against Rangers four years ago. Barcola was unplayable and the away end sang about how he ‘runs down the wing for me’ to the tune of Buddy Holly’s Heartbeat.

In truth, he does a lot more than just making runs down the wing. He cuts inside, he can score goals, he is not selfish and enjoys link-up play, he is hard-working off the ball. Or, to summarise, he is a complete player who is a two-time European champion worth £123m for a reason.

Iraola was able to allow Barcola and fellow big-money attacker Wirtz to garner some belief in their ability after a week of being hounded from all quarters, while also giving a rest to some tired stars and handing out minutes to others.

Virgil van Dijk had to settle into the unfamiliar surroundings of the substitutes’ bench, the first league or Champions League game – that was not a meaningless dead-rubber – he had not started since September 2023, though he did come on to captain the Reds for a 200th time.

Jeremie Frimpong, severely lacking in confidence, scored one and assisted another two, while fellow full back Kostas Tsimikas, wearing the armband for an hour, managed two assists and proved his worth as a fine set-piece taker. Iraola will trust both more after this match.

And then there was the energetic, likeable local lad Lewis Koumas. The Wales international scored for the first time this season and, boy, did he deserve it after working his socks off and seeing two strikes chalked off for offside earlier on.

He had also made the assist for the first Barcola goal after canny work from 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha – one of two teenagers starting alongside Trey Nyoni. Barcola’s second showed his ingenuity to wriggle free from a defender, the third demonstrated his positional instinct.

LASK had a late rally with three late goals after Iraola had changed both centre backs, as substitute Florian Flecker scored two in three minutes.

Evidently, there are still a few minor teething problems for the new boss to iron out but this breathtaking attacking display, in the hometown of Adolf Hitler, will give Iraola confidence his team have what it takes to conquer Europe.

Sports.title: Mason Greenwood booed by Aston Villa fans as former Man United star plays in England for the first time in over FOUR years - after Old Trafford career unravelled following rape arrest
Sports.content:
Mason Greenwood was roundly booed by Aston Villa fans, with the former Manchester United star playing football on English soil for the first time since January 2022 in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Greenwood, 25, was regarded as a future star for United having risen through the club's prestigious academy, before his career in England unravelled following his arrest for attempted rape, assault and controlling and coercive behaviour.

Subsequent charges were dropped in February 2023 when key witnesses withdrew. He has denied any wrongdoing.

Since leaving United in 2024, he has enjoyed spells at Getafe and Marseille, before leaving the French club to seal a £36million move to Turkish side Fenerbahce last summer.

Now, back in an English football ground for the first time in over four-and-a-half years, Greenwood was hardly going to slip under the radar.

Greenwood was booed by sections of the crowd at Villa Park when he jogged out for the warm-up – though Fenerbahce’s deafening support did its best to drown out the noise.

Mason Greenwood (pictured) was roundly booed by Aston Villa fans on Wednesday night

There was a similar reaction when the teams were read out and, during the early stages of the match, there were catcalls every time Greenwood touched the ball.

He has a solitary England cap, from a Nations League meeting in Iceland in September 2020. He is also eligible for Jamaica but last year he decided against accepting the call from then-boss Steve McClaren. Before tonight, Greenwood had six goals in 14 appearances for the Istanbul giants.

This was not the first time Greenwood had crossed swords with Villa, having had his shirt partly torn by Tyrone Mings during a pre-season friendly against Marseille in August 2025, following an altercation with Villa midfielder Amadou Onana.

Greenwood, 25, was perhaps grateful that the 6ft 5in Onana missed Wednesday's match due to injury.

More to follow.

Sports.title: Frank Warren calls on Oleksandr Usyk to return and make more boxing history as he plots huge 12 months of heavyweight mega-fights in the United States: 'My door is open'
Sports.content:
Frank Warren calls on Oleksandr Usyk to return and make more boxing history as he plots huge 12 months of heavyweight mega-fights in the United States: 'My door is open'

Frank Warren is ready to cross the Atlantic on his tidal wave of thunderous world heavyweight title fights.

Having established Queensberry as the dominant boxing promoters in the UK, Warren is primed to pitch for big fights in the US. Not least in New York’s fabled Madison Square Garden.

This Saturday’s Slugfest II between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley at the O2 and December’s Battle of the Aged between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua in Cardiff - both for versions of the world championship - will be the prelude to a 2027 crammed with sell-out battles at sky-high prices.

They will involve the winners – and possibly the losers – of those fights, plus Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic, the Croatian iron man who beat him for one of the titles, and Agit Kabayel, who will shortly defend another of the belts in front of a 50,000 stadium crowd in Germany.

‘After 12 months putting on the big fights the fans love,’ says Warren, 'we are looking at a year chock-full of multiple heavyweight events involving all these guys and more.’

If Wardley gets revenge over Dubois by regaining his WBO title one of those happenings could be a trilogy match. Fury v Dubois is on the hob. As is the conquering of America., To which end Queensberry have signed Jared Anderson, the only heavyweight over there who looks remotely capable of coping in this company. Says Warren: ‘Jared will be a key part of our US expansion.’

Frank Warren is plotting a huge 12 months of heavyweight mega-fights in the USA next year

The promoter has invited Oleksandr Usyk to return and 'make even more boxing history'

That move will pitch Warren into a promotional rivalry with Dana White, the UFC boss whose new boxing company Zuffa has muscled into a share of the Fury-Joshua action – and a war of insults with AJ’s promoter Eddie Hearn.

Warren has watched those bitter exchanges with amused interest as well as reflections on his own disputes with Hearn down the years and says: ‘Nobody pays good money to watch promoters squabbling. The fans only have eyes for the men in the ring. I get on fine with Dana. Like me, he relishes competition.

'As far as Queensberry is concerned we are enjoying fabulous times the like of which has never been seen this side of the Atlantic.‘

Their heavyweight roster will be supplemented further by the return to action of popular Kiwi Joseph Parker from the positive drugs test which cost him a world title.

Most intriguingly of all, Warren is keeping tabs on Oleksandr Usyk. The Ukrainian genius who is the greatest boxer of two generations vacated all his undisputed heavyweight titles ‘to give the new generation their chance.’

But he has never triggered the retirement which would have had him join Rocky Marciano as the only heavyweights to hang up the gloves undefeated. Instead he has been keeping active in crossover combat while reviewing other options. Such as returning to the squared ring, in which he defeated Joshua, Fury and Dubois twice each.

‘If Oleksandr wants to make even more boxing history, ’ says Warren, ‘then Queensberry is the only place for him to come. The door to all our heavyweights is not just open. It’s off its hinges.’

The return of the Cat of Kyiv would be one of Uncle Frank’s greatest coups.

Sports.title: Man City appeal verdict 'expected early next year' - as Andy Burnham faces questions over 'freebies from Abu Dhabi deleted from public record'
Sports.content:
Manchester City's appeal into their Premier League guilty verdict is expected to be heard by mid-January, according to the head of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR). City were found guilty of all their alleged serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018 by an independent commission. They were found to have made 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies in the biggest cheating scandal in British sporting history. The IFR could force owner Sheikh Mansour to sell the club, or bar any personnel from being owners or directors, once the appeal process is complete. IFR chief David Kogan told Times Radio: 'The Premier League have said that they want to get this resolved within the season and actually, of course, it's not the Premier League, it's an independent commission that's going to hear this, made of three retired either judges or lawyers. 'My understanding is there is a prescribed process, which is 12 weeks, and so people are assuming this will actually be heard by the middle or the end of January. But as I say, it's not our process, it's that of the Premier League's independent commission. What I don't think we can do is take any judgment until we're quite clear. Manchester City's appeal into their Premier League guilty verdict is expected to be heard by mid-January Andy Burnham, then Greater Manchester mayor, pictured with Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in 2019

Your browser does not support iframes.

'Obviously, City claim that they have some form of silver bullet to put off these charges and win the appeal, and we're not there to judge whether that's right or wrong yet, but I think we'll know in the early part of next year.' Kogan threatened to resign from his role if there is any political interference in the IFR dealing with the saga. The IFR was created in September 2025 and was given the task of protecting and promoting the sustainability of English football. But Andy Burnham has had to defend himself after being accused of 'covering up' links to Manchester City following a register of interests being 'deleted'. Kogan added: 'The prime minister is capable of saying whatever he wants to say. You asked me whether we have had any interference politically in any of the judgments we're making, and I'm telling you, categorically, we have not. 'We will take a judgment based on evidence, once the appeal has been heard by the independent commission of the Premier League, we're going to look at that evidence closely, we're going to actually have powers of investigation ourselves, and that will be what governs what we do.' City could face expulsion from the Premier League, a fine, a points deduction, and even having their trophies stripped. But Prime Minister Burnham came out in support of the crisis-stricken club's Abu Dhabi owners... before backtracking and vowing to release all material from his dealings with them. Independent Football Regulator chief David Kogan says he will resign if there is any political interference Mr Burnham previously claimed to have had just one formal meeting with City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. But he now stands accused of misleading the public after a deleted register of interest showed he joined Al Mubarak twice in a luxury box at City's Etihad Stadium, while he also accepted tickets to an Ed Sheeran concert, according to the BBC . Mr Burnham accepted City-funded freebies worth nearly £1,200 which appeared on a register of interests that he signed in December 2020 during his time as Manchester mayor and was later taken down from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA)'s website, they report. On April 18, 2020, the register shows a value of £699 given to 'dinner with the Chairman at Man City/ Man United derby at the Etihad.' And later that year on August 17, the entry reads: 'Dinner with Richard Leese and Chair of Man City for the Everton match at the Etihad.' The match ticket value is given as £38, while the hospitality is listed at £300. At PMQs on Wednesday afternoon, Mr Burnham was asked: 'Did anyone associated with the running of Manchester City raise the charges they were facing and have now been found guilty of, either with him or any member of his team?' The Prime Minister replied: 'They did not raise those issues with me. I'm very happy for everything to be set out in full, it is why I asked the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, in response to a call from the leader of the opposition and others to set out a full statement of my key dealings with the owners of Manchester City Football Club. 'That statement was published on Monday and it includes the issues in the news today and that is the position.' GMCA has not yet responded to Daily Mail Sport's request for comment. According to the BBC, it is the GMCA's policy to only publish entries from the current mayoral term. The details of Mr Burnham's contacts with City during his time as mayor were released by GMCA on Monday. They revealed the Prime Minister had a formal meeting with Al Mubarak at an investment summit in October 2021 while he was Greater Manchester mayor. He also chatted to Al Mubarak in the stands during a testimonial game in 2019 and was accompanied by City staff on official overseas visits to China and Japan.

Your browser does not support iframes.

But the deleted register of interests shows he was in a hospitality suite at the Etihad with Al Mubarak for a game against Everton and also the Manchester derby. Burnham had previously said on The Rest is Politics podcast: 'I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester. 'None of it is recent, in terms of meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting and that was in 2021. That is right and I will put that all out there.' The new revelation will only intensify scrutiny over the Prime Minister's relationship with City's Abu Dhabi owners, who maintain their innocence and are appealing the independent commission's verdict. The Guardian also reported on Wednesday that a club representative from City was invited on a government-backed trade delegation to India this week. Bev Craig, who replaced Burnham as Manchester mayor, took a representative from the club to Delhi and Mumbai on a trip organised by business secretary Jonathan Reynolds. Mrs Craig defended the decision, telling the newspaper it had played a key role in helping build infrastructure in her city. 'If a football club has broken the rules, a football club should be punished for breaking the rules, and that is pretty clear in an independent process,' she said. 'I think what can also be true at the same time though, if you ask residents in east Manchester, have they benefited from a new library, a new leisure centre, a new sixth-form college, infrastructure investment, the job opportunities that come from them being a good employment charter signee and an early adopter of the real living wage – then they will have felt that benefit.'

Sports.title: Teammates accuse British cycling's axed golden boy Matthew Richardson of having a 'God complex' - as his girlfriend ignores drama to win silver medal at the World Championships in his absence
Sports.content:
British Cycling's golden boy Matthew Richardson has been accused of having a 'God complex' after being axed from the team following allegations of using racist language.

Richardson, 27, was sent home from the Cycling World Championships on Monday with the 'misconduct' probe over his behaviour still ongoing, while his 23-year-old cyclist girlfriend Emma Finucane remains at the competition in Shanghai and raced to a silver medal in the Women's Team Sprint on Wednesday morning.

Finucane put on a brave face, smiling with her teammates Sophie Capewell and Rhianna Parris-Smith on the podium after losing gold to China.

Richardson has been accused of using racist and discriminatory language towards others, according to The Times, who also report that riders in the World Class Programme described him as 'arrogant' and having a 'God complex'.

'At the velodrome he’s the golden boy,' they added. 'Matty is one of their best chances of a gold medal in LA and he knows it.'

British Cycling began investigating Richardson after a formal complaint was made, it is understood.

The Olympic medallist broke his silence on Tuesday, writing on Instagram that he was 'deeply disappointed' and would co-operate with Team GB, who he joined after leaving the Australian programme.

Matthew Richardson is not competing at the World Championships amid the ongoing misconduct probe but his girlfriend Emma Finucane remains

Sophie Capewell (left), Finucane (centre) and Rhianna Parris-Smith are pictured with their silver medals on Wednesday after coming second in the Women's Team Pursuit

He said: 'I understand the seriousness of what has been raised in recent reports about my withdrawal from the 2026 UCI Track Cycling World Championships.

'British Cycling has said it looks into matters like this through its established procedures. I will co-operate fully with its processes. I assure everyone that I will do so properly, and appropriately and with contrition for the feelings of anyone who might be affected.

'Out of fairness to everyone involved, and on advice, like British Cycling, I will not be commenting further until any process is complete. I am deeply disappointed to miss the World Championships, and I wish the Great Britain team and every rider competing the very best.'

Richardson's exit sent shockwaves through the sport, while his girlfriend Finucane welcomed her parents to Shanghai ahead of the competition on Monday.

Her brother, Sean, 21, told the Daily Mail of his family's 'shock and surprise' at the latest development.

He said: ‘We are all pretty shocked and surprised - he’s a lovely guy. He’s been here a lot and never shown any signs of that sort of behaviour. My parents flew out to Shanghai yesterday - none of us knew.'

Emma, who won four gold medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, competes in the Individual Sprint, Team Sprint and Keirin. Ultimately it was China who took gold in the Team Sprint, with Finucane and Co settling for silver and Germany taking bronze on Wednesday.

In a statement sent to Daily Mail Sport, a British Cycling spokesman said: 'British Cycling can confirm that Matt Richardson has been withdrawn from the Great Britain Cycling Team squad for the upcoming 2026 Tissot UCI Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai, China.'

Richardson has been described as having a 'God complex' and being 'arrogant'

When approached by Daily Mail Sport about the misconduct allegations which are believed to have prompted Richardson's withdrawal, the organisation added that they would not be commenting further at this stage.

Richardson and Finucane live together in Manchester and have been dating since February 2024 after 'knowing each other for a long time'.

Richardson had been due to be one of four members of the men's sprint squad at the World Championships.

He had been due to join Harry Ledingham-Horn, Ed Lowe and Joe Truman in the squad.

Richardson had claimed three medals at the European Championships in Konya, Turkey, earlier this year.

The 27-year-old won gold in both the men's sprint and keirin events, as well as claiming silver in the team sprint with Truman and Hamish Turnbull.

Richardson had been due to make his comeback after he was injured during the Keirin World Series in July.

Richardson's partner is fellow British cyclist Emma Finucane, who welcomed her parents out in China amid the storm engulfing her boyfriend

Last week, Richardson said he is 'lucky' to be walking after being wiped out by a rival in an incident, which ruled him out of the Commonwealth Games three months ago.

Richardson had been slammed off the track by Japanese cyclist Kento Suzuki while competing in the event in July, leaving the velodrome in an ambulance.

The sprinter said he has not received an apology from Suzuki over the incident.

He was favourite to win gold in Glasgow but never got to take part after the horrifying crash. He was unable to walk for four days after coming away with a broken scapula and a heavily bruised hip.

Richardson had been hoping to defend the title he won when competing for Australia in 2022, before he switched nationality to represent Britain, which he claimed was like 'Hogwarts' compared to 'High School'.

The defector, who was born in the English town of Maidstone but moved to Perth at nine and went on to carve out a brilliant track career for Australia, caused a sensation by switching allegiance straight after winning two silvers and a bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics. He received a life ban from competing for Australia.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola's Man City U-turn over return plan as talks scheduled
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola's Man City U-turn over return plan as talks scheduled

Former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola will be back at Etihad Stadium just a few months on from departing the club

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola made the decision to come back to Manchester City to show a united front after their financial charges guilty verdict (Image: (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP via Getty Images) )

Pep Guardiola hadn’t planned to return to Manchester City so soon - but decided to come back due to his belief in the club's innocence over 114 financial charges. Just a few months on from leaving his role as manager, Guardiola is set to be at Etihad Stadium for City's Champions League clash against Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday.

‌



‌



In late September, the Premier League confirmed that City had been found in breach of all financial charges by an independent panel.

‌



An appeal has been lodged against the outcome with City continuing to protest their innocence. That stance was reiterated by Guardiola in a message on social media in the wake of their guilty verdict.

‌



That read: "I want every single @ManCity fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters. Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



And now Guardiola will be showing his support in person by flying into Manchester on Wednesday before watching City vs PSG in the directors’ box alongside chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak, as per The Sun. Talks with the latter and CEO Ferran Soriano will take place first.

They have also claimed that Guardiola had no plans to return to City so soon after departing but given what has happened since his exit, the 55-year-old is determined to stand by his former employers due to his unwavering belief in their innocence.

This will be City's first home match since the verdict and it arguably could not be against a better opponent with 2025 and 2026 Champions League holders PSG in town.

‌



View 2 Images Khaldoon Al Mubarak is set to meet with Pep Guardiola before the PSG clash

City beat Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday to keep their 100 per cent winning record intact with the players overcoming a hostile atmosphere inside Anfield. City captain Ruben Dias was quick to praise such an achievement while insisting that the players remain focused.

He said: "It's a win at Anfield. In whatever circumstance, so be it now maybe earlier in the season, so be it later in the season, any time - I and we will enjoy it just as much, and we will celebrate it however it feels in the moment, and it will obviously be a show of how much it means to us.

‌



"Yes, there's a lot of noise, and it's almost impossible to avoid seeing something - even us, being as private as we can be, and doing just our own lives. On your phone it's impossible to avoid everything.

"But I feel like we're all so very good at focussing ourselves on our job, doing it right, making the most of it, being happy every time we come to work, and our minds are very much there, and only there.

"It's the things we can control, the things we've always been doing, and enjoying so much. We have full confidence on the club, we trust the club, and we love to win!"

Sports.title: The star of the post-match interview and why it's wrong to slam players for speaking out
Sports.content:
There is a real art to a post-match interview.

And Gabriel Clarke is a master of his craft. Of course Lisandro Martinez was ready and willing with his words and message to the Manchester United hierarchy.

It was an incredibly powerful interview with Martinez saying he “expects more from the top” to deliver “more players to compete.” It could not have been more clear. He lambasted United’s lack of ambition.

And it has got us all talking. I cannot believe there are some people in the media - largely ex-players but staggeringly not all - actually questioning whether he should have spoken out.

‌



Honestly, remember you are part of the media now. That’s absolutely fine to think like that. But, come on, remember what world you are in.

Martinez was fascinating. As Clarke was winding up his interview on Amazon Prime, Martinez stepped back in just to make sure.

“Tonight it’s easy to say the coach, easy to say the players, but we also have to see the others, eh,” he said. Does anyone really disagree? Manchester United are in a sorry state.

What makes Clarke so good - and he has been doing this for years for ITV and now Amazon as well as being a first-class documentary film maker - is that he listens to the answers, spots the “line” and asks great questions.

‌



View 6 Images Lisandro Martinez took aim at the Manchester United board in a bombshell interview (Image: Amazon Prime Video)

So many don’t listen and fail to follow up. It’s the most common mistake. Even I get frustrated when people in our industry talk about “the quotes” as if they magically appear. The best answers come from good questions.

We are all talking about Martinez today because it was such a good interview. And, let’s be clear, there are some really good post-match interviewers out there. It’s a really good standard at the moment, in my opinion. The best all listen, all let the interviewee talk and are well prepared.

This was not your typical post-match interview. Far from it. Clubs are contractually obliged to put forward the manager and players as part of their TV contracts both in the Champions League and Premier League.

‌



Some of the demands are staggering. Huge numbers of interviews, same questions and same answers. There is the main post-match press conference and the TV interviews are often conducted in what is known as the flash area.

Players also walk through the mixed zone area where more post-match interviews are conducted with TV, rights-holders, non rights-holders and written media.

View 6 Images Mohamed Salah's mixed zone interview in 2025 went viral around the world (Image: Viaplay)

It can obviously sometimes be a bit of nightmare for press officers who often accompany players through the mixed zone areas (not always, I hasten to add) when they go off script. Press officers rarely step in, to be fair.

‌



Down the years, there have been some memorable stand-offs. One former England player getting so wound up with one journalist, the stand-up row quickly escalated further…

The time England players initiated a media boycott in Poland in September 2004 because they thought the criticism was over the top. They made a point of refusing to speak in the mixed zone. There were some pretty high-profile media pundits in that squad…

Only last season, former Liverpool star Mo Salah, accused the club of “throwing him under the bus.” It was a blockbuster interview which went round the globe.

It doesn’t happen if journos are not there, by the way. It was filmed, a press officer was behind and, quite understandably, looked a bit concerned.

‌



Way too much was made of that. What else do you expect him to do? It is obvious that he might want to alert colleagues as the manager or other players may be asked about what Salah said. Liverpool’s press operation is very good.

Should Man Utd punish Lisandro Martinez for comments on owners? Have your say READ MORE :

I will always remember Patrick Vieira speaking out after Arsenal crashed out of the Champions League in Valencia. From memory, there was only two of us, me and a great journalist, David Woods, and Vieira clearly had something to say.

“We have to finish second in the Premiership to secure our place in the Champions League next season," Vieira said. "We also have to win the Cup. That is the minimum to so when you wear the Arsenal shirt.

“But I have to be honest, even if we manage to reach these two objectives, I would qualify our season as average. In the championship we are 15 or 20 points adrift Manchester United, so for me it's really a season to be forgotten.”

‌



Roy Keane to MUTV was a cracker. The in-house channel! Obviously it leaked out. Keane has delivered quite a few down the years. Thierry Henry was a brilliant talker.

View 6 Images Harry Kane is always willing to speak to the media

Harry Kane is so prolific in the mixed zone. He takes his duties as England captain so seriously. So does Virgil van Dijk. They don’t have to speak - but they willingly do it. There is so much respect for them.

Football is more high profile than other sports. It is pretty common - more so in the Premier League - not to get anyone stopping.

‌



It’s a different set-up in the Champions League where the mixed zone is a bigger part of the event and players are supposed to always walk through (many still don’t).

In other sports, it’s definitely expected. I will always remember covering athletics and Christine Ohuruogu came through the mixed zone. She had won a medal soon after being banned for missing three drugs test.

View 6 Images The world's media descend on Lionel Messi at the World Cup

You have to ask about that. It’s relevant and is part of the story. Of course it is. We’re not cheerleaders. Athletics used to be terrible for having ex-athletes who were just cheerleaders. That’s fine - but get a ticket in the stand.

‌



Another journalist and a former athlete interrupted the interview with their harrumphing and complaints. Honestly, get another job.

Sadly, that’s why using former players or athletes for interviews does not always work. Contrast Gabriel Clarke’s post-match interview to Peter Schmeichel’s with Martinez and the ex-Manchester United keeper’s chat with Martinez feels pretty uncomfortable.

By the end, Schmeichel is even trying to talk down Martinez for being critical. “Nothing is won in October,” says Schmeichel. In fairness, the great Dane can be a pretty good pundit but this was not the time or the place. He was protecting United like he used to between the posts.

View 6 Images Thomas Tuchel sparred with Clarke following England's win over Norway. (Image: ITV Football)

‌



You cannot say that for all ex-players. It’s up to the TV companies what they do and who they use. Jan Aage Fjortoft often does very good and searching interviews. Sky and TNT often get decent stuff when former players analyse games with the manager or players. It’s different.

I really didn’t like the pile-on against Gabriel Clarke during the World Cup when he was tough with Thomas Tuchel after England’s gruelling game with Norway. Clarke never seeks the limelight. That's refreshing in itself. I don't like it when interviewers try to make themselves the story. That's just personal preference.

Clearly, fans might not have liked that World Cup interview, the England manager might not have liked it, but for other media outlets to try and make mileage out of it was disappointing. It’s good that after the Martinez interview, he is rightly getting the praise he deserves.

Sports.title: Man Utd identify Premier League boss as 'standout candidate' to replace Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Man Utd identify Premier League boss as 'standout candidate' to replace Michael Carrick

Michael Carrick is under increasing pressure following a disappointing start to the 2026/27 campaign, having managed just one Premier League win

View 2 Images The Manchester United hierarchy are believed to be admirers of Fabian Hurzeler

Manchester United have reportedly identified Fabian Hurzeler as their preferred candidate to replace Michael Carrick should they decide to make a change in the dugout. Carrick, who only signed a permanent contract in the summer, has come under increasing pressure in recent weeks with United managing just one win in their last six Premier League matches.

‌



‌



After guiding the club to a third-place finish last season, the United hierarchy placed considerable faith in Carrick. However, the early stages of the 2026/27 campaign have failed to deliver a repeat of that form, with the Red Devils currently sitting 13th in the Premier League table.

‌



As a result, questions are beginning to emerge over Carrick's long-term future at Old Trafford, particularly given the club's history of dismissing head coaches during the season. Erik ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, while his successor, Ruben Amorim, was dismissed at the start of 2026.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Despite the growing scrutiny, United are expected to give Carrick more time to turn things around before making any major decisions. However, the club's hierarchy will be looking for an improvement in results over the coming weeks, with October and early November potentially proving pivotal to their season.

According to The Sun, the United board are monitoring the situation closely and regard Hurzeler as their 'standout' candidate should they decide to replace Carrick. The Brighton boss was identified as a potential future United manager last year, alongside Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner.

‌



Iraola succeeded Arne Slot in the summer, while Glasner took charge of Nottingham Forest after leaving Crystal Palace. United ultimately opted to stick with Carrick after he secured Champions League qualification, but his position could come under further scrutiny if results continue to disappoint.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is under pressure at Man United

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Hurzeler, meanwhile, committed his future to Brighton by signing a new three-year contract in June. The Seagulls would therefore be in a strong position to demand a substantial compensation fee should United make an approach.

Brighton owner Tony Bloom warned last month that the club was 'prepared for any eventuality' if another side expressed an interest in appointing the German.

Since taking charge in 2024, Hurzeler has guided Brighton to four wins in six meetings with United, while leading the Seagulls to consecutive eighth-place finishes in the Premier League.

‌



Antonio Conte is another potential option for United, with the Italian currently out of work and potentially open to a return to English football.

The former Chelsea and Tottenham manager last took charge of a Premier League match in 2023, during his spell at Spurs. United have also monitored Kieran McKenna and Eddie Howe as possible managerial options.

Sports.title: Arsenal outline plans to make 60 staff members redundant despite record revenue
Sports.content:
Arsenal outline plans to make 60 staff members redundant despite record revenue

Arsenal have told staff that they plan to make 60 of them redundant despite the announcement of record revenue and a lucrative new contract for Mikel Arteta

View 2 Images Arsenal have confirmed they've began a process of redundancies (Image: 2026 Vince Mignott/MB Media)

Arsenal have made staff aware that they plan to make 60 individuals redundant despite announcing record revenues for 2024/25.

‌



‌



The Premier League winners, who are still revelling in their title of English champions, have told employees they will make make 60 positions redundant, with cuts set to be across a number of departments.

‌



Among the departments that are unaffected is the coaching group, as well as the performance teams for both the men's and women's sides. Those involved in the academy, the club’s community operation, the Arsenal Foundation, security personnel and workers dedicated to the women’s setup are also not part of the redundancy process, reports the Athletic.

‌



A consultation is underway and the decision could yet change, but the announcement comes despite Arsenal having an encouraging set of financial results for the season before last.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The Gunners announced they had almost broken even for the 2024/25 financial year, recording an overall loss of £1.4million, while posting record revenues of £691m. Among Arsenal's biggest revenue wins was their decision to sell the naming rights to their training ground to Sobha Realty in February 2024 – a deal which significantly contributed to the club’s revenues.

The announcement to make a raft of redundancies also comes after a new lucrative deal for manager Mikel Arteta, who recently committed his future to the club until 2030 after finally delivering the title.

The Spaniard’s new deal is believed to have made him the best-paid coach in the Premier League, but the loss of staff in light of such news is unlikely to be well received by supporters.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal enjoyed a huge commercial boost when they sold off the naming rights to their training ground

It also comes after the club spent £150m to land Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa in the summer. The trio further bolstering a squad that is seen as one of the best in Europe following continued investment.

Arsenal are not the only club to cut jobs in recent years. Manchester United's decision to rid of several jobs was well publicised and resulted in heavy backlash. Sir Jim Ratcliffe was behind the decision as he desperately sought to cut costs and was adamant that the moves were necessary to prevent the club going bust.

Sports.title: Wolves fan who 'mocked A66 crash' at Middlesborough game banned from football including Euro 2028
Sports.content:
Wolves fan who 'mocked A66 crash' at Middlesborough game banned from football including Euro 2028

Bradley Aston pleaded guilty to a public order offence after footage was posted on social media of him smiling and holding up a mobile phone towards Middlesbrough fans

View 3 Images Bradley Aston pleaded guilty to a public order offence after footage was posted on social media of him smiling and holding up a mobile phone towards Middlesbrough fans. The message "Police Killed Your Own" was clearly visible (Image: x)

A "vile" Wolves fan who mocked the seven people killed in the A66 tragedy has been banned from football for four years.

‌



‌



A court heard Bradley Aston would have gone to prison before a change in the sentencing guidelines. Aston pleaded guilty to a public order offence after footage was posted on social media of him smiling and holding up a mobile phone towards Middlesbrough fans.

‌



The message "Police Killed Your Own" was clearly visible on the screen.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Bradley Aston pleaded guilty to a public order offence after footage was posted on social media of him smiling and holding up a mobile phone towards Middlesbrough fans. The message "Police Killed Your Own" was clearly visible (Image: x)

Student Aston, 20, was arrested at the end of Middlesbrough's 1-0 win over Wolves at the Riverside Stadium on Saturday. He received an eight-week jail term suspended for a year. But he was told by magistrates in Wolverhampton that he would have been jailed were it not for recent changes to sentencing rules.

‌



Two police officers, PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died when a VW Passat car travelling the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into a force vehicle. All five occupants of the Passat, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, Jakub Matusiak, 23 and Michael Robert Cahill, 23, also died at the scene.

Cleveland Police's chief constable condemned Aston's "vile" actions for causing distress and anger among her workforce, the wider community and to officers' families. She said some of her staff may not be able to return to work. In a statement read to the court, she said: " My officers have faced an unprecedented level of trauma that will stay with them forever. To see such a vile message has created feelings of grief, anger and dismay."

View 3 Images Riverside Stadium, home of Middlesbrough (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



Aston, from the Coalpool area of Walsall, was kept in custody for his own safety after the footage was posted on social media, the court heard. Deputy district judge Steven Jonas said: "This was unbelievably serious and prior to the passing of the Sentencing Act 2026, there is no doubt in my view that you would be going directly to custody today.

"The words that you used were intended to cause not just maximum offence but, as importantly as that, they were intended to provoke a response. That could have resulted in a substantial disorder. Not only have you offended a vast number of people, you deliberately ran the risk of causing a substantial violent reaction."

The court heard Aston was now considering withdrawing from a sport performance analysis course. Accepting that the offence he admitted would have an impact on his proposed career, Jonas told him he would not impose the maximum football banning order of five years.

‌



"You are remorseful and most importantly you are only 20 years old," he said. The deputy district judge said there had been an element of planning to the showing of the message on the Snapchat app, and the offence was aggravated by being committed against those working to protect the public.

Defence solicitor Askara Rana said Aston was embarrassed at his actions and acted without thinking. She said: "Not only has he let himself down, he has let his family down, as well as the wider community."

Aston’s mother was in court to view the proceedings, Ms Rana said. The defence solicitor told the hearing: “Not only has he let himself down, he has let his family down, as well as the wider community.”

Article continues below

The defendant is in the second year of his university course, the court heard, and the conviction could have an impact on his future aspirations. Aston, who also works as a driver, was also ordered to pay a £154 victim surcharge and £85 in costs

The second-year university student was banned from going within three miles of Molineux before, during and after home games, as well as being banned from other grounds and matches at Euro 2028 and ordered to carry out community work.

Sports.title: 'I was in English ninth tier three years ago – now I'm eyeing Champions League debut'
Sports.content:
'I was in English ninth tier three years ago – now I'm eyeing Champions League debut'

A former non-league star could be set to make his Champions League debut

View 2 Images A former non-league star has since joined a Champions League club (Image: Nathan Zentveld - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Manasse Kianga could make his Champions League debut on Wednesday, just three years after playing in the ninth tier of English football. He is part of Slovan Bratislava’s squad as the Slovakian club prepare to take on Stuttgart in Europe’s top club cup competition.

‌



‌



The 24-year-old striker has been on a remarkable journey in a short space of time following his starring role for non-league side Rossington Main. Kianga helped the Doncaster side earn promotion to the ninth tier in the 2022/23 season and he is now managed by Manchester City legend Yaya Toure.

‌



It is worlds apart from when the South African moved to Rotherham around 2017. During his early days with Rossington, Kianga studied business and accounting at Thomas Rotherham College and also featured for Team Sport in the Rotherham and District Sunday Football League.

‌



He was ultimately forced to move back to South Africa in 2024 after failing to secure a permanent work permit. However, Kianga has since found success abroad and could make his Champions League bow with Bratislava after being promoted from the club’s reserves.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The striker came off the bench to score for Toure’s side during Champions League qualifying, helping the Slovakian champions overcome Swedish outfit Mjallby and earn a place in the league phase. Kianga missed out on a spot in the matchday squad when Bratislava faced reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain in their opening game but will hope to fulfil his aim against Stuttgart.

‌



Recalling the forward’s non-league journey, Rossington boss Ben Hunter recalled to BBC South Yorkshire: "He came to trial with Rossington and I had a look at him and straight away loved him. He was a really great guy as well and always played with a smile on his face."

“You could see his ability in terms of his speed and physical presence, but he was quite slight,” Hunter added. “He stayed with us and he did really well - a lot of higher up teams were interested in him.”

View 2 Images Manasse Kianga will aim to make his Champions League debut for Slovan Bratislava (Image: Nathan Zentveld - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Kianga played alongside former Bradford City and Grimsby Town striker Ross Hannah, who said of his old strike partner: “Me and him were a real problem for defenders and teams because of the way we complemented each other. It's amazing the journey he has been on.”

The versatile attacker previously joined Lokomotiva Kosice in the Slovakian third tier before heading to Bratislava earlier this year. After starring for their reserves, Kianga initially flourished under new boss Toure, registering two goals and assists apiece in the team’s first three league games.

‌



The forward has since dropped to the bench but will hope to make his mark in the club’s remaining Champions League fixtures, starting with their home match against Stuttgart on Wednesday. Bratislava will also host Real Betis, Shakhtar Donetsk and Inter Milan during the league phase, with away trips to Roma, LASK and Lille also on the horizon.

Rossington boss Hunter was among those who travelled to a Bradford court to support Kianga’s efforts to get a work permit and reflected on how the striker reacted to his setback. “The world was his oyster, I really believed he could have made it pro in England,” his former manager said. “He went back to South Africa and from there made a journey across Europe and ended up where he is.”
