World.title: Bangladesh arrests two for luring locals to fight for Russia in Ukraine
World.content:
Twenty Bangladeshi victims have been killed after being used by Russia as ‘bait’ to locate enemy positions, police say.

Share Bangladesh arrests two for luring locals to fight for Russia in Ukraine on social media

Police in Bangladesh have arrested two people they say are linked to a trafficking network that deceptively recruited locals to fight for Russia in Ukraine.

The suspects, identified as Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher, trafficked at least 30 people to Russia with false promises of high-paying jobs, Mohammad Asaduzzaman, commander of the elite police force Special Response Battalion, said on Wednesday.

Once abroad, the victims’ passports and phones were taken, and they were handed over to the Russian military, he said.

Seventeen of the trafficking victims, who arrived in Russia in early May, were killed on the first day of deployment after being given minimal training, Asaduzzaman said. A total of 20 Bangladeshis have been confirmed dead.

“Bangladeshis were used as bait to locate enemy positions,” he said. “Russian forces determined their next course of action after the Bangladeshis fell victim to drone attacks.”

In addition to the 20 Bangladeshis killed, two more are being treated in a Moscow hospital while six others are still on the battlefield, police cited a survivor who was injured and managed to return home as saying.

The victims were from poor backgrounds and had paid around $8,000 for the fake jobs that brought them to Russia, Bangladeshi media reported.

Both Russia and Ukraine have recruited thousands of foreign nationals into their armies since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago.

An estimated 28,000 foreigners from 136 countries are said to be fighting in the Russian army, and officials believe Moscow deployed some 14,000 North Korean troops to battle Ukraine’s 2024 incursion into the Kursk region.



Meanwhile, Ukraine says 16,000 foreign nationals from more than 70 countries – including nearly 40 percent from Latin America – are currently serving in its army.

Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly last month, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia deceptively recruits people from 47 countries for an “absolutely brutal” campaign and urged countries not to let Moscow “drag” them into the war.

Amnesty International has also accused Russia of using “deceptive, coercive and exploitative practices” to recruit foreigners to fight on the Ukrainian front.

Russia has previously dismissed accusations of coercing foreigners into joining its army.

Amnesty says it cannot conduct inquiries about foreigners in Ukraine’s army as it has no access to prisoners of war held in Russia, which designates the rights group as a “foreign agent”.

World.title: Israel’s former security chief sues Netanyahu for October 7 defamation
World.content:
Ronen Bar accuses Netanyahu of being warned before Hamas attacks, as elections loom.

The former head of Israel’s domestic security agency Shin Bet has sued Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for defamation over claims of his responsibility in the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack.

Coming just before Israel’s close-fought October 27 election in which Netanyahu is fighting for his political life, the case filed on Wednesday is set to ramp up the country’s political drama.

Ronen Bar, the former director of Shin Bet, accused Netanyahu of “lying to cover himself” and said it was slanderous of the prime minister to have accused him of “criminal failures” over the attack, in a 134-page court document.

Bar said he telephoned the prime minister’s military secretary as soon as signs of a possible attack became apparent, but that he did not have Netanyahu’s direct number.

Netanyahu has said he was not alerted by Bar on the morning of the Hamas-led assault, insisting that he could have stopped the attack had the Shin Bet’s then-director or military leaders called to wake him up the day of the early-morning attack.

Bar’s lawsuit says Netanyahu made accusations “that he knew to be false, with the aim of diverting the debate from his own responsibility for the events of October 7”.

Instead, it was Netanyahu’s policies over several years that had “increased the dangers posed by terrorist organisations in Gaza”, it said.

Likud response

On Wednesday, Netanyahu responded to Bar’s accusations in a statement issued by his Likud party saying, “Ronen, are you serious?”

“You had my number on the red line and could have called me immediately, as all security chiefs do,” Netanyahu asked, adding, “How many lives could we have saved if only you had called in time?”



Bar resigned as head of Shin Bet in June 2025 amid recriminations over the deadliest attack in Israel’s history, while insisting he had informed Netanyahu of the threat in advance.

He is seeking three million shekels (about $968,500) in damages from Netanyahu.

Warnings, lies, manipulation

The allegations in Bar’s lawsuit come days after Netanyahu’s former military secretary, Avi Gil, told Israel’s Channel 12 that the prime minister’s office had “falsified records related to October 7, 2023”, including altering the recorded time of a key phone call.

Gil, who served as Netanyahu’s military secretary from July 2021 to May 2024, said a stenographer in the prime minister’s office approached him in January 2024 with instructions from Netanyahu’s chief of staff to change the time of a four-minute call from 6:40am local time (03:40GMT) to 6:29am (03:29 GMT).

“She told me, I’m not allowed to change it,” said Gil, accusing the head of Netanyahu’s office of manipulating telephone records, adding, “Those are facts, and there is no dispute about them.”

Last month, the Wall Street Journal reported that Netanyahu had been warned of the attack by Egypt’s intelligence chief, Abbas Kamel.

In a rare move, Kamel reportedly phoned the prime minister just days before the attack, underscoring previous warnings in September 2023, when he is said to have flown to Israel to warn security officials in person that Hamas was planning an attack.

Polls show Netanyahu is in a tight race to stay in power in the October 27 election, after being hammered by former staff and government officials as well as the opposition for failing to prevent the bloodshed.

At least 1,221 Israelis were killed on October 7, 2023, after Hamas broke through the fence separating Israel and Gaza, according to Israeli official figures.

Also, 251 Israelis were taken captive, including the bodies of 44 Israelis killed that day.

In the three years since, Israel has killed more than 74,300 people in Gaza, according to the Health Ministry in the enclave.

More than 1,400 Palestinians in Gaza have been killed in Israeli attacks since a tentative “ceasefire” backed by the US was reached last year.

World.title: Real Madrid’s Vinicius banned for Clasico after hair-pull red card
World.content:
Vinicius will miss El Clasico on October 25, the first of his four-match ban for pulling Saliba’s hair in La Liga.

Real Madrid’s Vinicius Junior will miss the upcoming match against Barcelona in the Spanish league after being issued a four-match suspension for pulling an opponent’s hair during a La Liga game last week.

The Brazilian forward will miss Madrid’s next four league fixtures, including the highly anticipated October 25 El Clasico against fierce rivals and league champions Barcelona.

The Spanish federation’s disciplinary committee announced the ban on Wednesday after Vinicius received the red card against Villarreal last week.

The number seven thought he had scored Real’s second goal in the match on Saturday, but his effort was disallowed after a video assistant referee (VAR) review found he should be dismissed for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in the build-up.

The Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee confirmed the Brazilian will be banned for several matches, including the visit to face league leaders Barca, because of both the red card and his subsequent protests.

After the match, Vinicius, ⁠⁠⁠⁠who came on in the ⁠⁠⁠⁠52nd minute and was red-carded 20 minutes later, posted on social media, saying, “sorry to the team and the ⁠⁠⁠⁠fans”.

Vinicius was celebrating after scoring when referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called by the VAR to review the moments before his goal. The referee waved off the goal and pulled out a red card for Vinicius, who also goes by his nickname Vini Jr.

When he thought Vinicius had doubled the lead, Real manager Jose Mourinho ran to join the celebrations with his players.



But moments later, Vinicius was left livid by the referee’s decision. He screamed at Diaz de Mera while his teammates tried to calm him down as he left the field.

World.title: How six Ukrainian divers could have blown up Russia’s $20bn pipelines
World.content:
How six Ukrainian divers could have blown up Russia’s $20bn pipelines

How six Ukrainian divers could have blown up Russia’s $20bn pipelines

A Ukrainian military officer is on trial in Germany over an act of sabotage that remained unsolved for years. Serhii Kuznetsov is accused of leading a six-person diving squad to blow up the Nord Stream pipelines in 2022, severing an energy lifeline that connected Russia to Europe. Watch the full episode of Pinch Point on our YouTube channel.

World.title: Ex-UK army chef jailed for ‘terror’-related offence
World.content:
The former British Army member harboured ‘extreme right-wing’ views and was ordering explosives components, say police.

A British court has handed a former army chef a nearly four-year jail term for possessing weapons for “terrorist purposes”.

Mark Broadhurst, 28, was given the sentence on Wednesday at Sheffield Crown Court in England, two years after police uncovered online messages in which he expressed racist views and an intention to sell homemade firearms to right-wing groups.

Police found a stockpile of weapons at Broadhurst’s home address when they took him into custody in September 2024, including knives and crossbows, black powder, ammunition, air pistols and what officials described as “an improvised homemade cannon”.

The former British Army member was also found to be part of an online chat group with three other men who last year were jailed for planning to carry out a “terrorist” attack at mosques or synagogues as part of what they believed to be a coming “race war”.

Frank Ferguson, head of the special crime division of the UK’s public prosecution agency, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said Broadhurst was “clearly interested in violence and developing weapons that had the ability to cause untold harm to innocent people”.

Detective Chief Superintendent James Dunkerley, who heads “counterterror” policing in the northeastern region, said Broadhurst was found to be harbouring an “extreme right-wing mindset” and was “proactively ordering components to make explosives”.

Broadhurst pleaded guilty to firearm possession and possessing an explosive under suspicious circumstances, but denied they were for “terrorism” purposes. ⁠A judge, however, ruled that Broadhurst’s offences were connected to “terrorism”.



His conviction comes against a backdrop of rising racial tensions and hate crimes in the UK, with marginalised communities increasingly targeted.

British police in July arrested 12 people in connection with an “extreme right-wing terrorism threat” targeting an Islamic gathering in eastern England.

Six months earlier, UK prosecutors said they were handling the highest number of hate crime cases referred by police in its history.

World.title: Saudi tennis ‘slam’ with Alcaraz, Djokovic postponed amid Houthi attacks
World.content:
The Six Kings Slam exhibition tournament has been pushed from October to December by Saudi organisers.

An exhibition tennis tournament featuring the world’s top men’s players has been postponed for two months by the organisers in Saudi Arabia as the country reels from a spate of attacks by Yemen’s Houthis.

Turki al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority (GEA), said on Wednesday that the exhibition Six Kings Slam tennis tournament had been postponed due to “organisational and logistical challenges”.

The announcement came shortly after the Saudi Pro League postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr, for “logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches”.

The Six Kings Slam was due to hold its third edition later this month, with tennis stars including Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev due to take part alongside Taylor Fritz, Learner Tien and Alex de Minaur.

The event, originally scheduled for October 21-24 and to be streamed live by Netflix, will now take place from December 27-30.

“The Six Kings Slam tournament has been postponed due to logistical reasons and will now take place on December 27,” al-Sheikh said on X, sharing a statement from the Riyadh Season entertainment programme.

Earlier on Wednesday, the three SPL matches involving teams based in Saudi capital Riyadh were postponed.

The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.



The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures “will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes”.

The move comes two days after al-Sheikh promised that boxing’s world title fight featuring Saul “Canelo” ‌‌Alvarez and Christian M’billi will go ahead this month.

Alvarez vs M’billi is scheduled for October 31 in the Saudi capital, which has repeatedly come under attack from Yemen’s Houthis, but al-Sheikh sought to allay the doubts over the bout on Sunday.

“Canelo reached out ⁠⁠and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” al-Sheikh wrote in a social media post. “He [Alvarez] fears nothing.”

On Monday, Al-Nassr’s AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.

Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive in Yemen to retake coastal territory from the Houthis in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.

Saudi Arabia’s sporting programme has been heavily hit since the outbreak of the United States and Israel’s war on Iran in late February.

The Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix slated for April in Jeddah was cancelled.

The WTA Finals were also scheduled to be held in Riyadh next month, but will instead take place at Indian Wells in the US.

World.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says
World.content:
New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned.

Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company.

Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies.

Beskrestnov said SpaceX's move "cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation". The firm has not commented.

In Wednesday's post on Telegram, Beskrestnov said that SpaceX had "implemented overnight a speed limit on Starlink terminals" and this had already resulted in "the disruption of a number of missions".

In a follow-up post, the adviser stressed that Starlink was the most effective tool for enabling interceptors to shoot down Russia's newly developed jet-propelled drones.

It comes as at least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes, Zelensky said. Pictures from Kyiv showed residents, some dressed in their pajamas, with bloodied faces.

He added that "critical" energy infrastructure had been hit in Kyiv and the capital region, and in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv â despite US President Donald Trump's claim on Sunday that an "energy ceasefire" was in place between Russia and Ukraine.

Three people were killed in Kyiv, local officials reported. Russia said its "massive" strikes had hit communications and energy facilities used by Ukraine's military.

Later on Wednesday, at least six people were killed in a Russian drone strike on a warehouse in the north-western city of Lutsk, local officials said.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

World.title: Pope walking and recovering 'as expected' after surgery, doctors say
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV's recovery from surgery to remove a lower lobe of his lung is "progressing as expected", his doctors have said.

The 71-year-old pontiff has started to walk and has "resumed a normal diet" following the roughly 90-minute procedure, the medics said in an update shared by the Vatican.

The Pope was diagnosed with lung cancer after the surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Tuesday afternoon, which the Vatican said had been "successful" and proceeded without complications.

Blood tests and an X-ray early on Wednesday showed his recovery was "proceeding normally", the doctors said, and he has also undergone respiratory physiotherapy.

The whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical", the Vatican said following the surgery.

"After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room," it said earlier, before spending a "peaceful night" at the hospital.

The pontiff is expected to remain there for about a week as he recovers.

World.title: US inflation rises more than expected - here's what is happening with prices
World.content:
US inflation rose by more than expected in the year to September, according to official figures, in the final data release before the midterm elections next month.

The pace of price rises increased to 3.7%, up from 3.4% in the 12 months to August.

Inflation was above forecasts, driven by higher gasoline prices which have risen following disruption to Middle East energy supplies due to the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

The elections are being fought over cost of living pressures across the US.

World.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
World.content:
A Ukrainian man has gone on trial in Hamburg accused of blowing up Russia's Nord Stream gas pipelines to Germany, four years after one of the most dramatic acts of sabotage in modern European history.

Prosecutors say Serhii Kuznetsov played a leading role in a team of saboteurs that destroyed the pipelines, accusing him of a war crime. His defence has called for the case to be dismissed.

The case is highly sensitive in Germany, one of Ukraine's closest allies since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, seven months before the attacks took place.

Extradited to Germany last year, Kuznetsov denies the charges, as does a second suspect who is fighting extradition from Croatia.

Kuznetsov became the first suspect to go on trial for the blasts on Wednesday morning, and a packed public gallery looked on as he entered the courtroom, appearing relaxed.

He even smiled at times, including during initial exchanges where he spoke to confirm personal details such as his name and place of birth.

He had previously only been identified by German prosecutors as Serhii K and pictured with his face blurred, but a court spokeswoman said he had now waived his anonymity.

Kuznetsov, 50, wore a pair of headphones and appeared to listen intently to a translation of proceedings in Ukrainian, as the prosecution read out the charges against him of ordering divers and an explosive expert to attack civilian infrastructure.

The defence outlined their case, telling the court that only circumstantial evidence had emerged in the four years since the Nord Stream blasts.

"[Prosecutors] made a thorough investigation of four years," Italian defence lawyer Nicola Canestrini told the BBC outside the courtroom. "They did not find one single witness, they did not find no forensics, no DNA, no fingerprints - nothing!"

World.title: Australia's first-ever Michelin stars go to 11 restaurants in one state
World.content:
Australia has been awarded its first Michelin stars, with 11 restaurants in the state of South Australia receiving the distinction.

Magill Estate Restaurant in Adelaide was the only venue to receive two stars, while 10 others were awarded one star each.

South Australia's government paid for incognito inspectors to visit the state, according to national broadcaster ABC, which is why no spots have been recognised in other parts of the country.

The announcement comes more than a century after the Michelin Guide was first published in France and following years of unsuccessful attempts to bring it to Australia.

Michelin has approached the national tourism board about bringing the guide to the country more than once, with no luck.

South Australia decided to go it alone and pursued its own deal. The state government has not disclosed how much it paid, but Tourism Minister Emily Bourke defended the investment in an interview with ABC News.

"It is enabling us to create a tourism destination and put us on the world map," she said.

The move follows Michelin's expansion into New Zealand, which became the first destination in Oceania to feature in the guide in July, agreeing to pay NZ$6.3m (Â£2.7m; $3.5m) over three years for its inclusion.

World.title: Netflix to shed 1,000 jobs in steepest cuts since 2022
World.content:
Netflix has said it will cut 1,000 jobs globally as the streaming giant faces competition from rivals.

The cuts - the steepest since 2022 - will mainly affect its human resources, legal, product and technology teams and equates to around 6% of its total workforce.

Last month, Netflix 's co-chief executive, Ted Sarandos, told the Bloomberg Screentime summit that the company was "not growing as fast as I want us to".

The streaming industry is going through a period of consolidation following Paramount's $110bn (Â£83.6bn) merger with Warner Bros, the owner of HBO, while free platforms such as YouTube and TikTok continue to attract viewers.

In an email to staff, Sarandos and co-chief executive Greg Peters said Netflix would "continue to invest aggressively in high-impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation".

Netflix had come close to its own deal with Warner Bros but was outbid in the end by Paramount.

Commenting on the "organisational changes", Sarandos and Peters said: "Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritise our people and resources."

Managers will tell employees whether their job has been cut "soon".

World.title: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
World.content:
The 40-year-old Kenyan man who died on 5 October was diagnosed with Ebola shortly after being admitted to hospital in the capital, Nairobi.

A relative had taken him there shortly after picking him up at the airport. He had travelled from DR Congo, through Uganda to Kenya without his illness being detected.

Since his death, officials had determined that he had been in contact with 128 people - and since Tuesday 113 of them had been found, the health ministry said.

Of these, 108 were in quarantine in Kenya and tracing of the remaining 15 continued, it said.

More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

"Anyone with fever, unusual tiredness, muscle or joint pains, vomiting, diarrhoea or unexplained bleeding should seek care promptly at the nearest health facility," Kenya's health ministry said.

The current outbreak in DR Congo, which began in May, has been caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

Shortly after DR Congo declared an outbreak of Ebola in May, it was also reported in Uganda, where two people died.

However, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared that county free of the disease in August.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the continent's leading public health agency, has reconstructed the Kenyan patient's movements for the six weeks leading up to his death.

It revealed that he first started feeling unwell in DR Congo on 15 September - and showed how several opportunities to detect the infection were missed, including during several visits to Congolese medical facilities.

He then managed to travel through Uganda to Kenya - and was again not detected at airports screenings.

Health experts say it highlights the limitations of relying on temperature checks and self-declarations.

World.title: Hundreds of thousands of workers on strike across Republic of Ireland
World.content:
More than 300,000 workers, including nurses, doctors, teachers and civil servants, are on strike across the Republic of Ireland.

It comes amid an ongoing pay dispute between public sector workers and the Irish government, with a further strike planned on 21 October.

It is expected schools could be closed with hospital appointments cancelled and picket lines formed across the country during the 24-hour strike.

At the end of September, more than 100,000 workers, including nurses, school staff and civil servants, moved to work-to-rule measures.

At the start of October, primary and secondary school teachers in the Republic began work-to-rule action.

Previously almost 97% of FÃ³rsa members, who voted in an industrial ballot, did so in favour of action. It is the Republic's biggest public service union.

World.title: Atiku faults Tinubu’s expanded campaign council, use of Presidential Villa
World.content:
Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has criticised President Bola Tinubu over the expanded All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, accusing him of assembling politicians to shield his administration from criticism over economic hardship and insecurity.

He also condemned the decision to inaugurate the council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, describing the use of the facility for a partisan event as an abuse of public office.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku described the revised APC list as “a crowded confession of Tinubu’s fear”.

“Only a man afraid of his record would think he could bury it under hundreds of names. Tinubu can gather every governor, minister and political defector in Nigeria. None of them can erase the hunger in people’s homes, bring back those killed by violence or free Nigerians still held captive. Their families are waiting for answers, not another campaign list,” he said.

The criticism followed the APC’s announcement that the council, which is expected to coordinate campaign activities ahead of the 2027 elections, would be inaugurated on Wednesday at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa.

Use of Presidential Villa

The former vice-president accused Mr Tinubu of treating the seat of government as an extension of the ruling party.

“The Presidential Villa belongs to the Nigerian people. It is not a campaign venue or the private property of any political party. Using it for an APC political event is a gross breach of public trust and a troubling abuse of public office,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He questioned why the president chose the Villa when Abuja had other venues suitable for political gatherings.

“Why, then, did Bola Tinubu choose to inaugurate his campaign council at night, behind the gates of the Presidential Villa?” he asked.

However, the APC had announced that the inauguration would take place at 11 a.m. on Wednesday, contrary to Atiku’s reference to a nighttime event.

Turning to the council’s membership, Atiku accused the president of prioritising political alliances over the welfare of Nigerians.

“When the first list drew criticism, Tinubu had a chance to show that he understood the country’s anger. Instead, he returned with an even longer list, reaching into other parties for more names,” he said.

“He is collecting politicians like shields against public judgment. Let him collect them all.”

Poverty, insecurity and 2027 election

Atiku also cited the 2026 Global Multidimensional Poverty Index, saying an additional 17.9 million Nigerians had fallen into multidimensional poverty.

The figures cited in the statement compare an estimated 72.2 million Nigerians living in multidimensional poverty in 2021 with 90.1 million in 2024.

However, the period began before Mr Tinubu assumed office in May 2023, meaning the entire increase cannot be attributed to his administration.

“No campaign council, however crowded, can make food affordable, restore a worker’s purchasing power or explain why the sacrifices demanded of ordinary Nigerians never seem to reach Tinubu’s own political circle,” Atiku said.

He contrasted the APC’s expanded council with the ADC’s campaign structure, which he described as focused on presenting its case to Nigerians.

“The ADC has assembled a focused campaign team to take its case to Nigerians. Tinubu can keep adding names to his council. He cannot add a name that will make life affordable again for the families struggling under his government,” he said.

The former vice-president maintained that voters would judge the president by his administration’s record rather than the number of politicians supporting his re-election.

“On January 16, the ballot will contain no column for the size of a campaign council. Nigerians will judge Tinubu by the lives they have lived under his government,” he said.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has scheduled the presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January 2027.

World.title: Over 87,000 children treated for malnutrition in Katsina in eight months – MSF
World.content:
More than 87,000 children received outpatient treatment for acute malnutrition at four therapeutic feeding centres run by Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) in Katsina State between January and August.

The number is lower than the over 95,000 treated during the same period in 2025, but MSF says it remains extremely high.

Nearly 15,500 children were also hospitalised for severe or complicated malnutrition in the first eight months of 2026, compared with about 16,500 during the corresponding period last year.

MSF’s medical coordinator in Nigeria, Raphael Kananga, said the figures remained troubling despite the decline.

“This is lower than in 2025, when we treated more than 95,000 children over the same period, but the figure remains extremely high and is even above what we saw two years ago,” Mr Kananga said.

The figures cover children treated in MSF facilities and do not represent the total number of malnourished children in Katsina State.

MSF identified poverty, inflation, insecurity, displacement, disease outbreaks and extreme weather as major drivers of the crisis. These factors have disrupted farming and limited access to food in vulnerable communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Kwashiorkor complicates treatment

MSF also raised concern about the high number of children with kwashiorkor, a severe form of malnutrition characterised by swelling of the body and, in some cases, skin lesions.

Caregivers may find the condition difficult to recognise, which can delay treatment.

To address the problem, MSF opened a specialised unit within its inpatient therapeutic feeding centre in Katsina to care for children with kwashiorkor.

Badiyya Shafi’u, whose child received treatment at the facility, said she initially failed to recognise the symptoms as malnutrition.

“I didn’t think it was malnutrition. This kind of condition is difficult to recognise,” she said.

Her child’s condition had deteriorated to the point where he could not sit without assistance.

“Before, he could not even sit up on his own. If someone helped him sit, he would immediately fall back down,” she recalled.

Following treatment, she said, the child could sit independently, remain standing with assistance and had begun trying to walk again.

MSF did not provide a separate figure for the number of children diagnosed with kwashiorkor during the reporting period.

Improved harvests, security linked to fewer admissions

MSF attributed part of the reduction in treatment figures to improved security and better agricultural harvests in parts of Katsina during 2025.

Its partnership coordinator, Jean-Clément Ishimwe, said some families displaced by insecurity in Jibia and Batsari local government areas had returned home and resumed farming.

“Many people displaced from Jibia or Batsari local governmental areas because of insecurity had been living in areas such as Katsina, Mashi and Mani,” he said.

“Since last year, however, they have been able to return home and resume farming.”

According to Mr Ishimwe, the return enabled some households to access food more easily and coincided with fewer patients arriving at MSF treatment centres.

The organisation also linked the decline in hospitalisations to increased humanitarian interventions and the opening of additional outpatient and inpatient treatment facilities by the Katsina State Government.

MSF supported the expansion by training healthcare workers and strengthening services at the new centres.

It said these interventions likely helped reduce the number of children requiring hospitalisation ahead of the peak malnutrition season.

The decline in admissions, however, does not independently establish a corresponding reduction in the overall prevalence of malnutrition across Katsina State.

₦1 billion allocation and UNICEF commitment

MSF acknowledged increased government efforts to address the crisis but warned that inadequate funding and shortages of ready-to-use therapeutic food continued to threaten treatment services.

According to Mr Ishimwe, the Katsina State Government allocated ₦1 billion to tackle malnutrition, doubling its previous allocation, particularly for the procurement of therapeutic food.

He said UNICEF had also pledged to mobilise an equivalent amount through its Child Nutrition Fund.

“Strong commitments have been made by Katsina State, including the allocation of one billion naira to fight malnutrition,” he said.

“If these commitments are fulfilled, this will be an encouraging sign that deserves to be supported and expanded across Katsina State and throughout northern Nigeria.”

The MSF article did not specify how much of the state’s ₦1 billion allocation had been released or spent, or whether UNICEF had completed the proposed matching contribution.

The organisation said Katsina had expanded its network of ambulatory treatment centres from only a few in 2021 to approximately 400 in 2026.

Despite the expansion, funding constraints and difficulties obtaining therapeutic food remain recurring challenges.

MSF said reductions in humanitarian assistance from the United States and several European countries, including France, Germany and the United Kingdom, had further complicated efforts to sustain treatment programmes.

Wider crisis across northern Nigeria

The situation in Katsina forms part of a wider childhood malnutrition crisis affecting several northern states.

Across its nutrition projects in seven northern states, MSF said its teams treated 57,999 children in inpatient facilities and 225,778 through outpatient programmes between January and August.

The organisation also cited concerns raised by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria, which reported that nearly two million Nigerian children were affected by severe acute malnutrition, while only about two in every 10 received treatment.

The figures, cited in MSF’s article, reflect the society’s assessment rather than a new nationwide survey conducted by MSF.

The humanitarian organisation called for sustained financial support from federal and state governments, international donors and humanitarian partners to expand treatment services and improve access to therapeutic food.

It warned that without continued investment, many vulnerable children would remain exposed to life-threatening malnutrition despite the reduction in admissions recorded at its Katsina facilities.

World.title: Why Nigeria is lucky to have Tinubu as leader now – Oyedele
World.content:
Nigeria’s Finance Minister and the Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on Wednesday said the country is fortunate to have President Bola Tinubu at the helm of affairs at a time of economic challenges and global uncertainty.

Mr Oyedele made the remark on Wednesday on the sidelines of the World Bank/International Monetary Fund (IMF) meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, where he praised the president for his willingness to implement difficult economic reforms and his understanding of economic and monetary policy issues.

“I say to myself every time that Nigeria is lucky to have a leader like Mr President,” the minister said.

“A leader that says ‘I’ll do the right thing, even when it’s not popular’. There are so very few of them, and our president is not saying it; he’s doing it, he’s doing it even with pre-election (concerns),” he added.

Since assuming office in May 2023, the Tinubu administration has introduced a series of economic reforms, the impact of which international institutions like the World Bank and the IMF have acknowledged

The reforms include the removal of costly petrol subsidies, which had been a major drain on public finance for years, the unification of the foreign exchange rates and the sharp devaluation of the naira to attract foreign capital.

Although abolishing fuel subsidies has boosted government revenue and is seen as an investor-friendly move, it has triggered a cost-of-living crisis and spurred inflationary pressures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reforms in the foreign exchange market have helped increase accretion to external reserves, which stood at $55.1 billion as of 9 October, its peak level in over 18 years.

The banking sector also underwent a recapitalisation exercise that ended in March and helped Nigerian banks raise N4.7 trillion in new capital.

According to the Central Bank of Nigeria, the recapitalisation strengthened banks’ capital adequacy ratios, keeping the sector above international Basel benchmarks.

Mr Oyedele said President Tinubu possesses two attributes uncommon among leaders, notably those of democratic governments.

READ ALSO: AFC appoints Cardoso as board chairman

The first is his willingness to do what he considers right, even when the decision is unpopular or politically difficult.

“I remember at least three issues that were discussed with him recently, and on my own I would offer to say ‘maybe we wait until after the election’. And his question is always, ‘Is it the right thing to do?’ Yes, yes, it is. Why do we have to wait?” Mr Oyedele said.

“Number two attribute is that our President gets it. It’s not easy to understand issues to do with the economy, finance, monetary policy, like respect for the independence of the monetary authority. For Mr President, it’s 100 per cent,” he added.

The minister added that the president’s position on such matters has made it unnecessary for officials to discuss the issue with him repeatedly.

“We don’t even talk about it. So, I feel like we are so blessed, we cannot afford to wait even one minute,” he said.

World.title: GYMFEST Championship returns to Lagos for third edition
World.content:
The third edition of the GYMFEST Championship will take place on 7 November at The Dome, Freedom Way, Lekki Phase 1, Lagos State, with organisers seeking to attract more young athletes, schools, and gymnastics clubs.

The competition is convened by Tee Tumblers Gymnastics Club and the Society for the Performing Arts in Nigeria (SPAN).

According to the organisers, the first two editions attracted more than 400 athletes from over 20 schools and involved more than 60 certified coaches. They also reported that the competitions drew over 2,000 spectators and were supported by more than 20 volunteers, with no incidents recorded.

Yoyin Akpose, co-convener of the championship and founder of Tee Tumblers Gymnastics Club, said the competition was created to help address the limited opportunities available to young Nigerians interested in gymnastics.

“Every child should have the opportunity to participate in gymnastics. There is so much talent in Nigeria that we are not even close to harnessing, and we need to create more awareness and opportunities for these children to thrive,” she said.

Ms Akpose said the organisers hoped to establish structures and standards that would enable Nigerian gymnasts to compete at international events.

“The dream is to create the right structure and standards for gymnastics in Nigeria, so that our young gymnasts can compete internationally and Nigeria can produce more athletes capable of representing the country on the world stage,” she said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Organisers seek wider participation

Schools, clubs and coaches have been invited to register gymnasts for this year’s competition, while members of the public can attend as spectators.

The organisers said participating gymnasts would pay a ₦20,000 registration fee, while spectator tickets would cost ₦5,000. Sponsorship opportunities are also available to companies interested in supporting the event.

Sarah Boulos, co-convener of GYMFEST and founder of SPAN, said the competition combines sport and the arts to promote discipline and confidence among young people.

“Through dedication, arts, and athletics, we build discipline and international confidence. Every partner who joins us becomes part of an enduring legacy,” she said.

The organisers said previous editions of the championship received media coverage, and more is expected this year.

This year’s edition is sponsored by ProvidusUnity Bank, with Leadway Assurance, Indomie, Studio 24 and YD Company also supporting the event.

The championship will also give vendors space to showcase their products and services to attendees.

GYMFEST is organised to provide young gymnasts with opportunities to compete and develop their skills. Its third edition comes as organisers work to widen participation in the sport and create pathways for young athletes to progress to higher levels of competition.

World.title: Peter Obi fails to provide details after accusing Tinubu’s govt of targeting him
World.content:
The 2027 presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has failed to provide details on how President Bola Tinubu’s government has targeted and frustrated him.

Mr Obi had suggested that his life was under threat because Mr Tinubu’s government was constantly frustrating and targeting him.

The NDC candidate, a former governor of Anambra State, made the claim in July during a podcast interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo.

“Every single thing I do for a living, this government is frustrating it. Deliberately so. So, there is even a possibility, if they have the opportunity, I will not be alive,” he had claimed.

Giving instances of targeted attacks against him, Mr Obi referenced an incident at an airport where officials allegedly locked his car despite other vehicles being parked in the same area.

But Bayo Onanuga, the special adviser on information and strategy to Mr Tinubu, refuted the allegations and described them as “unfounded and misleading”.

The Minister of Aviation, Festus Keyamo, later refuted Mr Obi’s airport claims, explaining that CCTV footage from the airport showed that the former governor’s vehicle was parked unattended for about 30 minutes in a designated drop-off zone, contrary to airport regulations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Keyamo asked Mr Obi to pay a N25,000 fine for violating airport regulations and then apologise to Nigerians for claiming that his vehicle was “unjustly” clamped at the airport.

Ignored enquiry

On 13 August, PREMIUM TIMES contacted Mr Obi’s media aide, Valentine Obienyem, who asked our reporter to forward the letter of enquiry to him via his WhatsApp, which was done immediately.

In the enquiry, PREMIUM TIMES asked Mr Obi to identify his businesses and their specific locations, which he alleged are being targeted by the Nigerian government.

This newspaper also sought to know how and when he, as well as his businesses, had been allegedly targeted by the government.

The former governor was asked to give specific details of his claims of an unjust clampdown, especially since Mr Keyamo had refuted his earlier claim about the airport incident.

He was also to provide details of the benefits he was denied or struggled to obtain despite being entitled to them.

The politician was further asked to provide specific instances where people were targeted or attacked after he honoured their invitations or attended their events.

“We would appreciate any relevant documents, evidence, dates, locations or other information that may assist us in properly understanding your concerns and allegations,” this newspaper wrote in the enquiry.

After weeks of silence, our reporter sent Mr Obienyem a reminder on 9 September.

The reporter also sent a WhatsApp message to Mr Obi via his known mobile number in which he introduced himself and announced his intention to forward a letter of enquiry to him, which was done immediately.

Messrs Obi and Obienyem did not respond to separate WhatsApp calls on 18 September.

Our reporter, however, forwarded separate reminders to their WhatsApp lines the same day.

Mr Obi still did not reply, but Mr Obienyem, the following day, asked our reporter to resend the enquiry, which was done immediately.

After another 11 days of silence, this reporter forwarded separate reminders to Messrs Obi and Obienyem on 30 September.

But the duo, again, remained silent despite the repeated reminders.

World.title: AFC appoints Cardoso as board chairman
World.content:
Africa Finance Corporation (AFC), the continent’s leading multilateral financial institution, has appointed Olayemi Cardoso, the governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), as the chairman of its board of directors.

Mr Cardoso will succeed Ireti Samuel-Ogbu, who will remain a board member, according to a statement from the corporation on Wednesday.

Mr Cardoso’s appointment comes as the AFC continues to expand its role in financing and developing strategic infrastructure assets that address Africa’s infrastructure gap, accelerate industrialisation and strengthen regional integration.

“Mr Cardoso shares our conviction that Africa’s lasting stability depends on its productive capacity. His leadership will strengthen the AFC as we advance The Africa We Build 2050, mobilising African capital to build the infrastructure and industries that create jobs, prosperity and dignity for our people,” Samaila Zubairu, president and CEO of the AFC, said.

Speaking on his appointment, Mr Cardoso expressed optimism about working with AFC, noting that the corporation’s measure of success must be the productive capacity it creates, the industries it enables and the jobs it supports.

“A more productive Africa is a more stable Africa. AFC has the credibility and track record to mobilise capital and build the infrastructure and industries that drive transformation,” Mr Cardoso said.

“I look forward to working with the Board, management and member states to advance The Africa We Build 2050. Our measure of success must be the productive capacity we create, the industries we enable and the jobs we support,” he added.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Profile

Mr Cardoso brings extensive experience spanning international banking, investment management, economic policy and public sector leadership.

Since assuming office as CBN governor in September 2023, he has led far-reaching monetary, financial-sector, and institutional reforms to restore macroeconomic stability, strengthen policy credibility, and rebuild investor confidence in Nigeria’s economy.

Under his leadership, the CBN has implemented significant foreign exchange market reforms, addressed longstanding FX obligations, strengthened monetary policy transmission, and enhanced institutional governance and transparency.

CBN has also concluded a recapitalisation programme for the banking sector, aimed at strengthening the resilience and capacity of Nigeria’s financial system to support sustainable economic growth.

Before he was appointed CBN Governor, Mr Cardoso built a distinguished career in international banking and public service, including a 12-year tenure as the chairman of Citibank Nigeria and service as the commissioner for economic planning and budget in Lagos State.

He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Managerial and Administrative Studies from Aston University in the UK and a Master’s in Public Administration from Harvard Kennedy School, where he also served on the Alumni Board.

According to the AFC, Mr Cardoso’s experience in financial-sector reform, institutional governance and capital markets will provide valuable perspective on the corporation’s strategic direction as it mobilises investment to unlock Africa’s economic potential.

World.title: Ovom Erosion Project: Otti doesn’t just have capacity, he has empathy, By Ferdinand Ekeoma
World.content:
There are projects that are executed. And there are projects that are felt. The Ovom Erosion Project in Aba belongs to the second category.

Before Governor Alex Otti came, Ovom was not just an erosion site. It was a wound. A gaping, expanding disaster that swallowed houses whole, threatened lives, destroyed livelihoods and sent families fleeing from their ancestral homes. For years, it was a monument of abandonment – visited only during election seasons when politicians came with empty promises, cameras and loudspeakers, and left with votes.

The reclaimed, reconstructed Ovom Road previously ravaged by erosion

That politics of deceit ended on a quiet Sunday afternoon.

Governor Otti, on one of his unannounced inspections of Aba, drove into Ovom. No sirens. No prior notice. The convoy was sighted, and worshippers trooped out of churches in their numbers. Men, women, and youths – they surrounded him, not with placards, but with pain. They showed him houses half-buried and fences hanging in the air.

As usual, he listened and promised to return.

And as has now become his trademark, he did not return with another promise. He returned with action.

In record time, what was once a death trap has been tamed. The massive gully has been reclaimed, the road restored, the neighborhood secured, lives protected and the neighbourhood lit up. No drama. No endless flag-off ceremonies. Just engineering, empathy and execution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

That is the difference between this government and what we had in the past. In the past, disasters like Ovom were political goldmines – kept alive to be used for campaigns every four years. The worse the erosion, the better the campaign slogan. For Governor Otti, a disaster is not a campaign tool. It is an emergency that must be solved.

And that is what sets him apart. He does not just have CAPACITY. He has EMPATHY.

Empathy is why projects that used to take four years are now delivered in four months. Empathy is why a road is not just tarred, but tarred with drainage that actually drains. Empathy is why a worker is not just paid, but paid on time and with dignity. Empathy is why a market is not just demolished, but relocated with a human face, and lands taken for development get compensation.

Ovom is another proof that Abia is now in the hands of a man who sees the people first, and politics last.

For the people of Ovom who fled and have now returned, for the children who can now go to school without fear of being swallowed by the gully, for the landlords who thought they had lost everything, this is not just erosion control. It is hope restored.

And that is the Otti story: Capacity with a human heart.

Ferdinand Ekeoma is the Special Adviser Media and Publicity to the Governor Alex Otti of Abia State

World.title: 2027: Uba Sani rallies support for Tinubu
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani has counselled public office holders from Kaduna State to work towards President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, by mobilising towards a successful presidential campaign flag off on 24 October.

The governor who made this known at a high-level strategic meeting, also charged political appointees at both state and federal level to strengthen coordination of political activities, towards the success of the All Progressives Congress(APC) in the coming elections.

Governor Uba Sani pointed out that ‘’President Tinubu has demonstrated an unprecedented commitment to Kaduna State through transformative investments in infrastructure, education and economic development.

‘’Such extraordinary commitment deserves more than expressions of gratitude; it demands collective responsibility to consolidate these gains and sustain the momentum of development.’’

“We must translate our appreciation into decisive political action. I charge every federal appointee and stakeholder to close ranks, deepen grassroots engagement and work towards delivering a resounding landslide victory for President Tinubu in 2027,” the Governor stated.

Governor Uba Sani cited the Kaduna Light Rail, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano Highway, Kaduna–Birnin Gwari Road, Kaduna–Kano Rail Project and investments in federal tertiary institutions underscore the President’s commitment to the development of Kaduna State.

He emphasised that sustained collaboration between federal appointees and the State Government is critical in translating these investments into lasting economic opportunities, improved security and better living conditions for the people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The high-level strategic meeting was attended by the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, Minister of Environment, Malam Balarabe Abbas Lawal, Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko; Chairmen and Members of Federal Boards; Heads of Parastatals; Federal Commissioners; and other key stakeholders.

The meeting resolved to work closely with the APC leadership and key stakeholders to consolidate and coordinate political structures across the 23 local government areas in the state.

The participants expressed profound appreciation to President Tinubu for choosing Kaduna for flag off of his re-election campaign, his administration’s significant infrastructural investments and the appointment of Kaduna indigenes into strategic federal positions.

The political appointees described the President’s decision to host the campaign flag-off in Kaduna as a recognition of the state’s strategic political importance, reaffirming their commitment to ensuring a successful event.

They also resolved to strengthen stakeholder coordination before, during and after the elections, with emphasis on peaceful participation, effective engagement and post-election reconciliation.

The public office holders pledged to serve as worthy ambassadors of Kaduna State, leveraging their respective positions to support the policies and programmes of President Tinubu and Governor Uba Sani, by ensuring that the dividends of democracy reach communities across the state.

They renewed commitment to political unity, stronger federal-state collaboration and sustained support for the Renewed Hope Agenda and Kaduna State’s development priorities.

World.title: Vinícius handed four-match ban, to miss Real Madrid’s Clasico against Barcelona
World.content:
Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward #07 Vinicius Junior (C) is restrained by teammates as he argues with referee Isidro Escuderos after receiving a red card during the Spanish league football match between Real Madrid CF and Villarreal CF at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Júnior has been handed a four-match suspension after pulling an opponent’s hair during his side’s 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday.

The Brazilian was sent off in the 73rd minute after grabbing and tugging the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba as the two players sprinted down the pitch. Vinícius had scored moments earlier, but the goal was ruled out.

The Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee announced the suspension shortly before Real Madrid’s Champions

League match against Roma on Wednesday.

According to the committee, Vinícius received a two-match ban for the hair-pulling incident and an additional two matches for his aggressive reaction to the referee after being shown the red card.

Referee Isidro Díaz de Mera stated in his match report that the forward protested the decision by raising his voice and approaching him aggressively, adding that Vinícius had to be restrained by his teammates.

The suspension means Vinícius will miss Real Madrid’s home fixture against Sevilla on Sunday and their trip to Barcelona the following week for the highly anticipated Clasico.

He will also be unavailable for Madrid’s away matches against Racing Santander and Valencia.

The four-match ban comes as a setback for Real Madrid, who will be without one of their key attacking players for several important domestic fixtures.
