World.title: Pope out of bed, progress ‘normal’ after cancer operation
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV waves to the crowd after leading a mass to celebrate the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Basilica of Our Lady of Good Counsel, in Genazzano, near Rome, on September 7, 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP)

Pope Leo XIV is out of bed, walking and eating after doctors removed a cancerous tumour from his lung, while post-surgery tests show his progress is “normal”, his doctors said Wednesday.

Part of the pope’s right lung was removed in Tuesday’s operation at Rome’s Gemelli hospital and the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics is now awaiting the results of a biopsy to determine if the cancer has spread.

Blood tests and a chest X-ray meanwhile “confirm a normal post-operative course”, doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora said in a statement released by the Vatican.

“The values are within the expected range for the type of procedure performed,” they said.

The discovery on Tuesday that a nodule detected in Leo’s lung was cancerous has plunged the Catholic Church into a period of uncertainty.

“It’s a shock for everyone. We’re in ‘wait-and-see’ mode,” a Vatican source told AFP.

Doctors said his recovery was “proceeding as expected” and the pontiff had eaten both breakfast and lunch, been walking about his room, and had done some respiratory physiotherapy.

Another Vatican source said the pope had even celebrated a mass on Wednesday in a specially prepared room on the 10th floor of the hospital, where is staying.

The papal suite on the same floor is where popes are usually treated. It has a private chapel but is currently being refurbished.

– ‘Show my spiritual support’ –

The sporty 71-year-old, elected as the first pope from the United States only last year, made the surprise announcement that he would be undergoing surgery after Sunday prayers.

Messages of support flooded in from around the world, including from Britain’s King Charles III, who is also being treated for an undisclosed cancer.

A banner flying outside the hospital read “Long live the pope!” and a handful of people recited prayers for the hospitalised pontiff.

Nearby, nun Angele Bilegue said she had come to pray for Leo.

“I’m not worried. I came to express my closeness, to show my spiritual support, because I also came for Pope Francis,” she told AFP.

Leo’s predecessor, the Argentine Francis, spent five weeks last year being treated for double pneumonia at the same hospital, before his death at the Vatican on April 21, 2025.

Experts said much would depend on how advanced Leo’s cancer was, and whether it had spread, but the Vatican has said it had been detected early and was localised.

Before the operation, the Vatican said the pope’s recovery should take around a week. All his audiences have been cancelled until October 20.

“If we are dealing with stage I or II disease, and recovery is good… the patient can resume a normal life and usual activities within a few weeks,” Alain Gelibter, an oncologist at Rome’s Policlinico Umberto I hospital, told AFP.

The Chicago-born Leo had entered the hospital smiling and waving on Tuesday.

In the hospital chapel, dozens of faithful prayed for the pope’s health during the operation.

– New uncertainty –

The shock news of the tennis-playing pope’s illness has rattled the Catholic Church.

Expert Marco Politi, who has spent decades covering the Vatican, told AFP: “The Church is now in a state of uncertainty. When Leo was elected everyone foresaw a long papacy.”

Hendro Munsterman, a theologian and expert for Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad, told AFP “we have a pope whom everyone described as young, active and athletic. Now, we have a pope who also has his own vulnerabilities, which will change his image.”

His health issues may prompt him to speed up personnel appointments, Munsterman said.

Politi said Leo had been working on “repairing” rifts between various wings of the Church, and many will want him “to continue with this important mission as soon as possible”.

Filipino Cardinal Luis Antonio Tagle, newly nominated to the influential role of dean of the College of Cardinals, celebrated mass on St Peter’s Square on Wednesday instead of Leo.

The surgery has raised questions about whether Leo will go ahead with a lengthy visit next month to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he worked as a missionary for two decades.

Vanguard News

World.title: Barcola scores hat-trick as Liverpool thrash LASK 6-3 in Champions League
World.content:
Liverpool’s Uruguayan defender #33 Ronald Araujo (R) celebrates scoring the opening goal with his teammate Liverpool’s French midfielder #29 Bradley Barcola during the UEFA Champions League football match between LASK and Liverpool FC in Linz, Austria on October 14, 2026. (Photo by Branislav Racko / AFP)

Bradley Barcola silenced his critics as the Liverpool forward ended his goal drought with a hat-trick in a chaotic 6-3 win against LASK in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Barcola had come under fire for some lacklustre performances since his blockbuster £123 million ($161 million) move from Paris Saint-Germain in August.

But the France forward finally started to live up to his hefty price tag with his first goals for Liverpool in his seventh appearance.

Barcola struck twice before the interval at the Raiffeisen Arena after Ronald Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the first half with his maiden goal for the club.

Jeremie Frimpong netted the fourth after the break against the Austrian champions before Barcola completed his treble.

There was still time for Lewis Koumas to score his first Champions League goal as Liverpool maintained their 100 percent record in this season’s tournament after beating Atletico Madrid in their opening game.

It was a welcome boost for Iraola following his first defeat in eight games as Liverpool manager when Premier League leaders Manchester City won 3-0 at Anfield on Sunday.

Iraola this week said he has “100 per cent” trust in Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who has struggled mightily since joining from Bayer Leverkusen last year.

Injuries to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, who all missed the trip to Austria, increased the pressure on Wirtz and Barcola to carry the Liverpool attack.

The pair repaid Iraola’s faith with a much-needed display of their undoubted qualities.

Now Iraola will demand they produce that level of intensity and quality on a regular basis.

The trip to Linz was the second of six games in 18 days for Liverpool, forcing Iraola to make changes in a bid to save his players from burnout.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk, Milos Kerkez, Alexis Mac Allister and Victor Munoz were all rested as Frimpong, Kostas Tsimikas, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha came in.

– Clinical Barcola –

After some disjointed displays at the start of Iraola’s reign, this was an indication of what they can become under the former Bournemouth boss, although he will still be concerned about their defensive issues.

Araujo put Liverpool ahead in the 22nd minute, rising highest to meet Tsimikas’s corner with a thumping header past LASK keeper Lukas Jungwirth.

The on-loan Barcelona defender’s goal was swiftly followed by one for Barcola 96 seconds later.

Ngumoha was the catalyst with an incisive run into the LASK area and Barcola applied the finishing touch as he guided a clinical finish beyond Jungwirth.

Iraola’s men were running riot and Barcola scored their third in the 37th minute.

It was a riposte to the criticism of Wirtz and Barcola as the pair combined to cut through the LASK defence.

Barcola picked out Wirtz and the German played a pinpoint return pass that allowed the 24-year-old to fire past Jungwirth.

Frimpong has also frustrated Liverpool fans since signing last year, making his goal in the 51st minute a welcome tonic for the Dutch right-back.

Tsimikas got to the byline and lofted a cross towards Frimpong, who belied his diminutive stature with a towering header into the bottom corner.

Robert Ljubicic reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute with a composed finish from Yvan Dibango’s pass.

But Barcola sealed his treble with a nimble finish from Frimpong’s pass in the 66th minute.

Teed up by Frimpong, Koumas hit Liverpool’s sixth with a searing strike in the 72nd minute.

Despite the introduction of Van Dijk and fellow defender Joe Gomez, Liverpool lost control in the closing stages.

Florian Flecker’s diving header two minutes later punished slack Liverpool defending.

Flecker struck again with a close-range finish in the 77th minute, but nothing could spoil Barcola’s big night.

World.title: Man United line up three-man shortlist as sack looms for Michael Carrick
World.content:
Carrick

Manchester United are reportedly considering Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler, former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for Michael Carrick if the club decides to part ways with its current manager.

According to talkSPORT, the three managers have attracted interest from different figures within the Old Trafford hierarchy as pressure mounts on Carrick following a difficult run of results.

United’s reported interest comes after their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday, which extended their winless run to five matches across all competitions.

The result also followed a 1-1 draw against Tottenham Hotspur, a run of form that has raised concerns about the team’s performances and Carrick’s tactical decisions.

The defeat to Atletico also prompted defender Lisandro Martinez to criticise technical director Jason Wilcox over what he reportedly viewed as insufficient squad strengthening.

United will look to end their poor run when they face historic rivals Leeds United in the Premier League on Sunday.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, the station’s chief live football anchor, Adrian Durham, suggested Carrick’s position could become increasingly difficult if the team fails to improve.

“Does it feel like an inevitability? Absolutely, that Michael Carrick will go,” Durham said.

He added that Carrick would need to turn around the team’s results to improve his chances of remaining in the job.

Durham also expressed concerns about Carrick’s tactical decisions in the Atletico Madrid match, arguing that some of the changes made during the game contributed to United’s defeat.

Among the three reported candidates, Nagelsmann and Conte are said to be available for an immediate appointment.

Conte left Napoli by mutual consent in May, while Nagelsmann reportedly departed his position as Germany coach following the country’s elimination by Paraguay in the round of 32 at the World Cup.

The report said United’s director of recruitment, Christopher Vivell, was advocating for Nagelsmann internally as a potential successor should the club decide to dismiss Carrick.

Hurzeler, meanwhile, remains under contract with Brighton until 2029 after signing an extension in May.

The German coach is reportedly favoured by Wilcox and has overseen a strong start to the Premier League season, with Brighton winning four of their opening six matches to sit third in the standings.

Hurzeler has also guided Brighton to victory over Manchester United in the third round of the EFL Cup in September, adding to his credentials as a potential candidate.

However, Manchester United have not been reported to have made a formal appointment decision, and Carrick’s immediate future could depend on the team’s results in the coming matches.

World.title: You’re not Abraham Lincoln — Shettima berates Atiku for ‘disrespecting’ Tinubu
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar over what he described as disrespectful comments about President Bola Tinubu, saying anyone seeking the presidency must show discipline and respect for public institutions.

Shettima spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council for the 2027 election.

In his remarks, Shettima said Atiku’s repeated presidential bids and recent policy proposals did not, in his view, excuse language he considered disrespectful toward the sitting president. He also questioned how Atiku’s proposed production subsidies would be funded.

“Those who want equity must come with clean hands. You can call him Bola. If you like, you can call him Adekunle. But the truth is that he is the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“Your Excellencies, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, Atiku Abubakar. I will still respect him and call him his former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar.

“I will not follow suit with the maverick Babachir Lawal and call him Kachalla, no. But believe me, Atiku Abubakar, who has contested for the presidency of this country for the eighth time, is no Abraham Lincoln. He is more of Oginga Odinga.”

Shettima framed his criticism as an argument about the conduct expected of presidential contenders, saying the higher the office sought, the greater the responsibility candidates bear in their words and dealings with public institutions.

“The presidency of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is not an ordinary political prize. It is the highest expression of constitutional authority in our country. And those who aspire to occupy it must demonstrate, even before they get there, the qualities they will expect of themselves, if entrusted with the responsibility of leading more than 200 million Nigerians.

“Political ambition is not merely the desire to occupy public office. It is a test of character, cerebral strength, intellectual maturity, and responsibility. The higher the office a person seeks, the greater the discipline expected in his words, conduct, and relationship with public institutions,” he added.

Turning to Atiku’s proposal on production subsidies, Shettima questioned the cost and the competing priorities that might be affected.

“Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, this political season has become a masterclass in cinematic comedy. Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal for production subsidies raises questions that some changes cannot answer. Who pays? Who benefits? And which competing priorities must surrender their funding? A change in ideological wardrobe cannot balance a national budget.”

The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council inauguration, held at the Banquet Hall of the Presidential Villa in Abuja, formally brought the expanded campaign structure into focus as the ruling party prepared for the 2027 general election.

World.title: Reps order halt to disputed land development in Imo
World.content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja

The House of Representatives Committee on Public Petitions has ordered a halt to further development on a disputed parcel of land in Umundoche community, Ngor Okpala Local Government Area of Imo State, pending the resolution of a petition alleging illegal land acquisition and intimidation of residents.

The committee also directed that armed men allegedly operating in the community be disarmed following claims that villagers had been threatened with firearms amid the dispute.

The directives were issued on Wednesday during a hearing on Petition No. 901 of 2026, filed by J.U. Okoye Chambers against Prince Charles Amadi, also known as Chavon; Chikadibia Anyanwu; and Chidubem Nwosu.

The petition alleges the illegal acquisition of more than 2,500 hectares of land, shooting and attempted murder of villagers, the invasion of the community by armed men, desecration of a corpse, abuse of police powers and breach of a memorandum of understanding.

The petition also names HRH Eze Lambert Unuoha, traditional ruler of Nma 1 of Obioma Autonomous Community in Ngor Okpala, as a respondent.

Addressing the parties, the committee chairman, who was represented by his deputy, Rep. Matthew Nwogu, directed that no further activity should take place on the disputed land until the matter was resolved through the committee or other appropriate means.

“There are orders that no more actions on this land until this matter is resolved,” the chairman said.

“Either through this place, or through which other means you want to resolve it. That’s the first order. No more putting up caterpillars or bulldozers in that land.”

He said the committee had contacted the Department of State Services (DSS) and the police, which, according to him, denied supplying firearms to the men allegedly operating in the community.

“All the boys that are armed in that village should be disarmed. Because we have made contact with the DSS. They said they didn’t give them the gun. The police said they didn’t,” he said.

The chairman said the directives were intended to prevent further escalation while the committee examined the allegations.

The hearing featured disagreements among lawyers representing the parties over the status of a pending court case and whether the committee should continue considering the petition.

Counsel to Charles Farms Limited, identified during the proceedings as one of the parties involved in the dispute, told the committee that his clients had legally acquired the land and paid the relevant parties.

He rejected the allegations in the petition and disclosed that his clients had instituted legal proceedings against the petitioners.

According to him, he wrote to the committee on September 28, 2026, explaining his clients’ position and providing details of the court proceedings.

He, however, acknowledged that he had not brought the supporting court documents to the hearing.

The committee chairman said a letter and oral explanations were insufficient, demanding certified documentary evidence to establish the status of the case.

The lawyer subsequently undertook to organise the documents he had received, certify the necessary papers and submit them to the committee.

A committee member, intervening in the exchange, cautioned against allowing the existence of a court case to automatically terminate the legislative investigation.

He said the committee had a constitutional responsibility to consider petitions submitted to it, adding that the scope of the court proceedings would have to be examined before determining whether they covered all the issues raised in the petition.

“That a matter is in court does not immediately stop us from doing our duty. This is a constitutional committee. One of the very few committees written into the Nigerian constitution,” the lawmaker said.

He urged the parties to respect the committee’s procedures and allow the petitioners an opportunity to present their grievances.

“Tomorrow he might be the one petitioning this National Assembly over an issue. So let us respect processes, respect our constitution. And then respect the will of the people who have come here to seek justice,” he added.

The lawmaker also urged the committee to give the respondents time to file formal responses, noting that the proceedings would benefit from documentary evidence from both sides.

Petitioners allege intimidation of villagers

Counsel to the petitioners, Dr Julius Onyemi, told the committee that efforts had been made to resolve the dispute before the matter was brought before the House.

He said the first petition was submitted on July 17, 2026, followed by another on August 14 and a subsequent petition later that month.

Onyemi alleged that he had made several attempts to contact the respondents to resolve the dispute with the community but was unsuccessful.

He further alleged that the court action was initiated after the petitions had been submitted to the House and suggested that it was intended to frustrate the committee’s proceedings.

The lawyer also accused the respondents of using security personnel and armed men to intimidate residents and prevent them from accessing their community.

He urged the committee to ensure that the alleged intimidation stopped while the petition was being considered.

Onyemi questioned the circumstances surrounding the land acquisition and called on the parties to demonstrate compliance with customary land acquisition procedures.

He also raised concerns about the environmental implications of the proposed development, asking whether an environmental impact assessment had been conducted and made available to the community.

The lawyer argued that residents had a right to be consulted over activities that could affect their land and environment.

The respondents’ representatives disputed the allegations, maintaining that the land had been legally acquired. The claims remain subject to the committee’s investigation.

Committee demands video evidence

During the hearing, one of the respondents’ representatives challenged claims that armed men had visited the community and threatened residents.

He said he had been in the area since Monday and disputed claims that he was present at the location where the alleged incident occurred.

He offered to provide his flight itinerary and hotel booking details to support his account.

The chairman subsequently asked the parties to provide any available video or photographic evidence to establish what happened.

He said the committee was interested in examining the available evidence rather than relying solely on conflicting oral accounts.

The chairman reiterated that further development on the disputed land must stop and that armed men allegedly involved in intimidating residents must be disarmed.

The committee adjourned the matter until November 2026 to allow the respondents to study the petition, prepare their formal responses and submit the necessary documentary evidence.

The hearing formed part of the committee’s consideration of the petition seeking intervention over the disputed land in Umundoche community, Imo State.

The allegations have not been established as findings of fact. The respondents maintain that the land was legally acquired, while the committee is yet to conclude its investigation.

World.title: 2027: Accreditation, collation won’t be fully automated – INEC
World.content:
…Says Nigerians, not AI, will determine election outcomes

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has assured Nigerians that voter accreditation and result collation will not be fully automated in the 2027 general elections, insisting that citizens, not Artificial Intelligence AI, will determine the outcome.

Chairman of the Commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN said on Wednesday that “Algorithms will not, and must never, decide the 2027 vote.”

INEC in its Wednesday Bulletin said Amupitan spoke in Abuja while delivering the keynote address at the Artificial Intelligence and Democracy Forum 2026, held in collaboration with Yiaga Africa.

Amupitan said, as a foundational policy, no critical electoral decision, result collation, voter accreditation or candidate qualification would ever be fully automated or delegated to an autonomous system.

“Human accountability, statutory oversight and judicial review will remain paramount at every stage of the electoral chain,” he said.

Responding to the forum’s opening question, “Will Algorithms Decide the 2027 Vote?”, he said the answer was an unequivocal no. According to him, the choice of who leads Nigeria belongs exclusively to the Nigerian people.

The chairman said the forum was taking place 92 days before the general elections, in a digital landscape that had shifted significantly since 2023.

He warned that the Commission was no longer dealing only with the “analogue” challenges of logistics but with a world in which AI can influence what a voter sees, how the voter thinks and how the voter trusts.

“The greatest threat we face is not the hacking of a ballot box, but the hacking of the voter’s mind,” Amupitan stated.

He said generative AI had reduced to near zero the cost of producing convincing deepfakes, including videos of candidates saying things they never said and of INEC officials giving false instructions.

“If a voter cannot distinguish between truth and a synthetic lie, the foundation of informed consent crumbles,” he said.

The INEC chairman warned that a well-timed deepfake video or cloned audio recording of a candidate, an election official or a security chief could announce a false candidate withdrawal, a postponement of the election or inflammatory ethnoreligious statements, and spread virally within minutes.

He added that malicious actors could also impersonate the INEC Chairman, Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs and other officials to issue fake guidelines, declare unauthorised results or instruct voters to stay home.

On the Commission’s response, Amupitan disclosed that INEC had created an AI Unit within its Information and Communication Technology ICT Directorate, equipped with real-time digital monitoring tools, deepfake detection software and data analytics expertise.

He said any AI tool or automated system deployed by the Commission for logistics, database management or operational support must undergo rigorous audits to guarantee explainability, fairness and security before deployment.

The Commission, he added, was working on a Digital Strategy to audit the information environment and partnering with technology platforms for the rapid debunking and labelling of AI-generated content touching on electoral processes.

Amupitan called on technology companies, including Meta, X, Google, TikTok and Telegram, to rapidly restrict unlabelled synthetic media impersonating election officials, candidates or security personnel.

He also asked them to enforce disclaimers on political s and restrict micro-targeting based on ethnicity, religion or local origin.

He urged political parties and candidates to sign an Ethical AI Code of Conduct, committing to refrain from deploying deepfakes, synthetic impersonation, dark ads or automated botnets.

The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission does not view AI only through the prism of risk. He described it as a powerful force multiplier for administrative precision, predictive planning and institutional integrity.

He said while human collation remained the statutory standard for declaring results, AI could run parallel statistical audits on polling unit result sheets uploaded through the eEC8A, flagging mathematical inconsistencies, atypical entry patterns and image quality defects for administrative review.

On logistics, he said AI-driven geospatial analytics could help INEC deploy ad-hoc staff, vehicles, boats and sensitive materials to 176,846 polling units before 7:30 a.m. on election day.

Amupitan said the 2027 General Election would be the largest democratic exercise on the African continent, involving over 103 million registered voters across 774 Local Government Areas LGAs. He said 10 of the 14 major operational milestones under the Electoral Act 2026 had been successfully executed.

The two-day forum was attended by the Chairperson of the Economic Community of West African States Network of Electoral Commissions ECONEC and Chairman of the Senegal Electoral Commission, Mr Abdoulaye Sylla, along with National Commissioners, RECs, political party leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies, technology firms and the media.

Amupitan said algorithms had no moral compass, no civic duty and no constitutional oath. “They do not have a conscience, they do not have a country, and they do not have a vote. INEC’s job is to ensure that the voice of the people is heard clearly, above the noise of the machines.

“On election day in 2027, it will be the thumbprint of the Nigerian citizen, guided by their own will and their own hopes, that decides our future,” Amupitan said.

World.title: ADC accuses APC of coercing opposition governors into campaign council
World.content:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of coercing opposition governors into its presidential campaign council, alleging that the ruling party is undermining Nigeria’s multiparty democracy ahead of the 2027 general election.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council’s Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, made the allegation in a statement reacting to the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council in Abuja on Wednesday.

Ologbondiyan accused the ruling party of using state power to pressure opposition governors into its fold or include them in its campaign structure despite their continued membership of other political parties.

“What we are witnessing is not politics but political abduction. You cannot claim to be a democrat while using state power to force opposition governors into your party and then drafting them into your campaign council. This is political banditry,” he said.

The ADC spokesman also alleged that the APC was pursuing a political agenda aimed at concentrating power in the hands of one individual, claiming that national institutions, security agencies and the judiciary were being deployed to weaken opposition forces.

He urged Nigerians to resist what he described as an attempt to establish an immoral political order driven by the desire to retain power at the expense of citizens’ welfare.

Ologbondiyan further accused the ruling party of neglecting the economic hardship, hunger and insecurity confronting Nigerians while focusing on its political interests.

“These particular sets of leaders don’t care about the current conditions of the people but how best to remain in power at a time when average Nigerians find it difficult to eat and be secure,” he said.

He also alleged that the country’s democratic space was shrinking, citing what he described as the suppression of dissenting voices, harassment of opposition figures and the weakening of democratic institutions for partisan purposes.

“Never in our democratic journey have we witnessed this level of intolerance and desperation. The APC government has weaponised poverty, hunger and insecurity to subjugate Nigerians and cripple the opposition,” Ologbondiyan said.

He added that the situation was inconsistent with the democratic ideals for which late politician Moshood Abiola and other pro-democracy figures fought.

The ADC spokesman also promoted the party’s presidential ticket of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi, describing them as having the experience and democratic credentials to address the country’s challenges.

“Atiku Abubakar is a democrat to the core. He has the national spread, the capacity and the will to reunite Nigeria and restore our battered democracy,” he said.

The ADC Presidential Campaign Council called on Nigerians, media organisations, civil society groups and the international community to oppose what it described as the APC’s anti-democratic agenda and support efforts to protect multiparty democracy.

World.title: Transcorp Group Advocates Investment in Girls’ Rights
World.content:
Transnational Corporation Plc, through its power subsidiaries, Transcorp Power Plc, Ughelli, and Transafam Power Limited, Afam, hosted girls from Transcorp Power School, Ughelli, and Transafam Power Schools, Afam, to advocate for investment in girls’ rights as the world commemorates the 2026 International Day of the Girl Child. In line with this year’s theme,

“End Child Marriage and Invest in Girls’ Rights”, the session linked girls’ rights to education, confidence, ambition, leadership, and opportunity. Around the world, about one in five girls is married before her 18th birthday. West and Central Africa is described as the global centre of child marriage, with nearly 60 million women and girls in the region married as children, and Nigeria accounts for the largest share. An earlier United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (UNICEF) estimate put the country’s number of child brides at about 22 million. For each of these girls, early marriage too often means an end to schooling, risky early pregnancy, and a future decided by others. Speaking during the session, President/Group Chief Executive Officer of Transcorp Group,

Owen D. Omogiafo, OON, told the girls that there is no limit to what they can achieve. Drawing on her own journey, she shared that she was not born with a silver spoon but rose to lead one of Africa’s foremost business groups through tenacity, focus and determination. “You are not too young to have a voice, and you are not too young to have a dream. Nobody should decide your future for you. You have a right to choose your own path, so start painting the portrait of where you want to be in the future; and then work hard to get there.”

World.title: NSCIA Felicitates CAN at 50, Says Milestone Important for Nigeria
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA), led by its President-General and Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar has felicitated the leadership of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) and the entire Christian community in Nigeria on the occasion of the Association’s 50th anniversary.

In a statement y by its Secretary-General, Prof. Is-haq Oloyede, NSCIA said it regarded the 50th anniversary of CAN as a significant milestone not only for the Christian community but also for the Nigerian nation.

The Council noted that while the nation had

transited through various challenges and difficult moments, religious leaders and institutions had continued to play crucial role in promoting peace, dialogue, mutual understanding and peaceful coexistence among the diverse peoples and faith communities of the country.

The NSCIA maintained that it recognised the importance of the relationship between Muslims and Christians in Nigeria,

noting that the two communities constituted the overwhelming majority of the Nigerian population and shared a common responsibility to promote peace, entrench justice, advance security, contribute to responsible citizenship and the development of the country.

“The challenges confronting our nation, particularly injustice, insecurity, poverty, unemployment, social inequality and the need for accountable and responsive governance, require the collective efforts of all Nigerians.

“It is in this regard that the NSCIA attaches great importance to sustained inter-faith dialogue and cooperation. The Council particularly appreciates the platforms that have enabled leaders of the two faith communities to engage constructively on issues affecting the peace, unity and development of Nigeria, including the Nigeria Inter-Religious Council (NIREC),” NSCIA said.

It described the 50th anniversary of CAN as an opportunity to reflect on the responsibility of religious leadership in strengthening national unity and promoting peaceful coexistence.

The Council stressed that it believed that religious differences should never be allowed to become sources of division, hatred or violence, noting that respective faiths should continue to inspire the nation towards justice, compassion, peaceful coexistence and service to humanity.

NSCIA congratulated the President of CAN, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, the National Executive Committee (NEC), the various Christian denominations and associations under its umbrella as well as Christians across the 36 states of the federation and the FCT on the

golden milestone and wished the association greater wisdom in the discharge of its onerous national and sacred responsibilities.

World.title: Nigeria’s Sacrifices for Peace in Sierra Leone Will Never Be Forgotten, Says Former VP
World.content:
*Calls for Africa’s Economic Independence

Linus Aleke in Abuja

Former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Samuel Sam-Sumana, has expressed profound gratitude to Nigeria for its sacrifices in restoring peace to his country, saying the contributions of Nigerian troops will remain indelible in Sierra Leone’s history.

The former Vice-President also called for Africa’s economic independence to discourage young people from migrating to Europe and America in search of better opportunities and living conditions, often at the risk of their lives, owing to a lack of opportunities at home.

Sam-Sumana made these remarks when the leadership of the Defence Correspondents Association of Nigeria (DECAN) paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja.

He said Nigeria had played a pivotal role in supporting Sierra Leone during its conflict by providing troops and other forms of assistance that helped restore peace and stability.

He acknowledged that military personnel and civilians had paid the ultimate price in the struggle, stressing the need to ensure that their sacrifices were never forgotten.

“As a Sierra Leonean, I wish to express my profound gratitude for the role Nigeria and other countries played in helping Sierra Leone regain peace and stability,” he said.

The former Vice-President described Nigeria as a big brother in West Africa, stressing that the country’s stability and prosperity had far-reaching implications for the subregion.

“When Nigeria catches a cold, the rest of us sneeze,” he said, underscoring the interconnectedness of West African countries.

Sam-Sumana also urged DECAN to sustain its engagement with the military and strengthen professional cooperation between defence correspondents and security institutions.

He described journalists as indispensable partners in governance, accountability and national development, warning against the tendency of political leaders to regard critical reporting as an act of hostility.

“Constructive criticism is essential to improving public institutions and ensuring that those entrusted with public responsibilities remain accountable,” he said.

According to him, public officials should not fear criticism when it is fair, accurate and intended to promote the greater public good.

Reflecting on Sierra Leone’s civil war, Sam-Sumana said the conflict, influenced by the spillover of the war in neighbouring Liberia and competing interests in diamond resources, had resulted in enormous losses of lives and property.

He said the painful experience should strengthen collective efforts to prevent the recurrence of violent conflicts across West Africa.

“We must never forget those experiences. Rather, we should use them to strengthen our collective commitment to peace and prevent similar tragedies in the subregion,” he said.

Sam-Sumana further cautioned political leaders against allowing personal ambition to undermine national stability, insisting that peaceful political competition remained essential to democratic development.

He said peace was a collective victory that transcended political parties and individual ambitions.

On Africa’s development, the former Vice-President called for a fundamental shift from dependence on foreign assistance towards mutually beneficial partnerships, industrialisation and greater economic self-reliance.

He argued that African countries must move beyond exporting raw materials and importing finished products by investing in local industries, adding value to natural resources and creating employment opportunities for young people.

Sam-Sumana said the continent’s inability to harness its vast resources fully had contributed to economic hardship and forced migration, including dangerous journeys across the Mediterranean Sea.

In his remarks, DECAN President, Mr Odita Sunday, said the courtesy visit was intended to express the association’s appreciation to Sam-Sumana for accepting its invitation and participating in the DECAN Conference and Awards 2026.

World.title: APDC MD Explains How FCT Residents Can Access Homes Through Mortgages
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The Acting Managing Director of Abuja Property Development Company (APDC) Akeem Aderogba has shed light on how residents of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), particularly civil servants and low- and middle-income earners, can benefit from mortgage facilities to acquire homes without paying the full cost upfront.

He made the clarification Wednesday at the 20th anniversary symposium of APDC held in Abuja

Aderogba said the mortgage arrangement allowed prospective homeowners to pay an initial deposit of between 10 and 20 per cent of the cost of a house, while the outstanding balance is financed through mortgage institutions, making homeownership more accessible to residents.

Speaking on APDC’s efforts to address the housing deficit in the FCT, he said the initiative was designed to ease the financial burden on prospective homeowners who might not have the resources to pay for a house in a single transaction.

He explained that through mortgage financing, beneficiaries could secure their homes after paying the required deposit, with the balance spread over an agreed repayment period.

“For us, we take these issues into consideration before arriving at the prices of our houses. You do not need to look for all the money before you can move in. You can deposit maybe 10 to 20 per cent, and the balance will be financed by the mortgage institutions,” he said.

He disclosed that APDC had also collaborated with the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria through the National Housing Fund (NHF) to provide civil servants with access to affordable housing.

According to him, the arrangement, alongside support from the Federal Government Housing Board, enables eligible civil servants to access homes by facilitating payment of the outstanding balance to APDC.

He said the initiative was particularly beneficial to civil servants, who could otherwise find it difficult to raise the full cost of acquiring a house amid rising construction costs and inflation.

The acting MD noted that APDC had continued to expand its housing developments to help bridge the housing deficit in the FCT, adding that its estates were designed to serve different categories of residents, including low- and middle-income earners.

He disclosed that the organisation’s estates covered about 50 hectares of land, with more than 800 families moving into the development, while additional projects were expected to accommodate hundreds of other households.

Among the projects, he said, were Abuja APDC Homes in Karsana, expected to accommodate at least 200 families, and another development at APDC Homes, Ido Gwari, in Life Camp, projected to provide housing for at least 150 households.

He, however, identified the rising cost of building materials and infrastructure as major challenges affecting housing affordability and the timely completion of some developments.

He explained that the increasing prices of cement, sand and other construction materials, alongside the rising cost of infrastructure, had significantly increased the cost of housing development.

He urged the government to support housing developers by providing land and essential infrastructure, noting that infrastructure accounts for between 30 and 40 per cent of the total cost of housing development.

According to him, government intervention in infrastructure provision would reduce development costs and enable developers to offer homes at more affordable prices, particularly to civil servants and other residents of the FCT.

In her remarks the Group Managing Director Abuja Investments Company Limited (AICL) Amb. Maureen Tamuno, said APDC had operated for the past two decades as a subsidiary of AICL.

She said that APDC’s role of expanding housing opportunities remains critical because a house is the most important investment of a lifetime for ordinary citizens and households.

World.title: Falana Urges States to Utilise N267bn UBEC Funds for Basic Education
World.content:
Human rights lawyer, Femi Falana (SAN), has called on governors of the 36 states and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to utilise N267 billion in released intervention funds for basic education and access over N65 billion in counterpart funding yet to be accessed by states.

Falana, who is the Chair of the Alliance on Surviving Covid 19 and Beyond (ASCAB), made the call in a statement titled “Abandonment of Primary School Education for the Children of the Poor.”

He said the Universal Basic Education Commission (UBEC) revealed that as of August this year, about N267 billion in released intervention funds was yet to be utilised, while over N65 billion counterpart funding was yet to be accessed by states.

The Executive Secretary of UBEC, Dr. Aisha Garba, made the disclosure at the opening of a month-long technical capacity-building workshop organised by the World Bank-assisted HOPE-GOV Programme in Abuja.

The workshop is aimed at strengthening budget planning and execution for basic education and primary healthcare in the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

Falana recalled that on November 28, 2025, the Federal High Court ruled in the case of Femi Falana & Anor v Attorney-General of the Federation & 36 Ors (Suit No. FHC/L/CS/142/24) that the Federal Government, all 36 state governments and the FCT have a binding legal obligation to provide free, compulsory and universal basic education for every Nigerian child of primary and junior secondary school age.

“In spite of the clear terms of the above judgment,” he said, the funds meant for basic education remained unutilised or unaccessed.

“As a matter of urgency, the governors of the 36 states and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory should utilise the N267 billion in released intervention funds and access the over N65 billion counterpart funding in the UBEC Account,” he said.

Falana urged the authorities to “perform their statutory duties and respect the right of every Nigerian child to free and compulsory basic education from primary school to junior secondary school guaranteed by the Free, Compulsory Universal Basic Education Act.”

He also called on the Federal Government to provide a meal for schoolchildren per day to boost enrolment and nutrition in line with the National Social Investment Programme Agency Act.

“In view of the ongoing political campaigns, we call on the mass media to challenge all registered political parties and their candidates to bring out their programmes with respect to the implementation of the relevant laws on free and compulsory basic education for every child in Nigeria as well as the school feeding programme,” he said.

Falana added that, “Having regard to the enormous resources of the country, the removal of children of school age from the streets in all states of the Federation and the Federal Capital Territory must be carried out without any further delay.”

World.title: Makinde Demands Audit of N15trn Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway
World.content:
Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has demanded a comprehensive audit of the N15 trillion Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway project, accusing the Federal Government of raising fresh questions about its planning, procurement and cost following the recent realignment of the route.

It further said Nigerians deserved to know why the route was changed, how much had been spent and whether the Federal Government would reduce the contract sum, warning that the controversy had deepened concerns over accountability in the handling of public funds.

Briefing newsmen, APM Director-General, Felix Hassan Hyat, also urged Nigerians to reject President Bola Tinubu in 2027 and support Seyi Makinde, the presidential candidate of the Allied People’s Movement, APM.

Hyat faulted the explanation by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, that climate change and environmental challenges necessitated the realignment, arguing that the development raised questions about whether adequate technical and environmental assessments had been conducted before the project was awarded.

“The vague reasons of climate change and environmental challenges adduced by Minister Umahi at this point, beg the question,” Hyat said.

The organisation also alleged that the contract was awarded in 2024 without an approved engineering design, an open and competitive bidding process or budgetary provision and statutory appropriation by the National Assembly.

It further questioned the relationship between the contractor’s corporate group and another firm whose board allegedly includes individuals linked to the Presidency, raising concerns about possible conflicts of interest.

The group also alleged that the project was designed as a conduit for financing the All Progressives Congress’ election expenses. The statement provided no supporting evidence for the allegation.

Demanding full disclosure, the organisation called for the publication of procurement and payment records, an independent engineering assessment of the Ondo realignment and a comprehensive audit of the project’s total cost, expenditure to date and execution plan.

“We demand that the President Tinubu-led government should publish the relevant engineering assessment, alternative-route analysis, accompanying cost implications and comprehensive audit of the work and amount so far spent,” the organisation said.

It maintained that it was not opposed to road construction but questioned the priority given to the coastal highway while several existing federal roads remained in poor condition.

“Nigeria is in dire need of infrastructure, no doubt, but not opaque contracts and expensive excuses!” Hyat declared.

The organisation urged Nigerians to vote against the President in 2027 and rally behind Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA agenda.

It described Makinde as an alternative capable of building consensus across party and regional divides, insisting that the country’s future should take precedence over the President’s political ambition.

“The future of Nigeria must take precedence over President Tinubu’s personal ambition,” Hyat said.

World.title: FG Launches D30 Platform to Unlock Nigeria’s Creative Economy Potential
World.content:
Olawale Ajimotokan in Abuja

The federal government has taken a bold step towards unlocking the economic potential of the creative and tourism industries by launching the D30 Platform (Destination 2030) to strengthen access to sectoral data, research, mapping and economic intelligence.

Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy Hannatu Musa Musawa, said the platform will provide a more structured understanding of Nigeria’s creative and tourism assets, helping government institutions, investors and entrepreneurs identify opportunities, address industry challenges and make better-informed decisions.

She emphasized that the launch of D30 aligned with the ministry’s broader strategic ambition to generate more than three million jobs and contribute $100 billion to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product by 2030.

According to her, achieving these targets would require sustained investment, effective policies, improved infrastructure and stronger collaboration between government and private-sector stakeholders.

She stressed the need to move beyond recognising the country’s creative potential to systematically measuring, understanding and developing its economic value.

The minister enunciated several challenges facing the sectors, including the absence of sufficiently reliable, accessible and comprehensive data to establish the scale of opportunities available, identify infrastructure gaps and guide investment decisions.

She explained that the D30 Platform is designed to help address this challenge by bringing relevant information together to support more coordinated planning and economic development.

She said improved access to such intelligence could also contribute to a more transparent and predictable investment environment, encouraging greater private-sector participation in Nigeria’s creative and tourism economy.

The minister highlighted the importance of participation by government agencies, the National Bureau of Statistics, state governments, industry associations, private-sector operators and research institutions.

She stated that through collaboration, the platform could help reduce information gaps, improve the quality of sectoral intelligence and support more coordinated policy decisions.

Musawa acknowledged its technology development partner, Cavista Holdings, led by its Vice President, Olumide Olayomi for its role in developing the platform and project team who contributed to bringing the initiative to launch.

In his remarks, Olayomi said Cavista committed private funding and technical expertise to build D30 in partnership with the ministry.

“We saw an opportunity to contribute to an important national priority by providing an essential digital foundation for the sector’s development. D30 brings together information on creative and cultural industries, tourism infrastructure and sector intervention,” he said.

World.title: G27 Questions Mbah’s 2023, 2027 INEC Credentials, Defends Nnaji
World.content:
The G27 for Uche Nnaji support group has questioned the alleged decision of Governor Peter Mbah to submit a Senior School Certificate Examination (WAEC) certificate as his highest educational qualification to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The group made its position known in a statement signed by its spokesman, Chief James Ogbodo, in reaction to a publication questioning why Chief Uche Nnaji submitted his WAEC certificate as his highest qualification to INEC.

Chief Uche Nnaji is the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State for the 2027 election. His name is also among the candidates contained in the final list recently published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the Enugu State governorship election.

G27 described the publication as an attempt to shift attention from questions surrounding the qualifications Governor Mbah submitted to INEC during the 2023 general election.

According to the group, the governor should first address questions concerning the consistency of the qualifications he presented to INEC before questioning another candidate’s choice of credentials.

The group alleged that during the 2023 election, Mbah reportedly presented a Law degree as his highest qualification, alongside an NYSC discharge certificate. It further recalled the controversy that subsequently surrounded the authenticity of the NYSC document, noting that the matter has been disputed by relevant parties.

G27 therefore questioned why the governor chose to present WAEC as his highest qualification for the 2027 election rather than retain the same academic qualification he presented to INEC in 2023.

The group said the change had raised questions that, in its view, required clarification from the governor and the relevant institutions.

“Before asking Chief Uche Nnaji why he chose to submit his WAEC certificate, Governor Peter Mbah should explain why the qualification he presented to INEC in 2023 is different from the qualification he is presenting in 2027,” the group said.

G27 further argued that the controversy surrounding the NYSC document remains an issue that should be addressed through appropriate legal and institutional channels. It alleged that the matter was compounded by an oath concerning the disputed certificate, adding that the governor should clarify the circumstances surrounding the document and the declarations made concerning it.

The group stressed that its position was not intended to prevent scrutiny of any political candidate, saying that all public officials and candidates should be prepared to answer legitimate questions about credentials submitted to electoral authorities.

The group also responded to comments attributed to Mr. Daniel, who reportedly questioned Nnaji’s academic credentials while presenting himself as a first-class journalism graduate.

G27 said academic distinction should ordinarily be reflected in the quality of journalism produced by its holder, arguing that responsible journalism requires independent verification rather than hurried reproduction of allegations.

“A first-class degree should ordinarily produce first-class journalism; not a hurried copy-and-paste report built on recycled claims,” the group said.

It urged journalists and media organisations to independently verify allegations concerning candidates, particularly when such allegations involve academic records, court proceedings and official documents.

According to G27, Nnaji contested the 2023 election with the same basic academic credential he is presenting for the 2027 election.

The group said Nnaji’s reliance on his WAEC certificate should not, in itself, be treated as evidence of wrongdoing, noting that WAEC remains a recognised qualification.

G27 also dismissed suggestions that Nnaji’s interest in the governorship was primarily motivated by the desire to obtain constitutional immunity.

The group described the allegation as unfounded, maintaining that Nnaji’s stated political objective was to address what it described as economic hardship, taxation concerns, unemployment and inadequate industrial development in Enugu State.

It said Nnaji’s agenda was focused on rebuilding the state’s economy, attracting investment, promoting industrialisation and creating employment opportunities, particularly for young people.

The group said these policy questions should form part of the substantive debate ahead of the 2027 election rather than allowing political discourse to be dominated by personal attacks and disputed credential controversies.

G27 also took exception to what it described as a misrepresentation of Nnaji’s court action concerning his academic records.

According to the group, Nnaji did not admit that he had never received his university degree certificate, as allegedly suggested in the publication.

Rather, the group maintained that the substance of the complaint concerned the university’s failure to release his academic transcript.

G27 said the distinction was fundamental because a degree certificate and an academic transcript are separate academic records serving different purposes.

It therefore urged journalists reporting on the matter to obtain and examine the actual court processes before drawing conclusions about what Nnaji did or did not admit.

“A journalist has a duty to verify such a fundamental distinction before rushing to publication,” the group said.

The group maintained that Nnaji’s decision to seek judicial clarification was motivated by his desire to protect his reputation and establish the facts surrounding his academic records.

According to G27, “a good name is a legacy that belongs not only to a man but also to his children and generations yet unborn.”

The support group called for a fact-based political debate ahead of the 2027 elections, saying that candidates should be judged on their records, policies, qualifications and capacity to govern rather than through unverified allegations or personal attacks.

World.title: ‘A star is needed here in Naturena’: Moloisane on Kaizer Chiefs’ trophy target
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Thabo Moloisane has set his sights on winning trophies and helping Amakhosi end their long wait for league glory following his arrival at Naturena in July.

The 26-year-old was one of five new signings brought in ahead of the season and has already featured in the majority of the club’s matches.

Speaking ahead of Chiefs’ clash against Stellenbosch FC on Tuesday, Moloisane made it clear that winning silverware is a major priority in his first season with the Soweto giants.



The defender believes Amakhosi have an opportunity to challenge for the league title and is determined to play his part in ending the club’s lengthy wait for another Premiership crown.

“A star, guys, it is needed here at home. We have an opportunity to see if we can do it this season, and the league, of course. It is one thing that has gone past us for a long time and, for me, in my first season, I just want to get as many trophies as I can. That’s where the ambition is, and the rest can follow,” he said.

Kaizer Chiefs last won the league title in the 2014/15 season, and Moloisane is eager to help restore the club’s status as one of South African football’s leading forces.

Beyond his ambitions at club level, the defender is also hoping to work his way back into the Bafana Bafana setup.

Kaizer Chiefs star wants Bafana return

Moloisane acknowledged that returning to the national team will not be easy, given the competition for places, but believes hard work and consistent performances at a high-profile club like Kaizer Chiefs could improve his chances.

“We should give credit to the guys, you know. I was speaking to Mdu (Shabalala) last week, saying the line is long to get back into Bafana, but at the same time, I’m at a big institution watched by everyone. For me, it’s just to continue working hard. The journey is still long,” he told media.



For Moloisane, the immediate focus remains on delivering for Amakhosi and helping the club compete for honours, while keeping his hopes of a Bafana Bafana recall alive.

Will he win a star?

World.title: ‘Spirit of lust’: Bernard Parker hints at struggles?
World.content:
Bernard Parker has reposted several telling Instagram posts, hinting at infidelity, lust and a “miserable marriage”. This comes as the former Bafana and Kaizer Chiefs player – now coach of TS Galaxy – announced his split from his baby mama, Kacha Stepanovic, in a social media post.

The 40-year-old has not disclosed when or why he separated from his wife, Wendy Parker, whom he married in 2012.

BERNARD PARKER’S CRYPTIC REPOSTS

On his Instagram account, Bernard Parker has reposted several telling faith-based Reels about men who seemingly struggle with monogamy.



One was about “the spirit of lust” and featured a preacher warning Christians about “sex with demons”. Others were warnings about lust and “staying away from bad women”

Another was a segment of a message from a preacher, which was titled: “What to do when your marriage is miserable”. A different message featured another preacher calling on individuals to ask their families and partners for forgiveness after “destroying” a marriage.

‘PERSONAL ADDICTIONS’

In his statement posted on Monday, 12 October, Bernard Parker alluded to being unfaithful to his former partner, Kacha Stepanovic, who is allegedly the mother of his baby daughter.

He shared: “I want to be honest about my part in our journey. I have made mistakes and struggled with personal addictions that have affected my life and the people I love.

“Kacha, I’m truly sorry for the times I hurt you, let you down, and caused you pain. You gave me love, support, patience and kindness that I’ve never received before. I take responsibility for my mistakes, knowing that some things cannot simply be undone with an apology”

On her social media account, Kacha Stepanovic reposted Bernard Parker’s statement.



She also hinted at his alleged infidelity.

She shared on her IG Stories: “Lust and addiction will strip you of your family, your work, your name and everything you built.

“If betrayal was so easy, the devil would be next seated at the throne. Make sure whatever you do is worth losing it all”.

World.title: SASSA announces ALL payment dates for November 2026 cycle
World.content:
The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) has released revised social grant payment dates for November 2026, moving the cycle forward ahead of the upcoming Local Government Elections.

The agency announced the new schedule in a media statement on Wednesday, 14 October, confirming that older persons will receive their grants before the end of October.

According to SASSA, grants will be paid as follows:



Older Persons Grant: Friday, 30 October 2026

Friday, 30 October 2026 Disability Grant: Monday, 2 November 2026

Monday, 2 November 2026 Children’s Grants: Tuesday, 3 November 2026

Tuesday, 3 November 2026 Grants under review: Thursday, 5 November 2026

The Older Persons Grant payment falls in October but forms part of the November payment cycle.

SASSA said the revised schedule follows “extensive consultations between SASSA and various stakeholders” to keep grant payments running “efficiently, securely and with minimal disruption during the election period.”

National Treasury approved the revised dates after these engagements, clearing the way for the new schedule.

“The Agency remains committed to ensuring that eligible beneficiaries receive their grants in an orderly and reliable manner,” SASSA said.

The agency added that the adjustment aims to support the smooth administration of payments in the period surrounding the elections.

SASSA urges grant recipients under review to respond

SASSA reminded beneficiaries whose grants are under review to respond to official communication from the agency and attend review appointments when requested.



The agency said the fourth-day payment on 5 November “is specifically intended for beneficiaries whose grants fall within the review process.”

SASSA also urged grant recipients not to rush to its offices unnecessarily, as payments will be processed according to the announced schedule.

The agency encouraged beneficiaries to rely on its official communication channels for accurate information and to guard against misinformation and disinformation about social grants.

“SASSA remains committed to safeguarding the integrity of the social assistance system while ensuring continued access to social grants for millions of South Africans who depend on this vital support,” the agency said.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Jacob Zuma health latest: MK Party pulls plug on major event
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma remains in hospital as the MK Party cancels its election manifesto launch scheduled for Sunday, 18 October. Image: X/Gagasi FM

The uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) Party has cancelled its election manifesto launch as former president Jacob Zuma remains in hospital, while his foundation has accused the media of persecuting him over repeated enquiries about his condition.

MK Party parliamentary leader John Hlophe conceded that cancelling Sunday’s planned launch in Mbombela, Mpumalanga, was necessary.

The decision comes as the 84-year-old party president continues receiving medical care at Netcare St Anne’s Hospital in Pietermaritzburg.



Meanwhile, Jacob Zuma Foundation spokesperson Mzwanele Manyi has lashed out at journalists, accusing them of invading the former president’s privacy.

MANYI WARNS MEDIA OVER ZUMA HEALTH ENQUIRIES

In a statement on Wednesday, 14 October, Manyi said the foundation would no longer entertain constant requests for updates.

“The Foundation will not be giving a minute by minute update on H.E President Zuma,” he said.



“You are requested to afford President Zuma PRIVACY and DIGNITY he deserves.

“The permanent enquiries are not appreciated. We see it as PERSECUTION & INVASION of privacy.”

Dear Media



The Foundation will not be giving a minute by minute update on H.E President Zuma.

You are requested to afford President Zuma PRIVACY and DIGNITY he deserves.

The permanent enquiries are not appreciated. We see it as PERSECUTION & INVASION of privacy.



Mzwanele Manyi  October 14, 2026

The warning follows conflicting reports about Zuma’s discharge from hospital.

Reports on Tuesday suggested that doctors had discharged him on Monday night but advised him to remain in Pietermaritzburg for further observation.

However, Manyi dismissed those reports and confirmed that Zuma remained in hospital.



“Reports that H.E President Zuma has been discharged are NOT true,” he said.

The foundation has not disclosed the nature of Zuma’s illness or indicated when doctors expect to discharge him.

MK PARTY CANCELS MANIFESTO LAUNCH

The MK Party had planned to launch its local government election manifesto at the Siyathatha rally on Sunday, 18 October.



However, the party cancelled the event ahead of the 4 November municipal elections.

Hlophe acknowledged the need to call off the launch following concerns over Zuma’s condition.

WATCH: MK parliamentary leader John Hlophe concedes that it was necessary for the party to cancel its election manifesto launch, which was scheduled for Sunday in Mbombela, Mpumalanga.



This follows reports of party president and former President Jacob Zuma’s ill health. Zuma… pic.twitter.com/6LRcPAezdp  October 14, 2026

In its official announcement, the party said it would instead concentrate on campaigning at ward level and engaging communities.

It plans to distribute its election manifesto electronically to party structures and members on Thursday, 15 October.

The cancellation leaves the party without its planned mass manifesto launch less than three weeks before voters head to the polls.



RAMAPHOSA, MASHATILE WISHED ZUMA WELL

Zuma entered hospital on Tuesday, 6 October, after reportedly falling ill during an election campaign engagement in Msinga, KwaZulu-Natal.

The MK Party initially described his admission as a routine medical examination.

President Cyril Ramaphosa subsequently confirmed that Zuma had been unwell and was receiving treatment under the supervision of doctors.



As previously reported by The South African, Ramaphosa and Deputy President Paul Mashatile wished the former president a speedy recovery.

Manyi has also criticised what he considers unequal media scrutiny of Zuma and Mashatile, questioning why the deputy president’s recent illness did not attract similar attention.

The foundation maintains that Zuma is recovering well but has urged journalists to stop demanding regular medical updates.

World.title: Tides: What beachgoers and anglers can expect along the coast on Thursday
World.content:
Beachgoers and anglers should check Thursday’s tide times before heading to the coast. Image: Unsplash

f you’re heading to the coast on Thursday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Spring tides can cause greater changes in water levels along South Africa’s coastline.

However, tides are only part of the picture. Wind, waves and swell and the shape of the seabed can also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.



When to expect the next spring tide at the coast

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual, changing conditions along the coast.

The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing.

High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides reveal more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Three CIT robbery suspects shot and killed in KZN
World.content:
UMLAZI - Three suspected cash-in-transit robbers have been killed in a shootout with police and private security in Umlazi, KZN.

Initially, police had reported that four suspects were shot and killed, however, this number has since been revised to three by KwaZulu-Natal police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda.

Netshiunda said a manhunt for other suspects involved in this alleged robbery has been launched.

"We know with experience that there are getaway vehicles and there are those who were not at the crime scene. So, we don't know how many of them were at the crime scene, but a manhunt is on for those that we saw, which we are pursuing now," Netshiunda said.

World.title: CheckPoint Podcast | Is South Africa's Middle Class Paying Twice To Survive? Xhanti Payi | 14 October 2026
World.content:
The Hidden Cost Of Paying Privately For Public Services In South Africa

A household can afford to pay its taxes and still find itself buying essential services all over again. The wider consequences reach beyond family budgets.

A salary increase should, in theory, leave a household with more room to breathe. There might be money available to save, improve a home, take a holiday or invest in

a small business. But for many South Africans, additional income does not necessarily translate into greater financial freedom. It may simply create an opportunity to purchase privately what the public system has failed to provide reliably.

Consider the decisions facing a household that relies on a salary to meet its obligations. Parents may pay school fees because they believe a particular school offers their children better opportunities. A family might maintain medical cover for greater certainty about access to healthcare. Private security, backup electricity and dependable internet connectivity can all become regular expenses. These choices differ across households, and public provision is not uniformly inadequate. Yet the underlying question remains: how much income is left for building financial security once essential needs have been met?

This is the often-overlooked cost of unreliable public provision. Citizens contribute through taxation, but some also spend additional money securing alternatives. The result is not necessarily literal double billing for an identical service. It is a second layer of expenditure that can reduce disposable income and leave families more vulnerable when unexpected costs arise.

The issue becomes particularly revealing when transport is considered. A private vehicle is frequently discussed as a lifestyle purchase, but for some workers it is also a practical response to the limited availability, convenience or reliability of alternative transport. Owning a vehicle can offer independence, yet it comes with financing costs, fuel, maintenance and insurance. A household may therefore be spending heavily just to maintain reliable access to work.

Official statistics illustrate how significant transport already is. Statistics South Africa's Income and Expenditure Survey for 2022/23 found that transport accounted for 15.3% of household consumption expenditure, making it the third-largest spending category. The National Household Travel Survey of 2020 also recorded substantial dependence on minibus taxis and long journeys for many public-transport users. These surveys cover different periods, but together they show why transport deserves attention as an economic issue rather than merely a commuting problem.

There is a further complication: the middle class cannot be defined only by a salary band. Two people earning similar incomes may have very different levels of financial security. One could have manageable housing costs and relatively few dependants. The other might support an extended family, service debt and pay privately for several essential services. Their earnings may look similar on paper, while their ability to save or absorb an emergency differs considerably.

Economist Xhanti Payi raises this wider problem in a CheckPoint: The Podcast conversation with Nkepile Mabuse, describing the middle class as an economic shock absorber. It is a useful metaphor because the pressures do not stop with the individual household. When people devote more income to maintaining basic stability, they have less available for other purchases, investment and supporting new enterprises.

This does not mean that every private alternative is evidence of government failure. Families make choices based on preferences, geography, convenience and affordability. Nor does it mean that public services can be improved simply by increasing expenditure. Reliability, management, maintenance and accountability matter as much as budget allocations.

The practical question for policymakers is what improvements would produce the greatest financial relief for households. A reliable transport system could lower commuting expenses. Better-maintained infrastructure could reduce the need for

private backup services. More dependable public institutions could make some household expenditure a matter of genuine choice rather than perceived necessity.

For households, the measure of economic progress cannot be salary growth alone. It must also include how much of that salary remains available after the essential costs of everyday life have been paid. A stronger middle class is not simply one that earns more. It is one that needs to spend less of its income compensating for systems that ought to work.

References:

· CheckPoint: The Podcast, 14 October 2026. Nkepile Mabuse in conversation with economist and strategist Xhanti Payi. Episode transcript.

· Statistics South Africa. *Transport Month: Key Data and Sector Insights* (2025), drawing on the Income and Expenditure Survey 2022/23.

· Statistics South Africa. *National Household Travel Survey 2020*, published 4 March 2021.

Catch up on all CheckPoint Podcast episodes here: ⁠https://www.enca.com/checkpoint-podcast-0
