Neither the state government nor CEGESA had commented in the sources reviewed for this guide. Our report Nuevo León Gave Sanctioned Firm About US$6M covers the contracts in detail.

Neighbouring Tamaulipas says it has no contracts with the listed people or firms, though Treasury says CEGESA won state work there. Its anti-corruption ministry ordered all state agencies to block any registration, award or contract with them, Proceso reported.

The wider exposure comes from geography, because Laredo carries nearly 40 percent of all US-Mexico commercial traffic. Treasury says the cartel’s stronghold sits directly across from Laredo and that it steers public contracts and manipulates regional elections.

What US Law Requires From Investors

Property of the listed people and firms in the United States, or held by any US person, is now blocked. Blocking means freezing, not seizure, so the owner keeps title but nothing can be transferred, withdrawn or dealt in.

A US person who blocks property must report it to OFAC within 10 business days. Rejected transactions need their own report within the same period, with a copy of the original transfer instructions.

Holders of blocked property must also file an annual report with OFAC by 30 September. OFAC publishes a standard form for that report on its website.

Any company owned 50 percent or more by listed persons, alone or together, is blocked too, even if it is not named. Control without that ownership does not trigger automatic blocking, but OFAC urges caution with such firms.

US persons are generally barred from any dealings with blocked persons unless OFAC issues a licence or an exemption applies. OFAC’s notice of 13 October lists no general licence for this action.

OFAC can impose civil penalties on a strict liability basis, so a company can be fined without knowing it broke the rules. Criminal penalties are also possible, and the cartel’s terrorist status adds a separate risk.

Knowingly giving material support to a designated terrorist organisation is a federal crime under section 2339B of the US criminal code. OFAC flagged that risk for all eight cartels and gangs designated as terrorist groups in February 2025.

Non-US companies, including Mexican ones, may not cause US persons to violate sanctions or engage in conduct that evades them. Foreign banks that knowingly handle significant transactions for listed persons risk losing or facing limits on US correspondent accounts.

Practical Checks for Companies With Mexican Partners

OFAC’s March 2025 alert told companies with operations in areas where the designated cartels are active to reassess their compliance controls. Its compliance framework names five components: management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing and auditing, and training.

In practice that starts with screening partners, contractors, landlords and carriers against OFAC’s SDN List, including aliases and addresses. The 13 October entries give locations, company registration numbers and, for the trucking firm Tamex, a US freight carrier code.

Ownership checks matter because unnamed firms owned 50 percent or more by Garza García or his companies are blocked automatically. Construction subcontractors, fuel and propane suppliers, freight carriers and horse-racing businesses match the sectors named in the cartel sanctions.

OFAC treats an effective compliance programme as a factor that can reduce civil penalties after a violation. Records of each screening, decision and escalation help a company show that such a programme worked.

Treasury also pointed to the whistleblower programme of FinCEN, its financial crimes bureau, which can pay awards for tips on sanctions violations. Awards apply when the information leads to penalties above US$1 million.

What It Means for You

For shareholders in US-listed or Mexican companies, the listing affects only dealings with the named people and firms. It does not restrict trade, investment or travel in Nuevo León in general.

A company that finds a match must freeze the property and report it, and most seek legal advice before any further step. Firms that find indirect links, such as a supplier’s subcontractor, can ask OFAC’s compliance hotline for guidance.

Travellers and expats face no new legal duties from this action unless they deal with the named people or firms. Our Monterrey City Guide for Expats and Visitors and Mexico Security and Crime Explained 2026 cover day-to-day safety.

For the investment backdrop, see Mexico Nearshoring Explained: Record FDI, the USMCA Review and What Could Stop It. The cartel sanctions add a compliance task to that picture rather than a ban on doing business.

What Is Not Known

Treasury has not said which candidates or parties allegedly received cartel money, or when. It has not disclosed whether any US assets were actually frozen.

On Wednesday President Claudia Sheinbaum of the left-wing Morena party said Washington had shared no evidence of campaign financing. A day earlier, Hacienda said Mexico’s financial intelligence unit (UIF) had found signs of possible money laundering among some of those named.

How those two positions fit together, and whether Mexico will freeze accounts or bar the firms from public contracts nationwide, is unclear. Whether OFAC will list further Nuevo León companies is also unknown.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do cartel sanctions affect US investors in Nuevo León?

They bar US persons from dealing with the 15 listed people and firms and require their US-held property to be frozen. They do not restrict investment in Nuevo León in general.

What must a company do if it holds blocked property?

It must freeze the property and report it to OFAC within 10 business days. It must also include it in an annual blocked-property report due by 30 September.

Are companies owned by the listed people also blocked?

Yes, any entity owned 50 percent or more by listed persons, alone or together, is blocked even if it is not named. Control without that ownership does not block a firm automatically, but OFAC urges caution.

Can a company be fined for an accidental breach?

Yes, OFAC can impose civil penalties on a strict liability basis, without proof of intent. An effective compliance programme can reduce a penalty.

Did Nuevo León do business with a listed company?

Its border agency Codefront gave CEGESA three contracts worth about US$6 million in 2022 and 2023, according to transparency records. The state government had not commented in the sources reviewed.

World.title: Venezuela Sanctions: What the Rodríguez Delisting Signals
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

The Parque Central towers in central Caracas, Venezuela. (Photo: Wilfredor, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT · VENEZUELA

Key Facts — The country Venezuela, an oil state on South America’s Caribbean coast, has been led by acting president Delcy Rodríguez since US forces captured Nicolás Maduro on Saturday 3 January 2026.

— Why it matters Venezuela sanctions are being unwound person by person, and the latest name removed belongs to the man who leads the government side in US-backed talks.

— Why now The US Treasury delisted National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez on Wednesday 14 October 2026, the day a third round of government-opposition talks was due to open in Caracas.

— What happened He follows his sister Delcy, delisted on 1 April 2026. Diosdado Cabello, Vladimir Padrino López, Cilia Flores and Maduro himself remain on the US blacklist.

— The numbers The US list still carries 405 entries under Venezuela programmes, 186 of them individuals, including state oil company PDVSA and the central bank.

— What it means for you US firms may now deal with Rodríguez, but most business with PDVSA and the Venezuelan state still needs an OFAC general licence.

— Still open Washington has given no reason. The next markers are the talks on political guarantees, a Maduro court hearing on 15 October and a PDVSA bond licence date on 5 November.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 10.5% chance that Venezuela schedules a presidential election by 31 December (14 October, 2:48 p.m. ET).

— Power Index Venezuela ranks 13th of 14 in Venezuela ranks 13th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 27.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Venezuela sanctions eased again on Wednesday 14 October 2026, when the US Treasury delisted National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez. He leads the government side in US-backed talks in Caracas, so the move matters to US investors, oil firms and Venezuelan exiles.

The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), which enforces US sanctions, gave no reason in its notice. The timing, however, coincides with a political process that Washington openly sponsors.

What the Delisting Tells Us About Venezuela Sanctions

The removal came on the day a third round of government-opposition talks was due to open in Caracas. Efecto Cocuyo reported that the round would focus on political and civil guarantees for an eventual election.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Venezuela ranks 13th of 14 with 27.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (81); weakest: economic relationships (0). Alignment group: Closer to Beijing. Some pillar data are incomplete for Venezuela; see the index notes. WatchSovereign in selective default; inflation of 252%; public debt at 309% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Rodríguez leads the government side, while Dinorah Figuera, who presides over the 2015 Assembly’s Delegated Commission, leads the opposition team. Opposition leaders María Corina Machado and Edmundo González Urrutia are not part of the talks.

On Friday 9 October, Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Figuera in Washington and urged progress on political freedoms and electoral reform. The State Department said such steps would lay the foundation for free, fair and credible elections in Venezuela.

So far the pattern is relief granted name by name rather than in one package. His sister Delcy, now acting president, came off the list on Wednesday 1 April 2026, about three months after Maduro’s capture.

Washington has also managed business access through general licences rather than by delisting state companies. On Monday 28 September OFAC amended licences covering Venezuelan oil and petrochemical products, supplies to Venezuela and contingent investment contracts.

On Friday 21 August it added licences for telecommunications supplies and contingent telecoms investment. These licences let US firms negotiate contingent deals while the underlying Venezuela sanctions on the state stay in place.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Venezuela Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Still on the List

The current Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list still carries 405 entries under Venezuela programmes, 186 of them individuals. They include state oil company Petróleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) and the Banco Central de Venezuela, the central bank.

Former president Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, both held in New York, remain listed. So do Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello and former defence minister Vladimir Padrino López.

Padrino López and Flores were designated in the same 25 September 2018 package as the Rodríguez siblings. The Treasury said then that sanctions were meant to change behaviour and could be lifted for officials who helped restore democratic order.

That 2018 language remains the clearest official guide to how Venezuela sanctions can be lifted for individuals. OFAC has not said whether Rodríguez met those conditions.

Dates to Watch in the Coming Weeks

The first test is the third round of talks itself. The first two rounds, in August and September, each ran for about a week and ended with a signed accord.

Those rounds produced a committee to vet Supreme Court candidates, unblocked news websites and steps on justice reform. After the second accord on Friday 25 September, Rodríguez said Venezuela would hold four elections within constitutional deadlines.

Some analysts read that remark as pointing to a presidential vote only in 2030. Opposition delegate Jorge Millán called the announcement unilateral and not an agreement reached at the table.

On Thursday 15 October, Maduro and Flores are due before Judge Alvin Hellerstein in New York to answer new charges. Prosecutors added a torture conspiracy count last week and extended a narco-terrorism charge to Flores, Efecto Cocuyo reported.

Their trial is set for June 2027, with a sovereign-immunity dismissal motion due for a hearing on Tuesday 17 November. Both are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

For bondholders, the key date is Thursday 5 November 2026. OFAC’s General License 5Z, issued on 16 September, delays a key authorisation until that day.

That authorisation would let holders of PDVSA’s 2020 8.5% bond pursue the pledged shares of CITGO, PDVSA’s US refining arm. OFAC has postponed it repeatedly since October 2019, so a further extension remains possible.

What It Means for You

For US banks, law firms and oil traders, Rodríguez is no longer off-limits, and his assets under US jurisdiction are unblocked. That removes one legal hurdle to direct dealings with the man who chairs Venezuela’s legislature.

PDVSA and the central bank remain blocked, so most oil and finance deals under Venezuela sanctions still depend on OFAC general licences. Companies should read the current licence versions and take legal advice before any transaction.

Holders of Venezuelan and PDVSA debt should watch the 5 November date and any new licence that changes it. Visa rules and other countries’ sanctions are separate matters and were not addressed in Wednesday’s notice.

Our profile Jorge Rodríguez: Venezuela’s Negotiator and Power Broker traces his career, and US Delists Venezuela’s Jorge Rodríguez covers the OFAC notice. For the wider picture, see Venezuela Politics 2026, Who Holds Power After Maduro, Venezuela Geopolitics Explained, US Now Runs Its Oil and our Caracas city guide.

RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

What Is Not Known

OFAC has not explained the removal, and we found no official comment from Washington or Caracas by Wednesday afternoon. It is not known whether conditions, a licence or private assurances are attached to it.

It is also unclear whether further delistings, including of PDVSA or the central bank, are under review. Nobody has said whether the third round of talks will produce an election date.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, bets that Venezuela will schedule a presidential election by 31 December trade at 10.5%, with about US$144,000 traded on that line. Earlier lines for 31 January and 31 March closed without a date being set.

A separate Polymarket market gives Delcy Rodríguez a 93.5% chance of being Venezuela’s de facto leader at the end of 2026, with about US$410,000 in volume. Her brother is priced at 0.15% at 2:48 p.m. ET on Wednesday, and these figures are bets, not polls.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does the Jorge Rodríguez delisting signal for Venezuela sanctions?

It shows Washington easing Venezuela sanctions name by name as US-backed talks move forward. OFAC gave no reason, so any link to the talks is an inference rather than an official statement.

Who is still under US sanctions in Venezuela?

Nicolás Maduro, Cilia Flores, Diosdado Cabello and Vladimir Padrino López remain on the SDN list. State oil company PDVSA and the central bank are also still listed.

Can US companies now do business with Jorge Rodríguez?

Yes, US persons are no longer barred from dealing with him, and his assets under US jurisdiction are unblocked. Deals involving PDVSA or the Venezuelan state still need an OFAC licence.

What happens on 5 November 2026?

OFAC’s General License 5Z takes effect that day unless it is changed again. It would let holders of PDVSA’s 2020 bond pursue the CITGO shares pledged as collateral.

Will Venezuela hold a presidential election soon?

No date has been set, and the third round of talks focuses on political guarantees for an eventual vote. Polymarket bets price a date being scheduled by 31 December at 10.5%.

World.title: Brazil Services Slip 0.1% in August
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Shoppers and diners in the main hall of São Paulo's Municipal Market, the Mercadão. Services to families, which include food services, were the only segment to grow in August. (Photo: Celykzk, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

ECONOMY · BRAZIL

Key Facts — The country Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy, with more than 210 million people, and its services sector spans hotels, restaurants, transport, telecoms and IT.

— Why it matters Services data shape interest-rate expectations in Brazil, which move the bonds, stocks and currency that US investors hold.

— Why now IBGE published its Monthly Services Survey for August on Wednesday 14 October, three weeks before the central bank’s next rate decision.

— What happened Services volume fell 0.1% from July after a flat July, while a separate tourism activity index rose 2.5%.

— The numbers Services volume was 0.6% higher than a year earlier and 2.2% higher over 12 months, and 0.3% below its October 2025 record.

— What it means for you A cooling services sector adds to the case for more rate cuts, which matters for US holders of Brazilian assets and travel firms.

— Still open Whether the tourism rebound lasts and how the central bank reads the data at its 3 to 4 November meeting.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives a 0.25-point cut in the Selic rate at the November meeting an 87% chance (14 October, 2:48 p.m. ET).

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 85% · Lula 14.5% (US$182 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 86% · Lula 15% As of 14 October, 2:40 pm ET (19:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Brazil services volume slipped 0.1% in August from July, the national statistics office IBGE said on Wednesday 14 October. The dip leaves the sector just 0.3% below the record it set in October 2025.

For US investors, it adds to signs of a cooling economy as the central bank weighs cutting its 13.75% Selic rate again. Tourism activity, a separate index covering travel-related businesses, rose 2.5% for a second straight monthly gain.

What the August Data Show

The Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) runs the Monthly Services Survey, known by its Portuguese initials PMS. It measures the volume of services sold, which strips out the effect of price changes.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

On seasonally adjusted figures, volume fell 0.1% in August after a flat July and a 0.1% rise in June. The last clear monthly gain was a 1.2% jump in April, which followed a 1% drop in March.

Compared with August 2025, services volume was 0.6% higher. It grew 1.7% in the first eight months of 2026 and 2.2% over the past 12 months.

Nominal revenue, which includes price changes, rose 0.2% on the month and 6.1% on the year. The gap between revenue and volume growth suggests that service prices are still rising briskly.

The sector stands 19.9% above February 2020, the last month before the pandemic hit Brazil’s economy. Since its October 2025 peak, however, the index has moved sideways within a narrow band.

Brazil's services volume index has moved sideways since its October 2025 peak. (Chart: The Rio Times; data: IBGE, 14 October 2026)

Where Brazil Services Grew and Shrank

Only one of the five main Brazil services segments grew in August: services provided to families, which rose 2.1%. That group covers accommodation, food services and other personal services.

Information and communication services, which include telecoms and IT, were unchanged from July. Professional and administrative services fell 0.2%, as did transport, auxiliary transport services and mail.

The catch-all group of other services posted the steepest monthly fall, down 1%. It was also 2.5% lower than in August 2025.

On the year, transport was 2.8% lower, while information and communication grew 4.3%. Services to families were 4.2% higher and professional and administrative services 1.7% higher.

Tourism Rebounds After a Weak June

IBGE’s tourism activity index, calculated separately from the five segments, rose 2.5% from July. It was the second monthly gain in a row, adding up to 5.5% since June.

Part of that gain is a recovery, because the index had fallen 3.9% in June. In August it was 0.9% higher than a year earlier but still 0.8% lower for the year to date.

The tourism index stands 12.4% above its February 2020 level. It is 1.1% below its peak, reached in December 2024.

What It Means for You

For US investors in Brazilian stocks and bonds, the data point to an economy losing speed under high interest rates. The central bank has cut its Selic rate five times since March, from 15% to 13.75%.

Weaker services activity gives the central bank more room to keep easing, but inflation remains the main constraint. Economists in the central bank’s weekly Focus survey expect 5.22% inflation in 2026, above the 4.5% ceiling of the target range.

The International Monetary Fund also trimmed its outlook this week, as covered in IMF Cuts Brazil 2026 Growth Forecast to 2.2%. For US travel firms and visitors, the tourism index shows demand for hotels, transport and restaurants recovering after a weak June.

For background on the economy and who holds power, see Brazil Explained 2026 for Newcomers on Politics and Economy and Who Dominates Brazil, Elites and Regions Explained. Readers in the country’s business capital can follow local news on our São Paulo city page.

What Is Not Known

The national figures do not show whether the August dip reflects weaker demand or one-off swings in the volatile other services group. It is also unclear whether the tourism rebound will hold into the end of the year.

The central bank weighs inflation, the labour market and the global outlook alongside activity data. Its statement after the 3 to 4 November meeting will show how much weight policymakers give to the slowdown in services.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, bets give a 0.25-point Selic cut at the November meeting an 87% chance (14 October, 2:48 p.m. ET). A pause is priced at about 10%, and a cut of 0.5 points or more at about 3%.

About US$59,000 has been traded on the market so far, including about US$8,900 in the past 24 hours. Over the past week, the price of a 0.5-point cut fell by about 6 points, while a pause gained about 5 points.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the Brazil services data show for August?

Services volume fell 0.1% from July on seasonally adjusted figures, IBGE said on Wednesday 14 October. It was still 0.6% higher than in August 2025.

Which part of the services sector grew?

Only services provided to families, which include accommodation and food services, grew, rising 2.1%. Information and communication was flat, and the other three segments fell.

How did tourism perform?

IBGE’s tourism activity index rose 2.5% in August, its second monthly gain in a row. It remains 1.1% below its December 2024 peak.

Why does this matter to US investors?

Services data feed into the central bank’s interest-rate decisions, which move Brazilian bonds, stocks and the currency. The Selic rate stands at 13.75% after five cuts since March.

When is the next interest-rate decision?

The central bank’s Monetary Policy Committee, known as Copom, meets on 3 and 4 November. On 14 October, Polymarket bets gave a 0.25-point cut an 87% chance.

World.title: Egyptian Pound Slides Past 53 per Dollar
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

CURRENCY · EGYPT

Key Facts — The country Egypt is the most populous Arab country, controls the Suez Canal and is in an IMF-backed economic reform programme.

— Why it matters A weaker pound raises the cost of Egypt’s fuel imports and cuts the dollar value of Egyptian treasury bills held by foreign investors.

— Why now Brent crude above US$100 a barrel and regional tension have lifted demand for dollars and pushed some foreign money out of Egyptian debt.

— What happened The central bank’s official rate closed at 53.18 pounds per dollar on Wednesday 14 October, the weakest for the pound since 19 May.

— The numbers Foreign investors sold a net 5.8 billion pounds (about US$109 million) of treasury bills on Wednesday. Remittances rose 27.2% to US$33.9 billion in January to August.

— What it means for you A dollar now buys more pounds for travellers, while US holders of Egyptian debt face currency losses.

— Still open Whether the central bank lets the slide run or slows it, and whether oil prices ease, is not known.

The Egyptian pound weakened past 53 per US dollar on Wednesday 14 October, its lowest level since May. The Central Bank of Egypt’s official rate closed at 53.04 pounds to buy and 53.18 pounds per dollar to sell.

That compares with 52.90 pounds per dollar at Tuesday’s close, a daily move of about 0.5%. For American readers, a weaker pound makes Egypt cheaper to visit but raises risks for US investors holding Egyptian government debt.

Why the Egyptian Pound Is Falling

Al Manassa, an independent Egyptian news site, said the close was the dollar’s highest since 19 May, citing central bank data. Masrawy, a Cairo news portal, said the pound broke through 53 in early trading for the first time in five months.

At Wednesday afternoon’s close, state-owned National Bank of Egypt and Banque Misr quoted 53.05 pounds to buy and 53.15 pounds per dollar to sell. Commercial International Bank (CIB), a private lender, quoted 53.18 pounds per dollar to sell, matching the central bank, Youm7 reported.

Ali Metwally, an analyst at Mosaic Economics, told Al Manassa that rising global energy prices could lift demand for dollars in Egypt. Egypt imports more petroleum products than it exports, and its petroleum trade deficit widened 31.5% in the fiscal year to June.

Brent crude has traded above US$100 a barrel since early October and reached US$107.15 on Wednesday, Al Manassa reported. The rise followed a strike on a Saudi Aramco facility by the Houthis, the Iran-aligned movement that controls much of northern Yemen.

Mina Rafik, a macroeconomic analyst at Prime Investment, said foreign investors may be leaving over regional tension and higher US bond yields. Foreign investors were net sellers of 5.8 billion pounds (about US$109 million) of Egyptian treasury bills on Wednesday.

Rafik pointed to expectations that the Federal Reserve keeps raising rates while Egypt’s central bank holds its own rates steady. That mix can shrink the extra return that draws short-term foreign money, often called hot money, into Egyptian debt.

The Stabilisers Behind the Pound

The central bank reported on Tuesday 13 October that remittances from Egyptians abroad rose 27.2% to US$33.9 billion in January to August. That compares with US$26.6 billion in the same months of 2025, a cushion for the currency.

Banking expert Mohamed Abdel Aal told Al-Masry Al-Youm that remittances and record tourism income shield the pound from a sharp fall. He expects the rate to hold between 52 and 53 pounds to the dollar over the next two months.

Abdel Aal said Egypt’s flexible exchange rate can allow sudden jumps, but it stops a large gap opening between official and market rates. He described the latest moves as fluctuation rather than a trend with no ceiling.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) completed its seventh review of Egypt’s loan programme on 30 July, allowing about US$1.5 billion in new funds. It urged Cairo to keep the exchange rate flexible and to keep building reserves.

The IMF also expects inflation to rise to 16.7% in the second half of 2026, partly because of a weaker currency. A further slide in the pound would add to that pressure on Egyptian households.

Earlier reporting on the central bank’s reserves is in Egypt’s Reserves Hit Record US$57.35 Billion, and on the external accounts in Egypt Current Account Deficit Hits US$22.5 Billion. What It Means for US Readers

For American visitors, the slide means more pounds for each dollar on a trip to Cairo, Luxor or the Red Sea resorts. Rising inflation of the kind the IMF expects can wear that gain away over time.

US funds that hold Egyptian treasury bills earn high pound yields but lose value in dollar terms when the currency weakens. Wednesday’s net foreign sales show that some investors are already cutting their exposure.

Egypt imports much of its fuel, so a weaker pound raises the cost of energy bought in dollars. It also matters to Washington, which treats Cairo as a key partner on Gaza, the Suez Canal and Red Sea security.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the Central Bank of Egypt will let the slide continue or act to slow it. The full scale of foreign selling of Egyptian debt this week has not been published.

Oil prices and regional tension are the main swing factors for the pound in the coming weeks. If Brent eases and remittances keep rising, analysts quoted in Egyptian media see room for the rate to settle near 53.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Egyptian pound’s rate against the dollar?

The Central Bank of Egypt’s official rate closed at 53.04 pounds to buy and 53.18 pounds per dollar to sell on Wednesday 14 October. That was the weakest level for the pound since 19 May.

Why is the Egyptian pound falling?

Analysts point to higher oil prices, which raise Egypt’s fuel import bill, and to foreign investors selling Egyptian treasury bills. Regional tension and higher US interest rates add to the pressure.

Is the Egyptian pound pegged to the dollar?

No, Egypt uses a flexible exchange rate set largely by supply and demand in the banking system. The IMF has urged Cairo to keep that flexibility while building reserves.

Is Egypt cheaper for American travellers now?

A dollar buys more pounds than it did on Tuesday, which helps visitors paying local prices. Rising inflation can reduce that gain over time.

What supports the pound?

Remittances from Egyptians abroad rose 27.2% to US$33.9 billion in January to August, and tourism income is strong. The IMF programme also gives Egypt access to new funding after each successful review.
