We sincerely regret the inconvenience caused to our passengers due to this unforeseen disruption and appreciate their patience and understanding. The safety and security of our passengers and crew remain Air India's highest priority,â AI statement added.

World.title: Govt renames flagship social assistance scheme, drops Indira Gandhi tag
World.content:
The proposed changes cover three pension schemes and the National Social Assistance Programme under the rural development ministry.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday approved the continuation of its flagship social security scheme National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) for five years until 2031, while renaming it Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana and dropping former PM Indira Gandhiâs name from three of its sub-schemes.Announcing the decision, I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the âcomprehensive social security netâ will cover vulnerable groups, including the elderly, widows and persons with disabilities. The scheme with an outlay of Rs 53,428 crore is expected to benefit 3.2 crore people.The revamped programme revises the eligibility criteria for pension for persons with disability (PwD) and increases the assistance provided under the sub-scheme.As per the official release, Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme has been renamed PM Vridhavastha Pension Yojana, the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme is now PM Vidhawa Pension Yojana and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme becomes PM Divyangjan Pension Yojana.This comes after the Cabinet approved a new rural employment guarantee scheme, Viksit BharatâGuarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), in December last year, replacing the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA).Under the revised disability pension sub-scheme, monthly assistance will increase to Rs 375 for beneficiaries from birth to 79 years and to Rs 625 for those aged 80 and above. Till now, beneficiaries aged 18â79 received Rs 300 per month, while those aged 80 and above received Rs 500.The eligibility threshold for benchmark disability has also been reduced to 40% from 80%, bringing the scheme in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Govt said the revision was necessitated by the law, which has also mandated that disability-related assistance be at least 25% higher than that provided under comparable schemes for other categories. The revised scheme is expected to cover more than 27.48 lakh beneficiaries.The pension amounts under the old-age and widow pension schemes, as well as assistance under the National Family Benefit Scheme, will remain unchanged. The old-age pension ranges from Rs 200 to Rs 500 per month and covers 221.31 lakh beneficiaries, while the widow pension ranges from Rs 300 to Rs 500 per month and covers 67.38 lakh beneficiaries.Under the National Family Benefit Scheme, a one-time financial assistance of Rs 20,000 is provided to a household following the death of its primary breadwinner, provided the deceased was aged between 18 and 59 years. The scheme covers up to 3.59 lakh beneficiaries.

World.title: After Musk’s Ambani meltdown, Rubio to visit Reliance refinery
World.content:
File photo: US secretary of state Marco Rubio is set to visit Mumbai and Jamnagar from October 17-22

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel next week to Mumbai and Gujaratâs refinery hub Jamnagar, announced the State Department. The brief stopover in Jamnagar, which will see him touring the Reliance oil refinery, is being seen through the lens of Relianceâs plans to invest in a major refinery in Texas, the first of its kind in 50 years in the US and a major priority for the Trump administration.The announcement about Rubioâs Jamnagar visit came days after billionaire Elon Muskâs social media jab â addressing Mukesh Ambani as PM Ambani and the real boss of India â over alleged regulatory delays being faced by the Musk-controlled satellite internet service provider Starlink.This will be Rubioâs second visit to India this year, following his trip to Delhi in May for a meeting of the Quad foreign ministers. Energy is likely to be a key focus area for Rubio during his visit beginning Monday.âHe will meet with senior government officials to strengthen the US-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Secretary Rubio will also meet with business leaders to promote opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation,â said the State Department in its announcement.Rubio is also expected to have a bilateral meeting with his counterpart S Jaishankar in Mumbai. The visit comes shortly after another round of tensions over the talent mobility issue, with the US suspending firms, including many from India, from the PERM green card programme. India had strongly condemned remarks by US Vice President J D Vance, who characterized foreign tech workers as foreign indentured servants, calling the statement deeply offensive and unjustified.India had responded angrily to Vice President J D Vanceâs remarks describing tech professionals from abroad as foreign indentured servants, calling his remarks deeply offensive and unwarranted.India is also likely to bring up its concerns related to the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (SRIA) that empowers the president to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on countries importing Russian oil. That threat may have subsided for now though with the US itself allowing Russia to temporarily export diesel to America and global marketplace. India is expected to reiterate its position that energy security and stable markets must take precedence over rigid geopolitics.Rubioâs visit will also mark the beginning of several high-level engagements between the 2 sides in the next few months. The ministers will meet again on the margins of the G20 foreign ministersâ meeting in Atlanta on October 30-31. Another meeting of the Quad foreign ministers will also take place on the sidelines.PM Narendra Modi will also travel to Florida for the G20 summit in Florida on December 14-15. He is expected to have a bilateral meeting with Trump. Thereâs also the possibility of a Quad leadersâ summit taking place during Modiâs US visit.While the foreign ministersâ meeting in Atlanta would be the 4th such meeting since the return of Trump to the White House, a leadersâ summit remains elusive. During his visit to India in May, Rubio had described Quad as linchpin and a cornerstone of the US global strategy as a nation. However, there has been no word so far on the dates and likely venue for the next leadersâ summit.

World.title: ‘Docs leave women seeking MTP to God’s mercy and force them approach courts’: J&K HC
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir high court has expressed displeasure over doctors hesitating to undertake abortions without judicial orders even in âjustified casesâ, despite this being permitted under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971.âThe registered medical practitioners, especially doctors working in the associated hospitals of medical colleges and in other district hospitals, do not shoulder their statutory responsibilities in terms of the provisions of MTP Act, 1971 and the rules of 2003 framed thereunder in justified cases, thereby leaving the aggrieved mothers at the mercy of the God, who feel constrained to shoulder further mental agony and burden of approaching the courts of law for legal directions,â the court said.Disposing of a petition seeking termination of a nearly 32-week pregnancy on grounds of foetus anomaly, a single bench of Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani directed the medical superintendent of Srinagarâs Lalla Ded Hospital to constitute a medical board for the examination of the petitioner. The court ordered that immediate action be taken based on the medical boardâs opinion regarding the MTP.Under the MTP Act, termination of pregnancy beyond 24 weeks is highly restricted.Justice Wani said clause 2-B of section 3 and clause 1 of section 5 of the MTP Act clearly state that the provisions relating to length of pregnancy shall not apply when MTP is necessitated by the diagnosis of any substantial foetal abnormalities by a medical board and/or is immediately necessary to save the motherâs life. Where statutory directions are clear, medical practitioners or medical boards âshall not unnecessarily avoid to attend such emergent casesâ, the judge observed in his Oct 6 order.The petitioner submitted that scans conducted at the gestational age of 12 weeks and six days, and again at 21 weeks and four days, showed no gross congenital anomalies in the foetus. Serious foetal abnormalities were detected for the first time only on Sept 24, when the pregnancy had reached 31 weeks and six days.Doctors, however, refused to undertake MTP without the courtâs permission because of the advanced state of pregnancy, prompting the petitioner to approach HC.

World.title: 'Shocked': Odisha governor's 'will work for BJP' remark sparks political row
World.content:
The BJD shared a PTI video in which Ram was heard speaking about his plans after taking charge as governor. Reacting to the remarks, the party said it was shocked and accused him of undermining the principle that a governor must remain above party politics.

Naveen Patnaik hopes governor will uphold constitutional dignity

Congress seeks governor's recall

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Mahua Moitra takes a swipe at BJP

NEW DELHI: Odisha's newly appointed Governor Braj Mohan Ram has triggered a political row after reportedly saying he would work to strengthen the BJP, drawing sharp criticism from the opposition Biju Janata Dal (BJD) and Congress on Wednesday. Both parties said the remarks raised questions about the impartiality expected of a constitutional office-holder. The Congress demanded that Ram be recalled, while BJD president Naveen Patnaik urged him to uphold constitutional dignity.The BJD shared a PTI video in which Ram was heard speaking about his plans after taking charge as governor. Reacting to the remarks, the party said it was shocked and accused him of undermining the principle that a governor must remain above party politics.âWe are shocked to hear his comments in a PTI video, where he reiterates that he would work towards strengthening the BJP. We condemn the remark as it negates the fact that the governor is above party politics,â the BJD said in a statement.Patnaik, the leader of the opposition in the Odisha Assembly, also expressed concern over the reported remarks. In a social media post, he referred to the governor's enthusiasm for party work and hoped he would discharge his constitutional responsibilities impartially."The people of Odisha are witnessing the enthusiasm of the nominated Governor for undertaking party work. Hope that Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath will bestow upon him the zeal and strength to serve the people of Odisha, through which he will fulfil his duties impartially while upholding constitutional dignity,â the leader of the opposition in the Odisha Assembly said in a social media post.He tagged Rashtrapati Bhavan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the post.BJD media coordinator Lenin Mohanty also criticised the comments, calling them unbecoming of a governor.The Congress accused Ram of openly expressing a partisan position before assuming a constitutional office. Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (OPCC) president Bhakta Charan Das said the governor's role was to protect the Constitution rather than advance a political party's interests.âThe Governorâs constitutional responsibility is to uphold the Constitution impartially, not to advance the electoral interests of any political party."Das said constitutional offices must remain above partisan politics. He alleged that Ram had stated he would work for the BJP's SC Morcha in Odisha, as he had done in Jharkhand in the past."It is extremely unfortunate for someone holding the dignified office of Governor to say that he will work to boost the BJP's vote share in Odisha. This exposes the true nature of the BJP," he said."The BJP government is systematically bringing one constitutional institution after another under the party's control. However, no one has ever engaged in such open partisan politics prior to assuming such a high office,â the OPCC leader said.OPCC spokesperson Arabinda Das demanded that the Centre immediately recall Ram. Alternatively, he said, the chief justice of the High Court should raise objections to administering the oath of office to him.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra also joined the criticism, taking a sarcastic dig at Ram and the BJP in a post on X.âHello Odisha- this is your new governor. He says his job is to strengthen saffron organisation in Odisha. The state has become a dump yard for unemployed senior sanghis! @Naveen_Odishaâ.Ram, a three-time former BJP MP, was appointed Odisha governor on Monday. The Odisha BJP had not responded to the reported remarks at the time of publication.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM announces relief for hailstorm-affected farmers
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand chief minister

on Wednesday announced relief measures for farmers affected by hailstorms and directed concerned officials to take necessary action.

Under this initiative, financial assistance equivalent to the amount prescribed under existing disaster relief norms will be provided for losses incurred by agricultural, horticultural, and sugarcane crops.

Additionally, steps will be taken to defer electricity bill payments for affected farmers and provide relief regarding Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loan repayments.

"The state government is committed to safeguarding the interests of farmers and helping them overcome hardships caused by natural disasters. Every possible measure would be taken to secure farmers' livelihoods and agricultural activities," Dhami said.

Hailstorm-affected farmers will receive additional financial assistance equal to the amount they are entitled to under the prescribed disaster relief norms.

To provide immediate financial relief to the affected farmers, the state government has also decided to defer the payment of electricity bills for the months of October, November, and December.

World.title: ’Blue drum’ murder case: Meerut court sentences wife, partner to death
World.content:
New Delhi

A Meerut court on Wednesday sentenced Muskan Rastogi and her partner, Sahil Shukla, to death for murdering her husband, Saurabh Rajput, whose dismembered remains were found in a cement-filled plastic drum in March 2025. Saurabh, a merchant navy officer, was killed on March 3 last year, and the body was discovered two weeks later. District and Sessions Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra pronounced the sentence after convicting the duo of murder and destruction of evidence. The case, which drew widespread attention because of the brutality of the crime, saw more than 100 hearings and the examination of 22 prosecution witnesses. Prosecution lawyer K.K. Chaubey told reporters that the judge referred to the Mahabharata while explaining the punishment, observing that “justice required punishment proportionate to the gravity of the offence”. “Apart from the death sentence, the court also imposed fines totalling ₹70,000 on each convict for murder and the offence related to the disappearance of evidence,” Mr. Chaubey said. The two accused, who attended the proceedings via video conference, reportedly broke down after the verdict was announced. Lawyers present in the courtroom distributed sweets following the pronouncement. The detailed court order is awaited. The crime Saurabh, 35, returned to Meerut from London in late February 2025. According to the police investigation, when his family failed to trace him for several days, they approached the police, who recovered his dismembered remains from a cement-filled drum at the house he shared with Muskan. The couple’s six-year-old daughter allegedly pointed to the container when asked about her father’s whereabouts. In the chargesheet filed in May 2025, the police claimed that Muskan and Sahil drugged Saurabh before stabbing him to death and dismembering his body. They allegedly placed his remains in the drum, sealed it with cement and sand, and left for a vacation in Himachal Pradesh. The police used industrial equipment to break through the hardened cement and retrieve the remains. The police filed a nearly 1,000-page chargesheet detailing the evidence against the duo, including forensic reports, call records, CCTV footage and witness statements. Muskan, who was pregnant at the time of the crime, later gave birth to a girl while in jail.

World.title: Sally Rooney's books no longer sold in U.K. over support for banned pro-Palestinian group
World.content:
Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books will no longer be sold in Britain over her ​plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action, a ‌pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney ​and her publisher said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).

The bestselling ⁠author, known for novels including “Normal People” and “Conversations with Friends”, has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after it was ‌proscribed by the British government under terrorism laws last year.

Ms. Rooney previously said in a witness ‌statement submitted to London’s High Court, in support ‌of ⁠a legal challenge over the ban on Palestine ⁠Action, that her plans could lead to her books being withdrawn from sale in Britain.

Her publisher Faber said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) that ​it had agreed with Rooney ‌that “we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format”, though it would sell her works elsewhere.

“Current legislation in the UK ‌has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on ​UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work,” Faber said in a statement.

“To sell ⁠a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.”

Ms. Rooney ‌said in a statement: “I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences.”

Palestine Action, which had increasingly targeted Israel-linked defence companies, was banned shortly after a June 2025 break-in ‌at the Royal Air Force’s Brize Norton base.

Last year, Palestine ​Action’s co-founder Huda Ammori challenged the ban and the High Court ruled in her favour ⁠in February, before the Court of Appeal overturned that decision ⁠in June. The Supreme Court is due to hear an appeal next month.

More than 3,000 ‌people have since been arrested for holding signs in support of Palestine Action and its proscription ​has been criticised by civil liberties groups.

World.title: Engineering, management courses offer diverse career opportunities, says Expert
World.content:
Engineering and management graduates have diverse career opportunities across traditional industries, emerging technologies, research and business leadership, said Dr. Mitrabarun Ghosh, Assistant Professor at Paari School of Business, SRM University-A.P.

He was delivering a career guidance session titled “Career Directions: Engineering & Management” for final-year B.Tech students at Tirumala Engineering College, Narasaraopet, on Wednesday. The seminar on “Careers in Management & Sciences” was organised by The Hindu Future India Club in association with Paari School of Business, SRM A.P., in collaboration with Tirumala Engineering College. R. Satyanarayana, Secretary and Correspondent of Tirumala Engineering College, Dr. Y.V. Narayana, Principal, and V.V.S. Pradeep of SRM University were present at the programme.

Dr. Ghosh explained the opportunities available through technical careers and management education, emphasising that neither path was inherently superior and that students should choose according to their interests, skills and long-term aspirations.

While engineering offers opportunities in technology, research, design and innovation, management opens avenues in leadership, strategy, marketing, finance and business operations. Combining engineering experience with an MBA can help graduates pursue careers in product management, consulting and leadership roles, he said.

He highlighted employment opportunities in information technology, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, semiconductors, manufacturing and global capability centres. Government career options through GATE, UPSC Engineering Services, ISRO, DRDO, Indian Railways and public sector undertakings were also discussed.

The speaker drew attention to emerging sectors, including electric vehicles, green energy, space technology, defence startups and chip design. Alternative career options such as technical writing, patent analysis, research, public policy and entrepreneurship were also explained.

Dr. Ghosh guided students on higher education opportunities in India and abroad through examinations such as GATE, CAT, GRE and GMAT. He advised them to consider institutional rankings, accreditation, placement records, faculty expertise, industry connections and return on investment while selecting colleges.

He encouraged students to identify a primary career path and a backup option, prepare strategically for competitive examinations, and strengthen their profiles through projects, internships and certifications.

World.title: Marco Rubio to skip Delhi, visit Mumbai and Jamnagar next week
World.content:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India for his second visit in six months, with energy and trade relations at the top of the agenda as he visits Mumbai and Jamnagar, the U.S. Department of State announced on Wednesday (October 14, 2026).

However, Mr. Rubio, who is expected to visit India from October 19 to 22 after travelling to Samarkand in Uzbekistan for a regional conference, will skip Delhi.

“[Mr. Rubio] will meet with senior government officials to strengthen the U.S.-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation,” the State department said in the statement, adding that Mr. Rubio will also meet business leaders to “promote investment opportunities”.

Mr. Rubio’s scheduled visit to Jamnagar is important as it hosts the world’s largest single-site refinery, operated by Reliance industries, and is expected to include a major reception hosted by the Ambani family. The Jamnagar refinery is one of the top three companies refining Russian Ural crude oil, although it has reduced its share of the imports. The visit would follow just a day after U.S. President Donald Trump is mandated by the U.S. Congress to propose extra tariffs as sanctions on India and other countries buying Russian oil, under the Sanctions Against Russian and Iran Act (SRIA) passed into law last month.

In March 2026, Mr. Trump announced that Reliance Industries would invest in a refinery in Brownsville, Texas, although details of the exact collaboration have still not been released.

The U.S. Secretary of State is expected to meet External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar during the visit, but the Ministry of External Affairs didn’t confirm the visit or answer questions on why Mr. Rubio is skipping Delhi on this visit.

Asked about the U.S. statement on the trip, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the government would make the announcement “at the appropriate time as to what will be the issues to be taken up”. He also said that the government would disclose details of the visit “as and when they happen”. To another question, he said that India had already conveyed its concerns over the SRIA to the U.S. government.

Tension in ties

The visit by Mr. Rubio comes at a time of tensions in the India-U.S. economic relationship for a number of other reasons as well. Senior officials and Ministers on both sides have acknowledged there is trouble in the Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA), with Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman saying that the talks last week had “plateaued”.

The U.S.-India ties were dealt another blow last week as the Trump administration suspended permission for five Indian tech outsourcing companies to certify Indian professionals as eligible for green cards or permanent residency. The visit would also come just ahead of the key mid-term elections in the U.S., where Mr. Trump’s Republican Party is expected to face losses.

Mr. Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi are due to meet nonetheless on December 13, on the sidelines of the G20 summit in Florida, and possibly in November at the ASEAN linked summits in Manila. Both leaders spoke over the telephone on September 30.

In Kolkata on Monday for celebrations of the U.S.’s 250th Independence day anniversary, U.S. Ambassador to India and the region Sergio Gor indicated to journalists that more engagements would be announced soon, saying “stay tuned for what comes next.” Mr. Rubio last visited Delhi in May 2026 to attend the Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting.

World.title: U.S. lawmaker concerned over India’s actions to 'purge 130 million people’ from voter rolls
World.content:
The Indian-origin U.S. Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal on Wednesday (October 14, 2026) voiced concern over reports of the removal of 13 crore voter names from the draft electoral rolls in India.

“I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls,” Jayapal said in a post on X, marking the first such comments by a US lawmaker on the issue.

The Democratic Congresswoman from Washington State said she supported the non-violent protests to counter "anti-democratic efforts in India.”

I am deeply concerned about the actions of the Indian government to purge 130 million people from the voting rolls. This appears to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing here at home to undermine voting rights in a democracy. — Rep. Pramila Jayapal (@RepJayapal) October 14, 2026

Ms. Jayapal said the developments in India appear to be a similar playbook to what the Trump Administration is doing in the U.S. to undermine voting rights in a democracy.

She said protecting democracies everywhere is essential work, and the Indian people — like the American people — deserve free and fair elections.

“Non-violent resistance movements are essential in these moments, and I stand with the Indian people who are engaging in non-violent protests to counter anti-democratic efforts in India,” Ms. Jayapal said.

Comparing SIR 2002-04 and 2025-26

According to statistics shared by the Election Commission of India (ECI), around 7.2 crore names were deleted from the draft rolls in the first and second phases when the SIR was held in 13 States and union territories.

During the ongoing third phase, where draft lists of 18 States and Union Territories are published, the number of deleted voters stands at 6.16 crore.

The Commission has said that if a genuine voter’s name was inadvertently left out during the SIR process, the voter could seek inclusion through the claims and objections process and subsequently through Form 6.

World.title: Cardiology dept. in Kozhikode MCH in need of critical care
World.content:
The Department of Cardiology at the Government Medical College Hospital (MCH), Kozhikode, which is visited by hundreds of patients from across north Keralam every day, is facing a serious shortage of doctors.

Though the sanctioned permanent staff strength is 14, only eight are on the rolls, and one of the doctors has been sent on a working arrangement basis to the Government Medical College Hospital, Wayanad, too.

According to sources, instead of filling up the posts of Assistant Professors, the authorities have been deploying Doctorate of Medicine (DM) trainees, who work at the hospital to complete their one-year bond period and then leave the job.

Senior doctors say that this stop-gap arrangement does not have any practical use. They claim that at least 10 years of continuous experience in the echocardiogram test room is required for a doctor to deliver an expert opinion. “The DM trainees can be deployed for outpatient department duty, primary angioplasty surgeries for heart attack, and basic echocardiogram procedures, that’s fine. But, if someone gets a doubt in a complex case in the echocardiogram test room, the senior doctors even on operation theatre duty may have to be called in to clear it. There are three such echo rooms here where tests are done simultaneously,” says a doctor.

The department has the posts of one Professor, three Associate Professors, and 10 Assistant Professors. The doctors say that even this staff pattern was set long ago and the number of patients has seen a drastic rise in recent years. Though there were two more posts of Professors earlier, they were reportedly shifted to other medical college hospitals. The present crisis is set to aggravate in the next three to four years when some of the senior doctors will retire from service, they point out.

For the record, around 600 patients seek treatment every day at the cardiology OP section. Over 5,500 procedures, including 980 primary angioplasty surgeries, were performed last year. The patients admitted with heart attack are directly shifted from the casualty to the cardiology intensive care unit (ICU). Up to 10 patients are reportedly shifted to the ICU every day and the primary angioplasty surgeries are done round the clock. There are two cath labs here.

Though the authorities have repeatedly intimated the government about the situation and applications were invited for the posts of Assistant Professors, many junior doctors are not keen on joining duty reportedly because of the unattractive entry-level pay.

World.title: Iran-backed Houthis strike Saudi oil company Aramco's headquarters, officials say
World.content:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels hit the headquarters of the Saudi state-owned oil company Aramco in an overnight strike, two regional officials said on Wednesday (October 14, 2026), damaging the offices of the firm's chief executive and other top officials.

The strike, in the eastern Saudi Arabian city of Dhahran, was the latest demonstration of the Houthis' ability to attack high-profile targets.

There were no casualties in the attack, which the officials said damaged the building's top three floors. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorised to discuss the matter with the media.

The Houthis had warned earlier they were targeting Dhahran with a ballistic missile.

The sight of smoke rising from some of Saudi Arabia's most sensitive facilities in recent days has rattled the region and global markets while increasing questions for US President Donald Trump, who has said he's evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Houthis in the latest front in the Iran war.

The Saudi energy ministry reported a “limited fire” at the Aramco building on Tuesday night (October 13, 2026). Aramco didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

On Wednesday (October 14, 2026), Saudi civil defence authorities in the capital, Riyadh, said debris from an intercepted strike had left one person injured. The state-run SPA news agency published images showing a damaged building and a vehicle with a large cylindrical object, seemingly part of a missile, lodged in its hood.

The Saudi-led coalition said that it had intercepted two Houthi drones, four cruise missiles and one ballistic missile targeting Riyadh, a ballistic missile targeting Dhahran and a cruise missile targeting Al-Kharj, a key military and industrial city. Alerts for incoming missiles were also sounded around Riyadh, though details weren't immediately clear.

Rebels call the strikes retaliation for ones at home

The Houthis called the attacks retaliation for “treacherous Saudi aggression” against Sanaa, the rebel-held Yemeni capital, and other areas, as the kingdom backs the forces of neighbouring Yemen's internationally recognised government in a major military offensive launched a week and a half ago. The rebel-run Health Ministry reported two dead in attacks in Yemen on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) and blamed the Saudis.

The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has been targeted multiple times in the past week with strikes that have killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300 others, greatly affecting aviation across the kingdom.

The Houthis, hardened by years of civil war, have emerged as Iran's most effective armed proxy of the moment, but experts say they also have their own agenda. Either way, they are applying increasing pressure on a key US ally.

Casualties surge along Yemen's front lines

There has been an “unprecedented surge” in combat casualties along Yemen's front lines, according to the International Committee of the Red Cross, particularly in the city of Marib, along the Red Sea coast and the besieged city of Taiz, where the World Food Program says it can no longer reach more than 6,00,000 people who depend on aid.

Main roads leading into Yemen's third-largest city have been closed amid rebel attacks, with regular clashes on the outskirts and overnight bombardment.

Residents are increasingly worried about dwindling supplies of fuel and food.

A Taiz resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity fearing the Houthis could seize the city, said that long lines now form outside shops, and public transportation has become increasingly scarce because of fuel shortages. The sound of loud explosions keeps her awake at night, she said in a telephone interview, adding that downtown Taiz hasn't been shelled.

On Wednesday, schools in Taiz were ordered closed for a month.

Houthi official describes diplomatic outreach for a ceasefire

A senior Houthi official told The Associated Press that regional and international powers have reached out in an effort to stop the attacks on Saudi Arabia as part of a ceasefire deal.

Mohamed al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Houthis' political bureau, said that Oman has tried to get both sides back to the negotiating table, and Russia and China also tried via Iran.

“We're welcoming any mediation that leads to an end of the war and the blockade between Sanaa and Riyadh,” he said. “We're ready for a comprehensive end of the war and the blockade from both sides, not just a temporary ceasefire.”

The rebels continued to warn of attacks on both airports and oil facilities. More than 3,000 flights scheduled to depart from airports across Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or listed as not operating in the past week, according to aviation analytics firm Cirium.

Saudi Arabia is running low on interceptors

The escalation has highlighted Saudi Arabia's struggle to intercept Houthi missiles and drones. The kingdom has pressed allies like the United States for more military support. Regional officials say Saudi Arabia, the world's top purchaser of US weapons, is running low on interceptors.

The Saudis are trying to stop daily attacks across a territory about three times the size of Texas. Experts say intercepting all of the missiles and drones is impossible. The Houthis have a large arsenal capable of reaching targets well over 1,000 miles (1,600 kilometres) away, with some warheads capable of changing direction midflight.

The Saudi-led coalition is also striking oil targets. Earlier Wednesday (October 14, 2026), the Houthi-run Health Ministry said that two people were killed in an airstrike on Tuesday (October 13, 2026) on an oil facility near the Ras Isa port in Hodeida province. The coalition attacked another oil facility in Sanaa.

The targeting of fuel storage facilities in Houthi-controlled areas marks a new phase, said Ahmed Nagi, senior Yemen analyst at the International Crisis Group, a think tank. He said that in a war of attrition, the rebels could risk losing much of their military capacity.

“The Houthis are betting on pressure, while the Saudis are betting on time,” Mr. Nagi said.

The fighting has revived Yemen's civil war after four years of relative calm. “There's a huge fear,” said one Sanaa resident, Umm Shadi, after the Saudi-led strikes there on Tuesday, adding that people are largely staying home.

World.title: Koder House fire under fresh scrutiny amid probe into synagogue arson
World.content:
The Kochi City police have decided to intensify the investigation into the fire that partially gutted Fort Kochi’s iconic Koder House and the recent arson incident outside the historic Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in the city, in view of the Jewish heritage associated with both institutions.

The fact that the person arrested in connection with the synagogue arson is being investigated for possible terror links has prompted the police to take a fresh look at the Fort Kochi incident. However, officials cautioned against drawing premature conclusions about possible foul play in the fire.

Addressing the media, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Kochi City) Arun K. Pavithran emphasised the need for a closer examination of the Koder House fire, even though there is currently no information directly linking the two incidents. Further conclusions can be drawn only after forensic copies of the electronic devices seized from the accused in the synagogue arson case are obtained and other materials are examined in detail, he said.

The Fort Kochi police have so far found no evidence of external involvement in the Koder House fire. Forensic findings are awaited to establish whether a short circuit, identified as the most likely cause, triggered the blaze. A final conclusion can be reached only after the Electrical Inspectorate and other scientific experts collect the necessary samples and complete their examinations.

Koder House has remained closed since the fire. Restoration work and reopening may require clearance from the relevant heritage and archaeological authorities. The blaze broke out on the evening of September 29, causing extensive damage to the historic property, which is renowned for its distinctive Indo-Portuguese architectural style.

World.title: National Assembly, Senate pass resolutions endorsing Centre's imposition of emergency in KP
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Shortly after the National Assembly passed a resolution endorsing the federal government’s imposition of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Wednesday, the Senate also gave its approval for the measure.

The Centre had imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Sunday, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled the motions regarding the proclamation of emergency before both Houses.

Senate proceedings

In the Senate, the resolution was passed amid the opposition’s outcry, with PTI senators staging a walkout.

The Senate’s approval followed a heated debate between treasury and opposition members, during which Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar defended the procedural propriety presenting the resolution in the House and getting it approved.

He argued that a “constitutional resolution” had been laid before the House in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Senate. “Under Article 232, a copy of [the proclamation of] emergency has been laid before the House. An attempt to bypass the constitutional procedure cannot succeed,” he said, adding that the requirement of a seven-day notice for tabling a resolution did not apply to one presented under a constitutional necessity.

“If its opponents have any objections, they should reject the resolution through their vote after the debate. We cannot deviate from the Constitution and rules of the House,” he said.

As opposition voiced opposition to the resolution, Senate Chairperson Yousuf Raza Gilani asked them to exercise patience. “This is not a classroom, do not make noise,” he remarked as senators from the opposition benches continued sloganeering.

Among them, PTI’s Humayun Mohmand said independent Senator Faisal Vawda had said months ago that governor’s rule would be imposed. He alleged that terrorism being cited as the reason for the measure was just an excuse and the actual “target is the PTI”.

“The decision to impose governor’s rule and emergency was taken months ago,” he alleged. Seemingly referring to the creation of Bangladesh, he said the federal government’s decision since 1970 had proved wrong.

PTI-backed Senator Hamid Khan also argued that there “seems to be some other objectives behind governor’s rule and emergency”. Referring to the talks between the Centre and the opposition ahead of governor’s rule and emergency in KP, he alleged that negotiations “were just a drama” and were held “only to deceive the people”.

“The real decision was taken elsewhere long ago,” he claimed. He further said that Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam Fazl chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who tried to mediate between the Centre and the opposition, had stated that while the negotiations were taking place, “a decision came”.

“Governments formed on the basis of Form-47 do not have the real mandate,” he added.

He further regretted that after the 26th Amendment, “there is neither any Constitution nor an independent judicial system”.

“The judiciary has been stripped of its independence, which closes the avenues to challenge unconstitutional steps,” he said.

Khan went on to say: “Article 232 has to be presented before the House for debate, not just for saying yes. Decision was taken by those whom Constitution does not allow to take the decision, but they have complete dominance over Constitution. At this time, neither is there any Constitution nor any court in the country.”

PTI Senator Mohsin Aziz railed against federal ministers, who have been accusing the PTI of facilitating terrorism.

“You talk about terrorism, what do you know about terrorism? People of KP sacrificed their children and picked up bodies. […] Did we support Pakistan or terrorists? Those calling people of KP terrorists should be ashamed. These are valiant people who saved this country,” he said.

Aziz said terrorism was a result of unemployment, hunger, non-availability of hospitals, water and education.

Senator Zeeshan Khanzada, also from the PTI, said he condemned the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. He accused the federal government of “abducting” Sohail Afridi, who has been rendered non-functional as the KP chief minister following the imposition of governor’s rule, and other PTI MPAs.

JUI-F’s Kamran Murtaza said the opposition’s resolution against governor’s rule should have also been included in the agenda for the day, but it was returned with objections.

Murtaza argued that the relevant material required for endorsement of enforcement of Article 232 and 234 — constitutional provision related to imposition of emergency and governor’s rule — had not been presented in the House.

Despite letters and applications, the government had not provided documents and material related to the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule, he said, adding that senators had to obtain that material through social media.

Members could not be satisfied with a decision until complete information came forth, he said.

NA proceedings

The NA question hour session was suspended due to discussions on the emergency. The motion in the lower House of Parliament was adopted with a majority vote after a discussion opened by Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar.

“The National Assembly approves the Proclamation of Emergency issued by the President on the 11th October, 2026 in the Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under second proviso of clause (1) of Article 232 of the Constitution,” read a post by NA’s official X account.

According to Article 232, if the “president acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days.

Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months.

Throughout Wednesday’s proceedings, opposition members participated calmly and did not stage any loud protest, unlike past instances when the PTI objects to the Centre.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also attended part of the session, with pictures released by the NA showing him shaking hands with Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif shakes hands with leader of the opposition in the National Assembly, Mehmood Khan Achakzai, on Wednesday. — Photo courtesy NA Facebook

Federal ministers defended the emergency imposition while assailing what they described as the PTI-led KP government’s lack of will to combat terrorism.

In tune with that, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari blamed the PTI for the circumstances that compelled the Centre to impose emergency in KP and termed it a “political suicide attack” for the party.

However, he also urged the treasury and the opposition to get back on the path of dialogue and make joint efforts against terrorism.

At one point during the proceedings, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq noted that the Oct 3 dialogue was held in a cordial atmosphere.

Sadiq praised both sides for “attempting more than their capacity so that the matter is settled”.

However, he said some matters were beyond the parties’ control and voiced his support for forming the same committees for negotiations if ever needed in the future.

Addressing PTI lawmakers, the speaker said, “Everyone’s response was that this [process of dialogue] should continue, but you also understand that your hands were tied.”

He took note of the PTI’s complaints regarding the jail conditions of party founder Imran Khan, adding that he had even provided details of facilities provided to the jailed ex-premier.

The session was adjourned to meet again at 11am on Oct 16 (Friday).

‘Political suicide attack’

Bilawal began his speech by highlighting that emergency and governor’s rule in KP were measures taken under the Constitution. Reading the relevant provisions, he asserted that the Centre tried its best to “engage the opposition so this step did not have to be taken”.

“They will have to accept, even if not publicly, but the responsible leadership of the opposition knows that the PTI itself carried out a political suicide attack on its KP government,” he remarked.

The PPP chief maintained that the PTI could not deny that its “leadership, particularly in the province had a key role in the political, constitutional and legal circumstances” at present.

Bilawal emphasised that the PPP’s stance was that “before employing this constitutional atomic bomb, we must engage with PTI and the opposition and try to address the federal government’s reservations that they were not supporting them in the war against terrorism”.

He observed: “If political space is restricted for one political party, it is impossible that it remains restricted for that particular party; it is limited for every political party, political worker and Pakistani citizen.

“We are responsible for this, but you cannot deny that you are also responsible for it,” he said.

Terming the imposition of emergency a “difficult decision”, Bilawal recalled alleged remarks by Sohail Afridi — the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional — that he would not combat terrorism the way the Centre wanted.

“If this was not a political suicide, then what else was it?”

The Bhutto scion wondered if the opposition and Afridi had left any reason for President Asif Ali Zardari, who he said prides himself on passing the 18th Amendment, to “refuse to sign” the emergency proclamation.

He argued that due to the PTI’s actions and statements, neither the president, the Centre, nor he had any legal or political reason left for not imposing emergency in KP.

“But even today, I would recommend to the federal government that we extend our hand forward once again for negotiations, political discussions and try to find a resolution and a middle path,” Bilawal added.

The PPP chairman noted that emergency was “always a stopgap measure”.

“We cannot sustain the emergency forever,” he added, emphasising that while the counterterrorism fight would be better than before, an “all-of-society and all-of-country response” was needed to eradicate it completely.

Regarding the Oct 3 talks of a joint delegation of the PPP and the government with the opposition, Bilawal said, “Late at night, I was informed that congratulations, negotiations are succeeding.”

He said the PTI was willing to declare the areas in KP with surging terrorism as “terrorist areas”, and the opposition was about to agree that the federal and KP governments would sign a pact on joint efforts against terrorism. However, the dialogue collapsed.

The former foreign minister pointed out that the security challenges Pakistan was facing were “way more complicated” than before, adding that India “could still not digest […] its embarrassment” from the May 2025 conflict.

Referring to remarks by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi that its ‘Operation Sindoor’ was still ongoing, Bilawal said: “It means that India is still sponsoring terrorist incidents in Pakistan, sometimes in the form of TTP (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) and sometimes in the form of separatist terrorist groups.”

He reiterated Pakistan’s stance that India was involved in terrorist activities being conducted from across the Afghan border.

The ex-foreign minister then highlighted Islamabad’s role as a mediator in the US-Iran war.

“But there is a state — which we do not recognise as a state — that will neither be happy nor ever forget that you took this step. And those Zionist forces will and are interfering in Pakistan’s internal politics and state.”

Concluding his speech, the PPP chairman emphasised the need for building consensus on “some fundamental issues” for an empowered lower house.

“Even today, we are saying, come and at least begin from this house,” he said while addressing the opposition benches.

Gohar demands implementation of NAP

Speaking in the NA, PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan said his party “rejected” the Centre’s move to impose emergency in KP.

He asked what “terrorism” Imran’s wife or sisters had allegedly been involved in that they had been put behind bars, or what the accusations were against the PTI MNAs and MPAs who he said were detained.

Gohar further said, “One person is not present in the house currently. When he comes during a joint session, then I will reveal the reality of the negotiations.”

He affirmed that the PTI had raised its voice against terrorism, adding that measures against the scourge must be taken according to the National Action Plan (NAP).

Gohar argued that the PML-N opposition during the PTI’s tenure carried out “14 long marches in two years, but you did not let us stage even one long march”.

Presenting his version of the Oct 3 talks with the government, the PTI leader said his party was being asked to immediately call off the long march. “I said where did [the topic] of terrorism arise from suddenly.”

Noting that the government had put forward “five reservations”, Gohar said PTI was willing to make the KP Police Act similar to that of Punjab and Sindh.

The PTI leader reiterated his party’s request for the production of certain MNAs it says were taken into custody.

Gohar also welcomed Bilawal’s proposal to continue dialogue.

Responding to Gohar’s remarks, the PPP chairman said the PTI was busy in its long march while the people of KP were being targeted by terrorists.

Bilawal reiterated that the opposition could keep arguing against the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, but no one could deny that the decision was grounded in the Constitution.

“I cannot insist on the government to continue talks with PTI despite being defrauded multiple times,” the PPP chairman said.

Pointing towards Gohar and Achakzai, Bilawal said: “I believe that none of them is allied with terrorists. I believe that they will definitely want to combat terrorism; however, they cannot deny the fact that their former chief minister contradicted this fact.”

Bilawal again requested all the stakeholders to unite and combat terrorism collectively. He also called for the provision of all facilities to the incarcerated PTI founder.

‘Threat to national security’

Addressing the house, the law minister explained that emergency was imposed in KP as the security situation there was becoming a threat to “national security”.

Tarar noted that after the Proclamation of Emergency was issued, the Constitution’s Article 232 required that both houses of the parliament approve the measure.

He recalled that the federal cabinet examined “material” regarding terrorism in the province during its Oct 11 meeting and then advised PM Shehbaz to recommend the imposition of emergency.

He noted that some people compared the measure to the emergency imposed by former dictator Gen Pervez Musharraf on Oct 12, 1999.

The minister particularly noted “internal disturbances” and cross-border infiltrations. He contended that the situation since Oct 15, 2025, when Sohail Afridi’s government came into power in KP, was “turning into a threat to national security to an alarming extent”.

He went on to highlight that there was a rise in terrorism in KP, especially after 2021, due to the approach of the provincial government.

“Perhaps there might be foreign, diplomatic and political reasons behind it, which got inflamed due to a political party’s point of view.”

Tarar stated that 2,911 incidents of terrorism took place between 2021 and 2024 in KP, but they surged to 3,787 incidents between Oct 15, 2025 and Oct 9, 2026.

He criticised the KP chief minister for ignoring martyred security and police personnel, and for instead preferring to promote his political designs and make visits across the country.

“Even this was announced that the federal capital will be conquered,” he said, referring to the party’s plan to hold a protest long march towards the federal capital.

The PML-N leader expressed his government’s gratitude to NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq for providing a platform for dialogue between the Centre and the opposition. He reiterated the government’s stance that the PTI had the agreement draft changed multiple times, but even then backed off from it.

Tarar observed that the PTI demanded the release of their party founder Imran Khan and his treatment in a private hospital despite knowing that only courts could provide such a relief.

He said two days would be “remembered in the country’s democratic history with regard to misfortune and a political party”.

On the emergency measure, the law minister noted that a special mechanism has been introduced for 12 districts of KP.

Speaking after Tarar, Achakzai criticised him for trying to prove that terrorism was not tackled in KP.

The opposition leader questioned the government’s mandate in the February 2024 general elections, quipping that the opposition would “surrender” if the minister could swear that the government won those polls fairly.

Achakzai alleged that the incumbent ruling coalition was formed “illegally”.

‘You do not have clean hands’

Meanwhile, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif went on to recall the tenure of the PTI government in the Centre and assailed the party’s past actions.

Referring to ex-prime minister Imran Khan’s plan to resettle members of the TTP, he said PTI tried to convince the then-opposition that “bringing these terrorists back would be better for Pakistan”.

The PML-N leader mentioned the 2019 episode of an Indian pilot’s capture in Pakistan: “They had threatened and we were surrendering. The then-prime minister was saying, ‘What should I do? Attack India?’”

Asif urged the opposition to reflect on its past actions, adding that Imran often used to praise former army chief retired General Qamar Javed Bajwa.

“As long as this contradiction remains in our words and actions and in our society, the circumstances of this country will not fix.”

He narrated his time behind bars during the PTI government, when Shehbaz “smuggled a blanket” to him to brace the low temperatures. “I used to eat the jail’s food,” he said, claiming that orders were given to remove the geyser when it was installed.

“But we did not hold rallies or mourn at D-Chowk or dig graves. We did not martyr police and law enforcement personnel,” Asif remarked.

“You demand equity when you have clean hands. You do not have clean hands, you cannot demand equity; this is a thousand-year-old principle,” he contended.

“You know very well what Gen Musharraf did to me. There was a 4x6 cell in Attock jail,” the PML-N politician said, emphasising that he stood with his party and ex-PM Nawaz Sharif.

Speaking on the current political situation, Asif alleged that Afridi used to “take directives […] from a person sitting in Afghanistan”.

He referred to a statement by the TTP condemning the imposition of emergency and deployment of troops in certain places. “Who is their ally and who is their rival?” he said.

The minister further countered the PTI’s stance that its leaders have not been able to meet Imran, who is imprisoned in the Adiala jail. “Meetings are held, [but] a lot of them are not publicised or brought on record,” he maintained.

Farooq Sattar urges PTI to ‘openly condemn terrorism’

In his remarks on the floor of the lower house, Farooq Sattar expressed Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan’s (MQM-P) confidence in the decision taken by the prime minister.

“This was an extremely difficult decision, but so unavoidable that you had no other option,” Sattar said about imposing emergency and governor’s rule.

“We trust your decision as we trust your experience, capabilities, political acumen, and that you made this decision in the interest of the nation,” he added.

The MQM-P lawmaker contended that the PTI was “on the wrong side and does not have concrete arguments” to declare that the decision was baseless or made with political motives.

“The main issue is of the mindset,” he declared, adding that Imran had “publicly said that the war on terror is not ours”. “This is their policy. This is their mindset.”

Sattar questioned whether the KP government had ever published reports to expose terrorist hideouts and extremist trends. He further raised questions about the government’s pursuit of cases against suspected terrorists.

“Openly condemn terrorism; else, the allegation of backing [it], if a commission is formed and God forbid, it is proven in the inquiry that there is political extremism and terrorism complicity, there is a nexus, then where will you go?”

Sattar recounted his past MQM experiences, saying, “I have also suffered such times. A lot of times, the narrative coming from the top was difficult to defend. Today, I feel that Barrister Gohar is also not in the position to defend his [party’s] position on KP.”

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.20 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.17
World.content:
The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.20 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.17 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs393.86 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.65 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 15 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Achakzai sees governor's rule next being imposed in Sindh, over water and mines
World.content:
Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai warned on Wednesday that governor’s rule would be imposed next in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”, urging the Centre to give provinces their rights and resources.

He was speaking in the National Assembly, where a resolution endorsing the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Sunday was passed. The federal government cited the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism as the reason for imposing governor’s rule in KP.

In days preceding the development, political tensions between the federal government and the opposition, mainly the PTI, had remained high after the party announced a long march to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. However, the march, initially planned for Islamabad, remained confined to KP until it fizzled out with the imposition of governor’s rule in the province.

In his address, Achakzai said KP’s “mistake is that it saved itself with the help of its people”. He also drew a comparison between the current situation with regards to KP and the one witnessed at the time of the creation of Bangladesh.

He also assailed the government for depriving the PTI of its election symbol ahead of the 2024 general elections. “And the mistake of his (Imran’s) party’s workers was that they contested the elections on 200 different symbols and turned your own game around on you. You are meting out the punishment for that? You are punishing 240 million people of Pakistan for that?”

The opposition leader also pointed out that Sohail Afridi, who has become non-functional as the chief minister after the imposition of governor’s rule and had been leading the PTI’s march, had not resorted to violence or using expletives in his call for the protest.

He went on to say, “When you try to snatch our right to self-determination, our right to vote, we all will stand against you. All of us, all provinces.”

Noting the participation of the PPP, which is in power in Sindh, Achakzai said it pained him. He then warned that governor’s rule would next be imposed in Sindh over the “occupation of water, mines and streams”.

“And then you will recall your mistake,” he said, noting however that there was still time to rectify mistakes.

“Reverse these decisions,” Achakzai said, urging that Parliament be made the centre of power. “And Pakistan will be saved.”

He warned that when the “state turns against its own people, they are compelled to look elsewhere”.

The opposition also criticised the government over the country’s economic situation.

“You are looting this country’s resources […] Have some mercy on this country. […] This country is drowning because of our mistakes. There is only one way to save it: through its Constitution and Parliament and by having a democratic system,” he asserted.

Achakzai also lamented the fact the Parliament was not taken into confidence over decisions related to foreign affairs, and that Pakistan had strained ties with most of its neighbours.

On Imran, who has not been allowed meetings with his family and associates for a long time, Achakzai said: “Which provision of the Constitution … places a restriction on meetings with the most popular leader of the country?”

He assured that if meetings were arranged with Imran, “we will just try to assess his health condition and will try to resolve matter between you. We promise we will meet him and not tell anyone. […] Have some sense. Negotiate.”

He concluded his address by declaring that the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP was wrong.

World.title: Omani FM meets PM Shehbaz, commends Pakistan's 'sustained diplomatic efforts' for regional peace
World.content:
Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr Albusaidi called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday and appreciated Pakistan’s “sustained diplomatic efforts” for de-escalation and peaceful solutions to regional challenges, a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

Both Pakistan and Oman have been engaged in efforts for de-escalation after US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February resulted in a conflict that has now expanded further into the Middle East.

Albusaidi’s meeting with PM Shehbaz was held on the second day of his two-day trip to Pakistan, during which he also attended the eighth session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) and held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

In his meeting with the Omani foreign minister, PM Shehbaz “highlighted that the strong bond of shared faith, geography, history, culture, and centuries of people-to-people exchanges between Pakistan and Oman provided a strong fraternal foundation to the bilateral relationship”, the PMO statement said.

The premier underscored that Pakistan considered Oman a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region, it added.

“The prime minister expressed satisfaction over the successful convening of the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission.

“He hoped that the meeting would provide a strong foundation for further expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two brotherly countries,” the statement said.

It further stated that PM Shehbaz “noted with deep satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on all regional and global issues”.

He appreciated Oman’s “principled stance” of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes, the statement said.

For his part, Albusaidi thanked the government of Pakistan for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation and “expressed satisfaction on successful holding of the 8th JMC session”, the PMO statement said.

It added that the Omani foreign minister “agreed that it (JMC session) would pave the way for enhanced bilateral collaboration in diverse sectors for mutual benefit”.

“The Omani foreign minister also appreciated Pakistan’s sustained diplomatic efforts towards de-escalating tensions and advancing peaceful solutions to regional challenges,” the statement read.

It added that PM Shehbaz also witnessed the signing of the Protocol of the 8th session of the Pakistan-Oman JMC, as well as agreements and memoranda of understanding for bilateral cooperation between the two sides in the areas of media cooperation, news and information exchange, historical documentation and archives management, communication and information technology and facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges.

Earlier in the day, Albusaidi held a joint press conference with Deputy PM Dar, during which the latter said that Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia were “totally unacceptable”.

At the outset of the press conference, Dar said that the two sides would sign a protocol relating to the commission.

He said that this reflected “a shared resolve to further strengthen and expand bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest”. He said that the two sides would also sign an agreement for mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and official passports.

“Pakistan-Oman friendship remains strong and forward-looking,” he told the media.

He added that the two ministers had also agreed to hold a business-to-business investment forum in Pakistan.

The ministers discussed the situation in the Gulf as well, he said, adding that “Pakistan remained committed to contributing constructively to diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability in the region”.

Dar said that the two sides also exchanged views on recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He said that he conveyed Pakistan’s condemnation of the attacks.

“I underscored that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are totally unacceptable. My brother [Albusaidi] actually fully endorses this. Violations of international law pose a serious threat to regional peace and security,” he said.

“I reaffirmed Pakistan’s full solidarity with Saudi Arabia and our unwavering commitment to the kingdom’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security in accordance with the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” he said.

They also “emphasised the urgent need for unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance to the people of Gaza”, Dar said.

DPM Dar also stressed that India’s unilateral abeyance of the Indus Water Treaty was “a material breach of international law”.

“This action threatens the water, food and energy security of Pakistan’s 250 million people,” Dar said.

Speaking at the occasion, Albusaidi said the JMC had “provided an important opportunity to review the state of bilateral relations”. He said that two sides “reaffirmed the strength of the longstanding ties” between the two countries.

“Both Oman and Pakistan attach great importance to dialogue and diplomacy as essential means of addressing regional challenges, easing tensions and promoting peace and stability,” Albusaidi said.

He also appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic role in the US-Iran war. He reaffirmed the two countries’ “shared commitment to further deepening our bilateral partnership and broadening cooperation across centres of mutual benefit”.

The two countries agreed that dialogue and diplomacy were “the only way forward” to resolve regional conflicts, Dar said in response to a reporter’s question.

“We are both on the same page,” he said.

Meanwhile, Dar told reporters that a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) would help expand business activities, adding that he was told that barring one, all countries had consented to the agreement.

Responding to a question about the gaps in bilateral talks between the two countries, Dar said Albusaidi’s visit was previously delayed because Pakistan had been involved in mediation efforts between the US and Iran.

Albusaidi added that discussions had continued “behind the scenes”.

Responding to a question about the Strait of Hormuz, Albusaidi said that Oman was committed to “unhindered navigation” through the strait “because of its vitality to the global economy and the region”.

JMC session

The meeting of the commission was co-chaired by Dar and Albusaidi.

The two sides “reaffirmed their close fraternal ties and commitment to expanding bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, maritime and logistics connectivity, agriculture, industry, energy, workforce mobility, human resource development, education, IT, media and climate change, among other areas”, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Both ministers emphasised the importance of strengthening people-to-people ties, facilitating workforce mobility, and promoting exchanges of business delegations from both countries to unlock new opportunities for trade, investment and institutional collaboration.

FM Dar stressed the need for “timely implementation of agreed outcomes through close institutional coordination and sustained engagement between joint working group meetings”, the statement added.

According to FO, the Oman FM thanked Pakistan for its warm hospitality, appreciated Pakistan’s efforts for regional peace and security, and reaffirmed Muscat’s commitment to further strengthening the longstanding partnership between the two countries.

Dar commends Albusaidi’s efforts towards regional peace

Speaking at the outset of the JMC session, Dar said the two had “worked out” certain areas of bilateral interest and discussed global issues in detail, including the US-Iran war, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab and Gaza in their restricted meeting.

Dar said the two sides had also discussed Jammu and Kashmir and other pressing regional issues. He commended Albusaidi’s leadership and efforts towards regional peace in the Middle East.

“I personally greatly admire your efforts. I know how much hard work you have put in,” he said, noting that Pakistan’s position on the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was “very unique”.

“We are members of both the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and, obviously, the United Nations and other multilateral bodies,” Dar said.

He stressed, “There should not be any long gaps between bilateral engagements,” noting potential in the areas of trade, economic activities and investment opportunities.

Dar said he had promised to visit Oman in 2027 to hold the next session of the commission there. He added that both sides had identified areas of mutual interest and discussed possible meetings.

He said Pakistan and Oman cooperated closely and cordially, adding that although their diplomatic relations had completed 55 years, their ties went back “centuries”.

Dar said the two countries shared a history of “love and affection”, particularly in relation to Balochistan and Gwadar. Referring to discussions on Bab al-Mandab and recent developments involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Dar said both sides shared similar views on resolving regional issues.

He said the impact of regional tensions was also visible in Pakistan, where energy supply chains had been affected, and fuel prices had skyrocketed, adding that the “common man could not afford the resulting burden.”

Speaking on the occasion, Albusaidi said Oman was committed to further strengthening bilateral engagement and cooperation in various fields that could bring greater benefits to the people of both countries.

“I am delighted to be here with my delegation in Islamabad this morning, in this very warm, friendly and brotherly country, Pakistan, with which, as you have rightly said, we share bonds of history, culture, tradition and unity,” he said.

He said the Pakistan-Oman JMC was one of the mechanisms for exploring further avenues of collaboration, adding that the two countries also had a business council and a political consultation mechanism between their foreign ministers.

“We can do much more, and as we made a joint commitment this morning to make this meeting a success, I believe the more we do, the more we can deliver on the promise and the aspiration of our leaderships and our people,” Albusaidi said.

He also commended Pakistan’s role in supporting dialogue and diplomacy in the region.

“Your efforts to encourage engagement, understanding, respect and recognition are commendable, and I salute you for all your efforts,” he said, adding that Oman greatly appreciated Pakistan’s role in providing space for dialogue between Iran and the US.

Albusaidi said there was significant potential for economic cooperation between Oman and Pakistan, particularly in trade, logistics, port connectivity, energy and food security.

“The potential exists, and our task is to remove any obstacles and create the conditions that allow businesses to thrive so that we can fully benefit from this potential,” he said.

He also called for greater cooperation in tourism, academic and technological fields, as well as more regular exchanges between the people of the two countries.

“Once again, I appreciate the efforts of our private sector and industrial partners,” Albusaidi said, adding that he looked forward to further discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation.

According to a joint statement, the two sides agreed to hold the ninth session of the JMC next year.

After the session concluded, Albusaidi posted on that he had a “constructive day” in Islamabad co-chairing JMC session with Dar.

“We reviewed practical ways to deepen our longstanding partnership in trade, investment, energy, logistics and other priority areas, and agreed on closer follow-up to turn opportunities into results,” he said, expressing gratitude for the “warm hospitality and the shared commitment to cooperation and regional dialogue”.

Dar, Omani FM call for sustained bilateral engagement

Earlier in the day, Dar also held a bilateral meeting with Albusaidi ahead of the JMC session, FO said. The visiting dignitary had arrived in Pakistan on Tuesday on a two-day visit.

The two ministers reaffirmed the close, fraternal ties between Pakistan and Oman and underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement to deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade, investment and people-to-people contacts, according to FO.

“The two sides also exchanged views on regional developments and emphasised the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in advancing lasting peace and stability,” FO said.

Albusaidi commended Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and security, while Dar acknowledged and appreciated Oman’s constructive role and shared aspirations for regional peace and stability, the statement added.
